0.content:
"A Lonely Place" (also: A Lonely Place): "A Lonely Place" is a named subarea in the northern zone of Elynas, the colossal dead beast whose remains form much of the Beryl Region of Fontaine. It is where the Traveler sets out in the Ancient Colors quest "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" to follow Jakob toward the heart of Elynas, and it is also the area listed for the world quest "The Lone Phantom Sail".

It is a map label rather than a settlement: no one is recorded as living in it, and the Melusine village of Merusea is a separate place.

Geography: Part of the Beryl Region, on the map level "Within Elynas: Northern Zone". Elynas' skeleton has become one with the mountains and lakes of the region, so this subarea belongs to the creature's body as much as to the landscape. The route onward to "A Very Warm Place", where Elynas' heart lies, runs through water.

In "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" a portal in this area is found blocked, and Seymour cannot bore through the rock wall because it is too thick for his output. Mamere then urges swimming through a water current instead, and the party reaches "A Very Warm Place" that way. Paimon remarks that the currents used to flow in the opposite direction.

Quests: Two world quests are tied to the subarea: "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" (Ancient Colors Act III, starting here; it leads to the confrontation with Jakob and the meeting with Elynas) and "The Lone Phantom Sail" (the enthusiast Ahes searches for the phantom of a white ship, the Sponsian).

"The Lone Phantom Sail" requires the earlier quest "Hey, This Isn't Pumpkin Soup...". Ahes signals with an old military conch, the party follows a ghostly half-ship, fights Rifthound packs near a wreck and ends by investigating a strange item there. Ahes treats the Sponsian as Admiral Basil Elton's flagship, of which only half the hull was left behind.

The Ancient Colors quest ends here in a fight. After Jakob springs a triangular barrier around the Traveler and sets Rifthounds on the party, Seymour, fighting as a Recon Log Mek in Pneuma mode, says nothing he can do will breach the dome; a Shatterstone Breacher Primus then attacks the barrier and breaks it. Mamere seems to hear "Father" at that moment and obeys a request to paint the Traveler and Paimon, which carries the party onward to the meeting with Elynas.

Atmosphere: Quiet, sparse and a little eerie: water, rock and the sense of standing inside something enormous. During "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" the view is deliberately hazed and pulled back (a gameplay effect), matching the creeping contamination Seymour warns about.

Dangers: Rifthounds appear in the related quests, together with the "contamination" Seymour reports as the party nears Elynas' heart. Jakob, by then revealed as an Iniquitous Baptist, waits at the end of the route in the quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the subarea is simply open for exploration. Nothing later than the 4.0 quests is recorded for it.

1.comment: "A Lonely Place": The Lone Phantom Sail
1.content: Ahes is an enthusiast who haunts the waters near A Lonely Place picking over a shipwreck and a tattered logbook said to belong to Admiral Basil Elton's white ironclad, the Sponsian. She tunes an old military conch to send signals and believes the ship answers her. With Paimon and the Traveler she follows a phantom half-ship to its wreck; the quest closes on a strange item found there. Whether the Sponsian truly survives is left to Ahes' own conviction.

2.content:
"A Very Bright Place" (also: A Very Bright Place): "A Very Bright Place" is a half-submerged cavern inside the southern zone of Elynas, the vast dead beast whose remains shape Fontaine's Beryl Region. Its walls hold many ore veins and it is filled with a congealed orange substance. The young Melusine Puca likes to collect pretty stones here, which is how the world quest "Strange Stone Chronicle" begins.

It is unlocked after step 3 of the Ancient Colors world quest "There Will Come Soft Rains", the point where the earthquakes and Rifthound attacks around Merusea Village begin.

Geography: On the map level "Within Elynas: Southern Zone" of the Beryl Region, the counterpart of "A Lonely Place" in the north. It is a cavern, part submerged, with veins of ore running through the rock and the orange material pooled through it. Puca, who lives in a village close to the ore veins, walks here to pick stones.

Puca's own words are that the stones here are pretty but not precious, and that she collects them for their looks. Her friend Glaisti says the two of them had visited the stone-picking spots many times without ever meeting the frightening creatures that appeared during the quest.

People: Puca, a small Melusine, comes here to pick rocks; her friend Glaisti sometimes accompanies her. Puca says her sister Sluasi runs a gemstone workshop while she herself does not, preferring to collect unusual rocks for their own sake. Chesil, a gem merchant in the Court of Fontaine, buys the ore the Traveler brings out.

Quests: "Strange Stone Chronicle" (Parts 1 and 2) starts here: the Traveler helps Puca find her lost token beside a strange ore, then takes a sample to the gem merchant Chesil, who is excited by it and pays an advance for more. In Part 2 Puca marks further spots on the map and the Traveler collects thirty pieces of Strange Ore for Chesil.

Chesil cannot identify the ore. The Traveler may give it a name of their own, or tell him it comes from near Elynas, which he notes is not a place people normally prospect. Puca says she showed the stone to her sister, who saw nothing precious in it; the quest plays on how a trader and a child value the same rock differently.

Dangers: Rifthounds attacked the Melusines around Merusea Village during "There Will Come Soft Rains". Puca was found trapped in seagrass at an ore spot during that quest and was freed by the Traveler, with Mamere and Seymour present.

In that quest the mercenaries Irus, Kaykaus and Kaykubad admit that Jakob had them dig up red stones for half a day, did not pay them, and then, with a hand-sign and words they did not know, called the monsters that chased them. They say he went toward the place where the giant rock hangs. The sources do not say which ore site they mined, so this cavern should not be assumed to be it.

Atmosphere: Glowing, damp and hushed: wet stone, ore glinting in the walls and an orange sheen over everything. The brightness is the point of the name, and it contrasts with the hazed, uneasy route through "A Lonely Place".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cavern is open and quiet. The Rifthound disturbances of the 4.0 quests are over.

3.comment: "A Very Bright Place": Strange Stone Chronicle
3.content: A short chain of world quests in which Puca loses a token near the ore veins and the Traveler finds it fused to an unfamiliar, shiny ore. Chesil, a gem dealer in the Court of Fontaine, cannot place it but sees a fashion in it and arranges a purchase. The quest is light in tone and has no bearing on the larger Elynas story.

4.content:
"A Very Warm Place" (also: A Very Warm Place, Elynas' heart, Scenery Within Elynas' Depths): "A Very Warm Place" is the name of the spot where Elynas' heart lies. Elynas is the huge dead creature whose remains fill Fontaine's Beryl Region and shelter the Melusines. The heart is why the air there is warm. When the Traveler first reaches it, it lies dormant under a layer of crystallized stone.

A viewpoint here is unlocked after finishing the Ancient Colors quest; its text says the heart that was nearly awakened has gone silent again.

Geography: Part of the Within Elynas: Northern Zone map level of the Beryl Region. The heart is not a freestanding room so much as a part of Elynas' body: crystallized stone covers it, and the warmth it gives off is the notable feature.

Elynas' remains, according to Jakob, are far larger than Orobashi's and take up almost the whole of the Beryl Region. The Melusines treat the inside of his body as their home.

History: In the Ancient Colors quest "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog", Jakob (by then an Iniquitous Baptist) used Abyssal power to reverse the crystallization briefly, wanting Elynas' blood. The Traveler caused the heart to crystallize again. Elynas, present as a spirit in the form of a Melusine, thanked them: if he were revived, his organs would move and wreck the Melusines' home inside him.

Elynas is a quest NPC whom the Melusines call "Father"; they came into being unintentionally through him. The wiki credits Rhinedottir with creating him, and says he came to understand that his happiness harmed others and wanted to die so that he could hurt no one. After death he wanted company though he could not speak to people, and spends his afterlife caring for the Melusines. He thought of Jakob as a friend even after Jakob's transformation.

Atmosphere: Warm, quiet and a little strange: crystal and stone around a sleeping heart, with small Melusines nearby, in an interior that is also somebody's body.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the heart is dormant and crystallized, and the Melusines' home is intact. No later content is shown to have changed this.

Origin: According to the wiki's account of Elynas' own words, he was once an unknown form drifting in cold, lonely cosmic darkness, often crying for company, before a "Mother" gave him a name. The Breacher Primus species are his indirect creations. These details come from the wiki's summary of the Ancient Colors quest and are not traced to exact dialogue.

5.content:
Abandoned Production Zone (also: Abandoned Production Area): The Abandoned Production Zone is a closed-off industrial level at the bottom of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's underwater prison in the Liffey Region. A lift near the waypoint on the Production Zone's lower level leads down to it. Four passages (Supply Warehouse 1, Supply Warehouse 2, the Energy Storage Warehouse and the Geode Mine Shaft) branch from a central chamber and are opened or shut by a large gear-driven drive valve. Notes left lying around show the fortress's daily life: petty complaints, makeshift experiments and boredom.

It is a point of interest from Version 4.1. A fortress guard called Camden is posted in it. The zone matters in two world-quest moments: the drive valve is used to reach a locked room in Safe Operation and to open the sealed Geode Mine Shaft in An Eye for an Eye.

Geography: Reached only by the lift beside the Production Zone's lower-level waypoint, which sits below the Administrative Area. The central chamber holds the Multidirectional Connection Control Drive Valve, with four paths radiating from it: Supply Warehouse 1, the Geode Mine Shaft, the Energy Storage Warehouse and Supply Warehouse 2.

Leaving and re-entering the area resets the valve to its original position, which keeps the lift route open. A hallway after Supply Warehouse 2 contains a punching bag and training notes, and a room beyond Supply Warehouse 1 holds a desk with a worker's memo. Energy Transfer Terminals let a visitor look into each passage before opening it.

Places: Central drive-valve chamber; Supply Warehouse 1 and Supply Warehouse 2; the Energy Storage Warehouse; the Geode Mine Shaft, a mine filled with Arkhium crystal and patrolled by Flying Energy Thieves; a hallway with a punching bag.

At the end of the Geode Mine Shaft a water current (open once An Eye for an Eye is finished) leads on to Bravais' Press Works, so the sealed shaft is also a back way into a separate hidden workshop.

People: Camden, a Fortress of Meropide guard, stands watch and is chronically sleepy. Other people appear only through the notes they left: a self-taught drink maker who tests recipes on colleagues, and someone training for the Pankration Ring who keeps a gruff diary.

The memo names Koblenz (made to taste an early recipe, fell ill for three days) and Delassaux (paid 280 Credit Coupons to try a later batch, and found it invigorating). The training diarist names Roussimoff, an opponent in the Pankration Ring training matches. None of them is otherwise described here.

Governance: The area is run by fortress rules. A posted Notice orders that work on the Geode Mine Shaft is suspended, the paths sealed, and the drive valve operated only with a technical expert present. Unauthorised access by non-essential personnel is prohibited. A Drive Valve Operations and Safety Manual explains the gear rule: when the central Core Gear Drive and a removable Gear Drivetrain point in opposite directions, the path indicated by the Core Gear Drive opens, and the valve halts if all four drivetrains are removed.

History: Canon gives no history of the zone beyond its present state. The Notice records that Geode Mine Shaft work was suspended, a new locking device was added there, and the research terminal's energy storage device was removed for safety. The zone's name, the Notice and the dusty rooms mark it as a former production area that was shut down.

Quests: In Scenes from Life in Meropide: Safe Operation the drive valve is used to open the room where Mitul is locked in. In An Eye for an Eye it opens the sealed Geode Mine Shaft so the Traveler can escape with Cater and Lanoire.

Gameplay note: bringing an Energy Transfer Device from the Energy Storage Warehouse powers the punching bag; striking it releases a common chest holding Credit Coupons.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed and quiet as of 7.1, with Camden on watch. No later content changes it.

Dangers: Moving machinery of the drive valve, Flying Energy Thieves in the Geode Mine Shaft, and the isolation of a dead-end level.

Atmosphere: Dim metal corridors, hanging pipes and the grind of heavy gears, with the sense that the people who worked here left in a hurry. Their scrawled notes give it a human, grumbling tone: cafeteria complaints, repetitive meals, sore muscles and schemes to earn Credit Coupons.

6.comment: Abandoned Production Zone: Drive Valve Notice and Safety Manual
6.content: A posted notice at the central chamber. Geode Mine Shaft work is suspended and connecting paths sealed; the valve may be turned only under a technical expert's supervision. The manual explains that a non-removable Core Gear Drive controls the central room while removable Gear Drivetrains set each path's direction, and that the path pointed to by the Core Gear Drive opens when the two directions oppose each other.

7.comment: Abandoned Production Zone: Memo of the Drink Maker
7.content: A desk memo tracks three recipes for a wholesome drink. Early versions of bulle fruit juice, rainbow rose and pluie lotus distillates, cinnamon, honey, tidalga and condessence crystal powder made Koblenz sick for three days. The writer swapped in Sumeru rose and nilotpala lotus, paid Delassaux 280 Credit Coupons to test it (he felt perky), and finally replaced the crystal powder with ground yellowish-green ore. He hopes the last version, which has a rich distinctive flavor, will succeed, and says he is not making Fonta.

8.comment: Abandoned Production Zone: Training Log of a Pankration Ring Hopeful
8.content: A diary pinned beside the punching bag. The writer records losses in training matches (once to a rival in a Blubberbeast fighting suit who slipped and flipped him), weighted runs, weightlifting sets and punches, and complains that Credit Coupon prizes barely cover food. He mocks Roussimoff for being laid out by a spicy-sauced Garlic Baguette and for supposed weaknesses to elements, then decides to stay for the title anyway.

9.content:
Alain Guillotin's Resting Place (also: Alain's grave, Alain Guillotin's grave): A small cave in Fontaine, just north of Chemin de L'Espoir and a little above the entrance to Annapausis, holds the grave of Alain Guillotin, the founding director of the Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering and creator of Sandrone. It is reached through the story quest "Those We Have Kept" in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event, and stays open afterwards.

The site was added in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII).

Places: The grave bears an epitaph in Fontaine script. In paraphrase it reads: here lies Alain Guillotin, Founding Director of the Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, White Cavalier of Protection, Lord-Artificer; may the waters protect and guide his soul across to the other shore, and "regrettably, there's nothing more to say."

The transcribed in-world inscription differs slightly: it calls him Maitre-Artificier and Director of the Institute, a White Knight of the Grand Waters, entrusts the keeping of his soul beyond the shores to the waters, and ends with a remark that it is a pity but everything has been said. Wiki translations of the Fontaine script are interpretations.

People: Alain Guillotin was a historical figure of the cataclysm era, around 400-500 years ago: a prodigy of the Institute of Natural Philosophy, a Marechaussee Hunter, and in his later years the maker of Sandrone, who became a Fatui Harbinger, and of her attendant Pulonia. His sister Mary-Ann and his adoptive father Emanuel are Guillotins as well. See his own entry for the biography.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the resting place is a permanent point of interest in the Court of Fontaine Region.

History: Wiki accounts place Alain, his sister Mary-Ann and his Seymour automaton in a clash with the Narzissenkreuz Ordo inside the remains of Elynas, which presumably cost Mary-Ann her life; Alain had refused Narzissenkreuz's invitation to join its plan. Later he built Sandrone and Pulonia. The wiki marks this chronology as incomplete pending 6.7 updates, and how he died and came to rest in Fontaine is not stated in the pages read.

10.comment: Alain Guillotin's Resting Place: Alain's Grave and Sunny Summer Fontinalia
10.content: The grave's unlock belongs to the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (6.7), so the quest is limited-time content. In its third act, "Those We Have Kept", the party (with Sandrone) deals with the ritual in the Tower of Gestalt and then goes to the Opera Epiclese and to the place Sandrone wishes to head to. The wiki ties the unlocking of the resting place to this quest but does not describe the scene at the grave.

11.content:
Alta Semita (also: High Pathway, Golden Aqueduct): Alta Semita (Latin, roughly "High Pathway") is the golden aqueduct system of Capitolium, the inner city of Remuria, sunk in the Sea of Bygone Eras off Fontaine. It once carried Ichor out from the Domus Aurea toward "the great lake in the far north", and from above it looks like a giant harp. After millennia it had broken apart. In the quest Gradus ad Capitolium the Traveler and the dragon Scylla rebuild it so that the gates of the Domus Aurea will open.

It was added in Version 4.6 together with the rest of the Sea of Bygone Eras. Scylla says that in Remuria's heyday the will of Phobos flowed through golden aqueducts to every corner of the kingdom, which is why restoring this section can unlock the palace.

Geography: A subarea of Capitolium, the inner half of the Remurian capital, lying beside the palace of the Domus Aurea. The aqueduct's pipes and channels run outward from the palace, a design the Domus Aurea's own plan echoes: Monsieur Os says the whole palace was built from a giant ship as an instrument, with pipes extending outward to broadcast the symphony.

A mural north of the aqueduct was painted with the power of the "symphony", as in the Faded Castle. Collegium Phonascorum lies close by, and the quest reconstruction runs through both places. Reaching Capitolium at all requires passing the Initium Iani and the Passage of Ianus.

Places: The harp-shaped aqueduct and its golden channels; the symphony murals and light-guiding devices that Scylla and the Traveler activate; scattered "scores" and a horn that must be lit; the approach to the Domus Aurea's gate.

Ancient Engravings here honour Aurelius, a Harmost, whose tomb the text calls the ocean itself.

People: No living inhabitants. Scylla, a Dragon Prince of the vishaps, guides the work; Monsieur Os (the Harmost Cassiodor speaking through the cat Osse) comments on the murals; Boethius, who Os says has lain low in the palace for millennia, waits in the Domus Aurea.

After the aqueduct is restored the Traveler has a vision in which Scylla addresses Remus, the Sebastos of Remuria, and learns his last plan.

Governance: Remuria's order ran on Phobos, the symphony, and the Harmosts under the Sebastos. The aqueduct was infrastructure of that order: the golden waterways carried the symphony's will, so repairing them lets Phobos's own defences open the palace.

Culture: Remurians recorded music as paintings on stone. Scylla says Remus's musicians once covered every rock and stone wall with their melodies, and that now only golden bees obey the call of the symphony. The Alta Semita's engraving shows a martial, triumphal side of that culture: it praises Aurelius as one who promoted Boethius, pacified tribes "uncivilized for the empire", and led the melodies of ten legions.

History: The aqueduct fell apart in the centuries after Remuria sank. In Gradus ad Capitolium Scylla, who has been freed from his seal at the Initium Iani and has little strength left, proposes to use the Domus Aurea's own power against it: reconnecting the ruined section will open the great gates "just as they once did". The reconstruction quests (Part I and Part II) have the Traveler follow golden bees to scattered scores, light a horn and return bird phantasms to their places.

The engraving beside the aqueduct gives one Remurian view of the war: Aurelius is called a Harmost who promoted Boethius and passed order to his successors, and Phobos is invoked to curse the traitors who colluded with "cruel, reprobate barbarians" and scuttled the flagship that bore him north; the text promises barbarism will be repaid twelve times over. It is a one-sided Remurian account.

Quests: Gradus ad Capitolium (the first quest of Pharsalia's Rhapsody, part of Canticles of Harmony) leads here. Its child quests, Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction: Part I and Part II, are set on the Alta Semita; Part II also uses Collegium Phonascorum.

After the aqueduct is restored, Scylla agrees to help against Boethius.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the aqueduct stands rebuilt after the 4.6 quests. No later content revisits it.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems around the Domus Aurea, drowned ruins and strong currents, and Boethius's mastery of Phobos's power.

Atmosphere: Gold light along a harp of pipes in the dark water, painted music fading on stone, golden bees drifting past, and a silence broken only by the humming of the symphony.

key: flagship of forty rows of oars
12.content: The engraving says nobody knows where Aurelius, a noble Harmost, lies buried; his tomb is the sea, for he sank with his flagship of forty rows of oars. It credits him with promoting Boethius, pacifying tribes for the empire and leading the melodies of ten legions, and curses the traitors who joined the barbarians and scuttled the ship. It ends with a promise that when civilisation crushes savagery, brutality will be repaid twelve times over.

13.content:
Annapausis: Annapausis is a flooded, hushed area in the Court of Fontaine Region, unlocked during the world quest The Narzissenkreuz Adventure. It lies where the Narzissenkreuz Institute, a Fontaine orphanage, once stood, and it is the setting in which the small Oceanid Ann leads the "Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team". The whole place has the feel of a story played out in a dream.

A statue of the Oceanid Lyris, who directed the orphanage about five centuries ago, stands near a small fountain southwest of the castle-like structure. The area is not labelled on the map until the player reaches it in the quest.

Geography: Annapausis is split into two layers. The upper part is filled with water and can be crossed only by diving; floating above it, that water sits over a lower part that can be walked, climbed and glided through. Everything there feels damp even away from the water, as if drip-fed from above. Its landmarks include a castle-like structure and the Little Fountain beside a water statue of Lyris, southwest of the castle.

Annapausis belongs to the Court of Fontaine Region and is entered from the nearby underwater waypoint northwest of the Court of Fontaine. Ann stays at the player's side while they remain in Annapausis and Chemin de L'Espoir.

People: Ann, a small Oceanid, and the other members of her self-styled Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team (Al, Jak, Petit Chou, Mori and "Colonel Kate") live out a play-story here in which they rescue "Princess Lyris" from the dragon Narcissus. The statue of Lyris recalls the real Oceanid who directed the orphanage.

Ann was born from the dreaming of the Oceanid Mary-Ann, who is a merging of the real Mary-Ann Guillotin and Lyris. Ann carries the memories of both and does not fully understand them. Seymour, Mary-Ann Guillotin's companion machine, has said the orphanage ruins lie at Annapausis' coordinates.

History: The Narzissenkreuz Institute raised orphans and the children of criminals. It fell apart in the cataclysm of 500 years ago, when its director Lyris and vice director Basil Elton left and did not return as expected, and its location was lost beneath the water; later accounts treat the sunken site as Annapausis.

Lyris survived, returned to Fontaine and circled the drowned ruins, saddened by what had been lost. Rene and Jakob, two former orphans, found her there and brought her into the secret Narzissenkreuz Ordo. A visit by Mary-Ann Guillotin and Seymour to the ruins is where the story told at the Little Fountain comes from (see the entry below).

After a battle with the Marechaussee Hunters, Lyris absorbed Mary-Ann Guillotin's personality, and the merged Oceanid Mary-Ann built a dream world called "The Real Annapausis" to hide from reality and wait for the others to return. Ann was created accidentally by that dream. These steps come from the Ann questline's wiki summaries; the order of events inside the dream is told through the quests The Narzissenkreuz Adventure, Search in the Algae Sea and Rowboat's Wake.

Atmosphere: Still, dim and waterlogged; a hush broken by bubbles, fountain trickles and the cheerful play-acting of children's heroes. Names and ranks sound like a nursery game (a "Colonel", a "fell dragon"), and the sadness underneath is only partly visible.

Dangers: The tainted Hydro phantasms that attack Petit Chou and Al in the opening quest are "Evil Fangs of Narcissus" in the game's make-believe; they are Tainted Water-Spouting Phantasms. Mimic enemies such as a Hydro Mimic Boar guard key spots. Water immersion is constant.

Quests: The Narzissenkreuz Adventure (Ann of the Narzissenkreuz, Act I, 4.0) introduces Ann, Petit Chou, Al, Jak and the setting. The questline continues in In the Wake of Narcissus.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Annapausis remains a submerged, dreamlike place in the Court of Fontaine Region; no later change to it is recorded in the sources checked.

14.comment: Annapausis: The Little Fountain and the Story
14.content:
Southwest of the castle, near the Lyris statue, an interactable called "A Story" lets the player hear a tale narrated by Mary-Ann Guillotin to Lyris after the Institute's destruction. In it the kind Princess Lyris is beloved by friends (Al, Ney, and "Colonel Kate") and her realm withstands the dragon Narcissus because she shares her "time" with her friends. In the end she gives up her past and present, entrusts her "future" as a drop of water to her friends, and sleeps in her tower. The teller says it is only a story and leaves the rest for another time. The same fountain accepts the Sword of Narzissenkreuz, whose two forms (Pneuma and Ousia) answer with short, poetic lines; offering a Drained Conch Cup there yields a Surging Sacred Chalice.

Mary-Ann ends by proposing a new beginning set far in the future, where a tiny life is born from the princess' pearl of water and needs a name; this is a hint about Ann. Lyris, listening, is described as more interested in the story than in the lesson, so the teller invites her to write the ending herself.

15.content:
Aquanigma (also: Sinthe production base): Aquanigma is the hidden headquarters of Vacher's Sinthe operation, reached by diving beneath Salacia Plain in Fontaine. In it the Traveler and Paimon found the factory where Sinthe was mixed and the laboratory where Vacher dissolved people in Primordial Seawater. It exists in game only as a quest domain during the Archon Quest "When All Return to the Waters".

The Traveler went there while Navia was stalling in the Opera Epiclese trial; the evidence found inside let her prove that Marcel, head of the Confrerie of Cabriere, was the hidden figure Vacher.

Geography: An underwater base with an unremarkable entrance that was found with the help of intelligence from Melus. Inside are an elevator, mechanisms that raise the water level to open the path upward, flooded passages needing a dive, and a final inner chamber that served as the innermost sanctum. A cracked wall can only be broken by a Xenochromatic Armored Crab's ability.

The route runs from the guarded entrance through a lift, flooded sections and several mechanism rooms to the innermost laboratory; all enemies met on the way are Ousia-aligned meks.

Places: The innermost chamber holds the evidence the Traveler examined: an experiment table with records of the experiments, shelves of bottles labelled as ingredients, mixtures in progress and ready-to-drink Sinthe (including a fruit-flavoured kind), boxes of personal belongings each labelled with a woman's name, a basin of pure Primordial Seawater, and a bookshelf with an investigation report on Callas.

Gameplay-wise the interactable items are logged in the Case Record as "Vacher's Experimental Records", "Sinthe", "The Missing Person's Possessions" and "Primordial Seawater Pool". The experiment records mention a researcher trying to repeat Jakob Ingold's findings on the Primordial Sea so he could save his lover Vigneire, who had been dissolved; the records call many specimens dissolved without any returning.

Dangers: The base is defended by Ousia-aligned clockwork meka (recon, survey and assault types) and by its mechanisms. During the quest the active party is limited to the Traveler.

Combat comes in waves of meks as the Traveler works through the mechanisms (gameplay detail: an Exquisite Chest rewards the second wave).

Atmosphere: Cold, quiet and clinical: a business and a laboratory in one, with neat labelling, rows of bottles and mementos of the missing. The writing in the experiment records is flat and matter-of-fact about horrifying results, which unsettles Paimon.

Quests: Visited in the Archon Quest "When All Return to the Waters" (Chapter IV, Act II "As Light Rain Falls Without Reason", 4.0). Finds here support Navia's charge in court and show that Sinthe, the serial disappearances and Vacher were tied together.

The discoveries show that Sinthe was diluted Primordial Seawater, that the missing young women's belongings were kept here, and that the researcher behind the experiments was named Vacher.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 canon gives no further use of the base. After Vacher's arrest the Sinthe production line was stopped and authorities moved to seize remaining stock.

Later events dealt with imitation Sinthe made from ordinary ingredients; Aquanigma is not shown again.

16.content:
Beaumont Workshop (also: Atelier Beaumont): Beaumont Workshop is a blacksmith's shop in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine, owned by Estelle. Its map description calls it the most renowned forging workshop in the Court.

Forging here is done by improved, fully automated machines that make works to an engineer's specifications, provided enough materials are supplied. It is unusual among Teyvat smithies in that its worker uses no hammer or anvil.

Places: The shop sits in the Vasari Passage district of the Court of Fontaine. Estelle serves customers at the counter, where the machines do the work behind her.

Its notice board advertises a one-stop custom service: clients are asked to bring a deposit, documents, their requirements and any relevant proof to a consultation, and the small print adds a surcharge for non-professional blueprints.

Per the wiki, this is the first blacksmith in the game whose worker has no hammer or anvil, because the forging is done by machine.

People: Estelle is the owner and the only named person associated with the workshop. Nothing about her history is stated in canon.

Atmosphere: A tidy, mechanised smithy: the sense is of precise engineering and paperwork, closer to a bespoke manufactory than a clanging forge.

Status as of 7.1: Open as a shop at the cutoff (7.1); nothing in later content changes it.

17.content: The workshop's advertisement board promotes full custom service and requires a deposit, documentation and proof at consultation, with an additional fee for non-professional blueprints. Its name is French, thought to combine words for "beautiful" and "mountain".

18.content:
Belleau Region (also: Belleau): The Belleau Region is the western part of Fontaine's map. It holds Poisson, a fishing town built in an old ship and a cavern below sea level, which is the main base of the Spina di Rosula; Romaritime Harbor, a waterfall elevator and lookout where Fontaine's aquabus line meets the way to Sumeru; and the western slopes of Mont Automnequi. In the Archon Quest it is where the Primordial Seawater disaster strikes Poisson.

The name looks like French for "beautiful water". The area's boss is the Emperor of Fire and Iron, and its local specialties are Beryl Conch, Lumidouce Bell, Rainbow Rose and Romaritime Flower.

Geography: Belleau covers Poisson, Romaritime Harbor and the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi. Mont Automnequi is one of Fontaine's best-known peaks and spans both the Belleau and Morte regions; this region has its western side. A tunnel, the Poisson Tunnel, cuts through those slopes so that the Clementine Line aquabus can pass. Fontaine is mostly water, but Belleau is one of the places where mountains, forest and cliffs show.

Romaritime Harbor stands beside a large waterfall, with a lower and an upper level joined by an elevator that takes a long time to reach the top. The harbour also provides passage to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru.

Places: - **Poisson**: fishing town at the foot of Mont Automnequi, built from a great ship and a large cavern below sea level.
- **Romaritime Harbor**: coastal elevator and observation deck on a waterfall, on the aquabus rail towards the Court of Fontaine.
- **West Slopes of Mont Automnequi**: the mountainside west of the peak, containing the Poisson Tunnel.

- **Poisson Tunnel**: the tunnel for the Clementine Line. The Fontaine Research Institute brought in huge engineering devices, including a boring machine nicknamed the Golden Vessel, to dig it. Its success led to a new generation of clockwork technology such as the Construction Specialist Mek.
- Romaritime Harbor has a Statue of The Seven and a Waverider Waypoint. Harbour staff include a harbour guard, sailors, a boat captain and Marechaussee Phantom members.

People: Poisson's residents mostly work in fishing or underwater salvage. The Spina di Rosula, a volunteer organisation that helps Fontaine's people with matters the Gardes cannot or will not handle, is based here; its president is Navia, who took over from her father Callas. Romaritime Harbor is staffed by sailors, harbour security, a member of the Gardes and a few travellers.

Poisson also has porters, a fisher, an engineer and Spina members such as the diver Archenoul. Several Poisson residents disappear or leave during the Archon Quest disaster and some return after it.

History: Legends say that before the first diluvian period Poisson was a central hub of Fontaine's maritime traffic. When the water level changed it lost its role as a major port but kept its cosy reputation. Roughly 500 years before the game's present, before the Cataclysm, the Siege of Poisson took place (see the Poisson entry): a violent episode in which the town was razed and many residents burned.

According to the wiki's compilation of quest texts, the siege began after Eduardo Baker, a vigilante peacekeeper arrested during the purge of Fleuve Cendre, was freed by his followers, who then seized Poisson and took Maison Gardiennage staff hostage. Marechaussee Hunter Emanuel Guillotin led the response. Renault de Petrichor and his wife were probably killed; his son Rene and Jakob survived and were sent to the Narzissenkreuz Institute.

The Fontaine Research Institute dug the Poisson Tunnel as one of the answers to the problem of linking the aquabus lines. A different aquabus route, the Callas Line, was shut down after the Institute's explosion (see the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region).

Atmosphere: Romaritime Harbor is noisy: the waterfall drowns out the comings and goings of the harbour, and the trip up is long, but travellers who board the Clementine Line feel the wait is worth it. Poisson is a quiet, cosy town of fishing boats and salvage divers; after the disaster it is subdued and busy with relief work.

Dangers: The region's boss is the Emperor of Fire and Iron. The great danger in the story is Primordial Seawater, which dissolves living people who touch it and which drowns the lower levels of Poisson during the disaster.

Travel: The aquabus runs from Romaritime Harbor to the Court of Fontaine. The harbour also gives onward passage to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru. Poisson sits on the Clementine Line at the foot of Mont Automnequi.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act V (Masquerade of the Guilty, 4.2) is set largely here: the quests Meeting Is Also Parting, Hunters, Prophets and Apocalypse are filed under the region. The rest are world quests, commissions and the like.

Other quests the wiki files under the region include Days Beneath the Waves, Birds in a Cage, Yesterday's Tears, Tomorrow's Light, The Child Who Doesn't Exist, A Lady's Invitation, Sea Breeze Rendezvous and Operation Downpour Simulation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Poisson is recovering from the Primordial Seawater disaster and no later content has changed the region.

The Spina di Rosula still runs from Poisson under Navia. The Fontaine Research Institute's tunnel and the aquabus remain in use.

19.content:
At the start of Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act V, an earthquake near Poisson is followed by water that rises quickly and then recedes. It turns out to be Primordial Seawater, which dissolves living beings. The lower levels of the town are hit hardest. Navia coordinates relief work, accepts Fatui help arranged by Arlecchino, and loses her friends Melus and Silver, who were swept away while carrying out the rescue plan she had started.

Neuvillette arrives separately and finds the Fatui helping. Navia later falls into the water and dreams of a trial at the Opera Epiclese in which the disaster's victims urge her to join them; Neuvillette rescues her and believes two Oceanids shielded her. The ruins near Poisson where the House of the Hearth heard that a child had found something are where stone slates about the Prophecy of Fontaine are found.

20.comment: Belleau Region: Romaritime Harbor and the Clementine Line
20.content:
Romaritime Harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built on the side of a waterfall, at the end of the aquabus rail running to the Court of Fontaine. The Clementine Line goes through the Poisson Tunnel; the harbour also provides passage to the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru.

The lower level has dock workers and a harbour security officer; the upper level has a boat captain, Marechaussee Phantom members and a self-proclaimed adventurer.

21.content:
Bertin's House of Curiosities (also: Bertin's House): Bertin's House of Curiosities is a shop in Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine, run by Mequignon. It sells curios such as jewels, instruments, perfumes and souvenirs, yet is technically a fashion workshop.

Mequignon collects curios as inspiration for her designs. Because of her artistic ideals she exchanges collection pieces that have stopped inspiring her for Hydro Sigils brought by adventurers.

Places: The shop lies in Quartier Lyonnais. Behind the counter stands a cabinet of violins that resembles a real-world orchestrion, a purely decorative detail.

The shop's name may allude to a historical French fashion designer; this is a wiki etymology guess, not canon.

People: Mequignon is the owner. Her goods are described as out of stock at times because nothing has caught her fancy lately, so her wares reflect her taste rather than steady supply.

Atmosphere: A cluttered, artful boutique: a designer's private cabinet of oddities that doubles as a shop.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

22.comment: Bertin's House of Curiosities: Mequignon's Exchange
22.content: Mequignon trades curios for Hydro Sigils, which adventurers collect in Fontaine, rather than for ordinary money alone. She does so because she only keeps what inspires her.

23.content:
Beryl Region (also: Beryl): The Beryl Region is a mountainous area in southern Fontaine, across the water from the Court of Fontaine. Its ridges and ruins are said to be what is left of a colossal beast, Elynas. Beneath its lakes lies Merusea Village, the home of the Melusines, and in the waters between the ridge and Mont Automnequi lies the Elton Trench, where Fontaine's old Navy sank.

In-game blurbs describe the area as beautiful but rarely visited by locals or tourists. The local boss is the Hydro Tulpa, and many Fatui, hilichurls, ruin machines and tainted Hydro phantasms roam it.

Geography: The region is built around a main island with two named subareas: Elynas, the northern half of the island, with the surface remains of the beast it is named for, and Merusea Village hidden inside the beast's body under mountains and lakes. West of it lies the underwater Elton Trench, between Elynas and Mont Automnequi. Mint-dotted highlands and ruins lie along the ridge.

The tall mountains are said by legend to be Elynas' skeleton, worn by wind and dust into a home for 'countless souls'. The official map blurb describes it as 'an ancient ruin-studded mountain range across the water from the Court of Fontaine'.

Places: - **Elynas**: the lush northern half of the main island, with the beast's surface remains.
- **Merusea Village**: the Melusine village, entered only from underwater, by diving near Elynas' skull or in the pool above the Beryl Region Statue of The Seven. Official text calls it an adorable and mysterious village where even the chimneys bubble.
- **Elton Trench**: underwater trench with shipwrecks of the former Navy.

The region also has an unmarked ruin north of Romaritime Harbor with a collapsed entrance, found in a treasure hunter's journal, and a Uninhabited Hypostasis Platform and Shrine of Depths near Elynas.

People: Merusea Village is home to the Melusines, who call Elynas 'Father'. On land there are named Melusines such as Carabosse, Cosanzeana, Flo, Iara, Laume, Lutine, Rufina, Sedile, Serene, Sluasi, Verenata and Virda; underwater there are Glaisti, Granna, Puca and Thirona. Xana is the village's vendor. The only named human NPC in the region page is Depierris.

The wiki notes that Elynas' spirit appears in Melusine form and that Melusines were a race created unintentionally by him.

Culture: Official text says that many centuries ago the followers of Egeria treated this ridge as a favourite excursion and picnic spot, singing about love and dreams as pure as polished gems. Those songs have faded; now only cool breezes cross the highlands.

History: Elynas was a giant being whose death and remains shaped the ridge. According to the wiki's account of the Ancient Colors quests, Fontaine's Navy fought him and its ships sank in what is now the Elton Trench; the ship Sponsian was split in half in the final attack. Elynas bled out and died, then looked after the Melusines in the afterlife.

Quests in this region show Jakob collecting Elynas' blood to revive him, and the Traveler stopping this because the revived body would crush the Melusine homes. Elynas thanked the Traveler in a brief 'time of life' before the attempt failed.

Jakob hired Eremites to buy paintings made with Elynas' blood from the painter Mamere, to gather blood without violence; the Traveler's chance meeting with Mamere spoiled this. Wildlife that fed on the remains may have produced at least two Consecrated Beasts, and Elynas' flesh is said to harden into a protective membrane rather than decay.

Atmosphere: Quiet and lonely: cool breezes over ruins and huge bones on the ridge, lakes below. Underwater, the Elton Trench is dim, strewn with wrecks and haunted by ghostly legends.

Dangers: The Hydro Tulpa is the region's boss. Elite enemies include Breacher Primuses, tainted Hydro phantasms, Fatui Pyro Agents and Electro Cicin Mages, Mirror Maidens, Lawachurls and ruin machines.

Travel: The ridge lies across the water from the Court of Fontaine. Merusea Village can only be entered by diving. The region has its own Statue of The Seven.

Quests: Region-tagged quests include the Ancient Colors storyline (including Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog), the Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste series, the Strange Stone Chronicle series, Narcissus's Waltz, The Lone Phantom Sail, Echoes of the Ancient World and several commissions and aesthetic critiques.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Elynas' remains still shape the area and the Melusines of Merusea live there.

No later version added Beryl-specific story in the sources checked.

24.content:
Elynas is a giant beast whose remains encompass much of the Beryl Region, according to the wiki. Melusines call him Father. He realised his joy was causing suffering for others and let himself die; in death he wished to protect the Melusines. He is mainly known through the Ancient Colors quests.

The wiki ties his blood to Abyssal power and to creatures such as the riftwolves and Breacher Primuses. Jakob's attempt to revive him is stopped by the Traveler.

25.content: An underwater trench between Elynas and Mont Automnequi where Fontaine's former Navy sank in battle against Elynas. Divers can find shipwrecks, Pneumousia blocks and relays. The name probably honours Admiral Basil Elton.

26.content:
Bravais' Press Works (also: Bravais Press Works, Bravais' Press Workshop, Arkhium Forge): Bravais' Press Works is a hidden underground workshop in the Submerged Stony Path below the Liffey Region of Fontaine. Its big Forging Press refines Arkhium Stock (fused from seven Mysterious Ores) into Arkhium Lumenite. Running the press ends with the whole chamber flooding, so it can be used only once. Its paperwork mentions a Senior Researcher named Bravais, whom nobody else seems to care about.

It is the site of the hidden exploration objective that the wiki calls Arkhium Forge (an unofficial name), released with Version 4.1. A passage opened by the finished work leads to a current ending at ruins beneath a Statue of the Seven.

Geography: Three routes reach it: a waterway from a Millennial Pearl Seahorse's chamber; a hidden tunnel in Kuisel's Clockwork Workshop just before its last room (open after the quest Road to the Singularity); and a water current at the end of the Geode Mine Shaft (open after An Eye for an Eye).

The chamber has a central Forging Press with its terminal, three steam valves with handwheels, a cooling and drainage terminal on a lower ramp north-west, a blocked water intake at the bottom and drainage pipes later clogged by Red Meanies.

Places: The press and main terminal; the cooling and drainage terminal; the desk with the Maintenance Log; the Emergency Handbook beneath the entrance platform. Beyond the finished press lies a newly opened passage with a precious chest, then a current. The wiki also names a Bravais' Hidden Study that the Lumenite opens, with luxurious and precious chests.

People: Senior Researcher Bravais is the only named person. The Emergency Handbook tells operators to contact Bravais about any fault it does not list. Beyond the press, the current ends at the ruins under the Liffey Statue of the Seven where Desnos is found.

Governance: The workshop follows written standards: protective gear, a full equipment inspection, correct stock placement, an energy supply check, and manual operation of the hammers at the right moment when the stock glows orange-red. Faults are handled by the Emergency Response Handbook, third edition.

History: Canon says little. The Maintenance Log shows an attempt to keep the cooling system and leaking seals under control with stopgaps. Repair requests note leakage near the water intake and say a temporary sealant was applied and the cooling system's use suspended because of backflow. The log notes that no one but Bravais really cares about the devices, and hopes the emergency drain proves useful.

The hazards were known: the log warns that removing the seals and running the cooling would fill the room at once and ruin the press. The player eventually triggers exactly that, so the press is destroyed by design at the end of the process.

Status as of 7.1: After the Arkhium Lumenite is collected the press is flooded and ruined; the workshop remains submerged. Nothing newer than 4.1 is recorded.

Dangers: Steam valves, overheating, Pyro Slimes that spawn from the heated press, a large Pyro Slime, nimble harvester meks near the handwheel, and rising water. In-game this is a puzzle of pressure, heat, cooling and drainage.

Atmosphere: Hissing valves, orange glow from the stock, then a deep flooded hall. The log sounds like a tired technician writing to nobody.

27.comment: Bravais' Press Works: The Forging Press Process
27.content: Gameplay-derived process (labelled as game mechanics). The operator closes three steam valves to restore pipe pressure, places the Arkhium Stock, powers and starts the press, and times the hammer strikes when the stock glows orange-red. After overheating, slimes are defeated, the press is cooled with Hydro or Cryo, then flooded by breaking a blocked water intake. Xenochromatic Hunter's Ray and Hat Jellyfish abilities clear the drainage pipes of Red Meanies. A final run ruptures a seal and floods the chamber, after which the Lumenite can be taken.

28.comment: Bravais' Press Works: The Maintenance Log and Emergency Handbook
28.content: The log laments stopgap fixes and that only Bravais cares about the machinery. The Third Edition handbook lists faults: insufficient energy supply from low pipe pressure, system overheated, water entering the system, and a blocked emergency drain, and says to contact Bravais for anything else.

29.content:
Caesareum Palace (also: Caesareum, Palace of Caesareum): Caesareum Palace is a ruin in Machimos, the outer city of Remuria's drowned capital. It served as a training ground for the empire's legions and as the place where the chains meant to bind the vishap prince Scylla were stored. According to the records, the Harmost Boethius ordered Legio VI to hold the Dragonborn back here, and the legion defended it to the end.

Engravings in two caves tell the story from the empire's own point of view: orders, a plan to seal the city, and an epitaph by a soldier who died holding the line. The area is reached through the Sea of Bygone Eras after Underwater Nocturne in Canticles of Harmony.

Geography: A subarea of the Sea of Bygone Eras with a western cave and an eastern cave. A nameless stone statue stands near the western cave and acts as a monument to the fallen. Praetorian Golems patrol the ground.

It lies among the ruins of Machimos beside the Initium Iani gate, Portus Anticus and Hortus Euergetis. Locked chambers deep in the western cave open only after the monument's challenge has been completed.

Places: Western cave: holds the first engraving, an order about Legio VI, and a hidden chamber with the second, the plan to seal the city.
Eastern cave: holds the soldier's epitaph near two Praetorian Golems.
Nameless Stone Statue: a monument that begins a combat trial against Bathysmal Vishaps when approached.

People: Legio VI Rithimi Versi, part of the Legion Athanatoi, under the Harmost Boethius, who took command from Euergetia. The soldier Aetius and his sister Placidia are named in an epitaph. Euergetia and Boethius are the authorities cited in orders.

History: When Scylla marched Dragonborn on the capital, the Harmost Boethius gave Legio VI Rithimi Versi the task of stopping them here. The legion defended the palace until the end, with not a single deserter and no enemy breaking through, according to ancient records.

The first engraving records Euergetia entrusting Legio VI to Boethius to guard the palace, and says the Dragonborn should be received with the legion's tradition of "gently uplifting barbarians" without enmity; the next lines are crossed out. The second, an order from Boethius, commands that Portus Anticus and the Initium Iani be sealed at once, seven defensive layers set, and the routes of escape closed. The three chains made for Scylla have been moved to the palace and, if the chieftain of the wicked drakes cannot be slain, are to imprison him there forever. It ends "For the Empire, for [name erased], for human civilization".

The third engraving, in the eastern cave, is the epitaph of Aetius and his sister Placidia. They did not die of illness but fell resisting the traitorous Dragonborn at the city gates; Legio VI had no deserters, and they followed Euergetia to the northern border to bring civilisation to the tribes. They choose "civilization and death". Other texts show that Scylla's invasion was actually part of Remus's secret plan to destroy Phobos, and that Scylla was lured into a trap and sealed.

Quests: In The Last Day of Remuria the Traveler, Paimon and Cassiodor in cat form free Scylla by breaking three chains of his seal; the palace's engravings explain what chains of that kind were made for. The optional exploration "Symphony of Yore, Restored Once More" collects six scores for the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, and the score Dies Irae is earned by completing the stone statue's trial here.

The trial has four waves: two Primordial Bathysmal Vishaps, then a swarm of hatchling vishaps while a buff from "ancient heroic spirits" damages nearby enemies, then the Coral Defenders. Completing it unlocks the sealed chamber and an achievement titled after the legion's lines about telling the citizens of the capital.

The engravings give a clear chain of command: Euergetia assigns Legio VI, Boethius directs it, and the soldiers are told to receive the Dragonborn as guests until the plan changes. The change is visible in the erasure of the gentle lines and in the second order, which seals the gates and prepares to trap the enemy. Two Praetorian Golems stand guard near the epitaph. The area also offers a time trial challenge of traversing.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet after the Requiem. The area is explorable and its dead legionaries are at rest.

Nothing after 4.6 changes it.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems, bathysmal vishaps and Primordial Bathysmal Vishaps appear here, and Coral Defenders appear in the monument trial. The deep water and the Remurian machines are hostile to explorers who do not know the area's rules.

Atmosphere: Stone caves, scarred rock and the memory of a soldier's pride. The tone of the engravings is dutiful and proud, and then desperate. The stone monument asks passers-by to say the legion did its duty.

30.comment: Caesareum Palace: Legio VI Rithimi Versi
30.content: A Remurian legion of the Legion Athanatoi named for rhythm and verse. It served the northern border under Euergetia's direction and later guarded Caesareum Palace under Boethius, where it held back Scylla's Dragonborn. Its vicarius Hirtius wrote a survey of the northern tribes found in the Faded Castle.

31.content: Three chains forged for Scylla, said to be made with Euergetia's blood and illegible bone, were moved here, to be used to imprison him if he could not be slain. In The Last Day of Remuria the Traveler breaks them one by one, helped by a negotiation with Legio IX golems who thought they were still at war. The same quest explains that the invasion was a pretext in Remus's own plan.

32.content:
Café Lutece (also: Cafe Lutece): Café Lutece is a well-known coffee house in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine. The wiki calls it the main restaurant for Fontaine. Arouet manages it. Its map description calls it the most popular café in the passage and says that the owner encourages customers from every background to discuss philosophy and other subjects as they drink their coffee. Any topic is allowed except death.

It sells coffee, snacks and sweets, and it has a message board where patrons trade gossip, dilemmas and opinions.

Places: A single café with a counter run by Arouet, whose stall is open at all times and restocks daily. Fonta, Île flottante, Conch Madeleine and coffee beans are on sale, and the café also sells recipes for Île flottante, Conch Madeleine, Crêpes Suzette, La Lettre à Focalors, Blubber Profiterole and Bulle Soufflé. Its message board stands beside Arouet.

Staff the wiki names are Arouet (manager), Chatelet (labelled 'Gestionnaire'), Gontharet and Menthe.

People: Arouet is the manager and sole named proprietor. His idle line is 'Coffee is life!'. The wiki lists him as formerly affiliated with Maison Gestion.

Clorinde is a regular customer, who tracks the days on which her favourite blend is on offer (mentioned in the quest Charlotte: Patience).

Culture: The café keeps one rule for conversation: all topics are welcome, philosophy above all, except death. Its message board invites gossip, deep thoughts, and suggestions for the café. Posts cycle at random.

The board's posts show a cross-section of Fontaine: a father asking whether to tell his son that the Oceanids left Fontaine long ago (with a child's message saying the real reason for the trip was to spend time with his father, and the owner suggesting that being together matters more than the truth); and a rumour thread about a missing-persons case, answered by a notice from Maison Gardiennage telling people not to spread unfounded rumours.

Coffee and conversation are the point of the place. The café offers a featured blend on particular days. The wiki notes that 'Lutèce' is the French name of the Gallo-Roman town that preceded Paris, and 'lucerne' is an Old French word for a lamp or lantern.

Atmosphere: A relaxed café where customers of all backgrounds sit over coffee and talk ideas, as its map description invites them to.

Dangers: No dangers are described in canon. The one house rule is to keep death out of the conversation.

Travel: The café lies in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine, marked on the map as a restaurant. It is open at any hour.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

33.comment: Café Lutece: Café Lutece Message Board
33.content: The board welcomes gossip and chit-chat, deep epiphanies, and suggestions or complaints about the café. Messages rotate randomly each time it is read. The topics range from a family visit to Fontaine in search of Oceanids, to a case of disappearing young women and the Maison Gardiennage's warning against rumours, to a post about acrobatic troupes banned from Palais Mermonia.

key: Central Laboratory of the Fontaine Research Institute
34.content:
Central Laboratory Ruins (also: Ruins of the Central Laboratory, Central Laboratory of the Fontaine Research Institute, Fontaine Research Institute ruins): The Central Laboratory Ruins are what remains of the heart of the old Fontaine Research Institute, in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region next to the Liffey Region. Years before the Traveler arrived, an experiment built around the crystal Arkhium exploded here and destroyed most of the Institute. The wreckage now hangs in a distorted gravity state beside large cubes of water floating in the air, and the surviving researchers treat it as a hazard that could blow again.

The site is tied to three names. Edwin Eastinghouse, the celebrated and reckless senior researcher, led the Arkhium project here. Raimondo and Choiseul now run the Institute from a new site and handle the ruins. Nacker, Edwin's former associate, was the man who knew how to operate Edwin's machine.

Geography: The ruins sit high above the surrounding lowland, held in a state of abnormal gravity. Large cubes of water, called Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies, float in the air around them; they are a by-product of the explosion, and the Institute's own people use them as a way to rise to the ruins by "diving" upward through them. The alternative is to glide in from the highest mountain on the opposite bank.

Inside lie wrecked laboratory rooms, broken houses and rock, the huge disc-like Experimental Field Generator, and a large lump of Arkhium wired to a suppression system. Residual Arkhium energy lingers in the air and water, and it does not fade quickly. Lower in the region are the Executive Office, the Academic Assembly Hall, the Materials Office and Mary-Ann Memorial Park, all of which were battered by the first shock waves.

Places: Central Laboratory (the ruined core): in the Institute's own map text, the laboratory sat at the centre of the campus, held the most advanced instruments in Fontaine and was chiefly occupied with the Experimental Field Generator.
Experimental Field Generator: a huge gravity-altering machine, now powerless except for backup cores.
Large Arkhium mass: the energy source kept dormant by an inhibitor with condensing components.
Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies: floating water cubes that carry residual energy flow.

Nearby, Mary-Ann Memorial Park took the first blast wave and lost most of its buildings; Nacker hoped some paper assets had survived there. A stone tablet in the region lists the deeds of ancient Marechaussee Hunters, an unrelated older layer of Fontaine's hidden history.

People: Raimondo and Choiseul lead the rebuilding from the New Fontaine Research Institute; Raimondo is the technician who handled the disaster evaluation, Choiseul the speech-making administrator. Nacker, once Edwin's associate, guides the Traveler to the ruins in the World Quest and then disappears. The reporter Chronie of The Steambird follows the expedition. Edwin himself was dismissed from the Institute for long unauthorised absence after he vanished.

History: The Institute's Arkhium Research Project aimed to use Arkhium, a powerful crystal energy source, to counter gravity and perhaps lift Fontaine into a "city in the sky" so people could survive the prophesied flood. An overload of the project's Arkhium Kinetic Core caused a huge explosion that destroyed most of the Institute and left the Central Laboratory in ruins.

Edwin Eastinghouse led the project with collaborators including Nacker and Raimondo. He built the Experimental Field Generator, which makes a Gravity Reduction Field. He and Raimondo created the Arkhium Kinetic Core to power it, together with a suppression device. After the blast, nearly every Arkhium crystal in the region was shattered into fragments that could still react to each other by resonance, so the Institute used the Generator's gravity field to gather and hold them beneath the ruins, and placed Survey Anchors to monitor radiation. Arkhium mining under the Fortress of Meropide was ended.

Edwin was believed dead, but later quests show him alive and still enthusiastic about Arkhium. By his own account he was inspecting other departments when it blew. He had re-established a lab in the Morte Region, found backers, and was eventually discovered and brought back; he and Nacker were then dismissed and sent to the Fortress of Meropide. The Institute officially kept him on the books for a time and then dismissed him for being absent without permission.

Nacker's rival story and Raimondo's are both told within the World Quest. Nacker treats Edwin's fall as a lost chance at the Director post and complains of Choiseul and Raimondo; Raimondo blames him for stripping the Institute's assets and for the later sabotage.

Quests: The World Quest 'Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble' (4.1, part of the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles) takes the Traveler through an absurdly bureaucratic qualification review at the New Fontaine Research Institute, then up to the ruins with Nacker and the reporter Chronie to lower the Generator's gravity field.

At the ruins Nacker prepares to turn the dormant Arkhium into a three-state form with Raimondo's catalyst. A second explosion rocks the site while the Institute leaders pose for a photo. Raimondo and the Traveler return, retrieve condensing components for the inhibitor, and the Generator, fed temporarily by two Pneumousia cores, moves on its own and must be shut down. The Arkhium is stabilised to an inert state. Raimondo concludes that Nacker stole the Arkhium Kinetic Core and overloaded the big lump as a cover for his escape, and asks the Traveler to keep quiet about it; the Traveler may instead tell Chronie everything. Choiseul declares that the site will be preserved and rebuilt as a safety education centre.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are stable but dangerous, kept under watch by the Institute, and the Arkhium is inert. No later version is known to have changed them.

Nacker's whereabouts were left open at the end of the World Quest; later content has him and Edwin dismissed and held at the Fortress of Meropide. The Institute itself works from a new campus.

Dangers: Out-of-control clockwork meka (Ousia and Pneuma types) keep reactivating when Arkhium energy flows, Hydro Slimes and tainted water-spouting phantasms appear around the condensing components, and the Experimental Field Generator can still move if powered. Direct exposure to active Arkhium causes nausea, vomiting, bleeding under the skin and even coma; the Traveler and Paimon show unusual tolerance. Swimming into the energised water cubes at the wrong moment is lethal, according to Raimondo.

Atmosphere: Blue light, cold stone, water hanging in the air, silence broken by humming machinery and the click of aggrieved meka. It feels like a failed ideal left to rot, with a faint smell of scorched metal. The in-game viewpoint text calls it the wreck of shattered dreams and warns that some people see its energy as having another purpose.

35.comment: Central Laboratory Ruins: Experimental Field Generator
35.content: A huge device invented by Edwin Eastinghouse to create a Gravity Reduction Field; early estimates said it could lift a block of buildings. It is powered by the Arkhium Kinetic Core, which Edwin and Raimondo developed along with a suppression system. After the explosion the Institute uses it to gather and hold shattered Arkhium. Nacker was personally trained by Edwin to operate it. Its backup cores are Pneumousia cores; when Raimondo draws on them, the machine moves and attacks the Traveler.

36.comment: Central Laboratory Ruins: Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies
36.content: Large cubes of water floating above the ruins, created by the explosion. The Institute treats them as a travel route: one can dive upward through them. After the second blast their energy flow grows turbulent and dangerous.

37.comment: Central Laboratory Ruins: Arkhium Kinetic Core
37.content: A concentrated power source built around a large piece of Arkhium, used to run the Experimental Field Generator. When it overloaded, the first explosion happened. In the World Quest Raimondo claims that the core was stolen by Nacker, after which a second, smaller blast followed.

38.comment: Central Laboratory Ruins: Nacker and the Second Explosion
38.content: Nacker is Edwin's former associate. He guides the Traveler through the review and ascent, and calls himself the one person who can run the Generator. After he stays behind alone to start it, a blast hits, and Raimondo says Nacker has taken the Arkhium Kinetic Core and overloaded the large Arkhium on purpose as a distraction. Nacker is not seen again in the quest. Raimondo says he would prefer to believe the man died, but his own analysis suggests that someone gathered undepleted Arkhium and piled it there to cover up traces of what had been taken.

39.content:
Chemin de L'Espoir (also: Path of Hope): Chemin de L'Espoir (French for "Path of Hope") is a subarea in the Court of Fontaine Region of Fontaine, within the map level of the Source of All Waters, the Great Fontaine Lake. It is known in canon mainly as a place on the map and as the starting point of a timed Daily Commission. No story or lore is tied to it.

Its only recorded content is the Daily Commission "Aim Upstream", in which the Traveler must reach a marked destination within 120 seconds. The subarea appeared with Version 4.0, together with the rest of the Court of Fontaine Region.

Geography: The subarea lies within the Court of Fontaine Region, the area around the city of the Court of Fontaine. The wiki lists no features, enemies, domains or landmarks for it, and there is no official description text. Describe scenes there only in general Fontaine terms and do not name specific landmarks.

The name is French (chemin de l'espoir, "path of hope"), and the English localisation renders it that way. Which route, bank or street it refers to is not stated.

Quests: "Aim Upstream" is a repeatable Daily Commission starting here: a short timed run to a target location, with rewards scaled to Adventure Rank. Only the Traveler is involved and it has no story significance.

The wiki's commission page shows two images of the start location but lists no dialogue, NPCs or lore. The time limit is the only mechanical detail: 120 seconds to reach the target. Because nothing else is known, any depiction of the subarea in a scene should stay vague and avoid inventing a destination or a hope-related legend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary, accessible part of Fontaine's capital region with no recorded events.

40.content:
Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland (also: Fantasyland): Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland is an amusement park and fan convention for film lovers in the Court of Fontaine Region. It was the idea of the engineer Lepine-Pauline and was built almost overnight by Navia and the Spina di Rosula for the limited-time Whirling Waltz event in Version 5.6. Its theme is Fontaine's film-making, and it is named for Surintendante Chevalmarin, whose image Lepine-Pauline was allowed to use by Furina.

During the event the Traveler helps run the park for Navia, choosing attractions, staff and theme dishes to raise its revenue.

Places: Three main attractions form the core of the park: Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces and Mellow Manor, with landscaped areas and booths built around crowd-favourite films. There is also a theme restaurant where the event's dishes are served; Escoffier is seen working at her station there.

The map description stresses two audiences: film buffs who want a stage to show their passion and promote their favourite films, and visitors who know little about cinema and simply want to enjoy the sights, lights and sounds. The park's attractions are upgraded and expanded during the event, and its facilities grow with revenue.

People: Lepine-Pauline, an engineer and film enthusiast, hosts the convention and gives technical support. Navia, president of the Spina di Rosula, leads the actual construction and operation. Kinich and Ajaw, Escoffier and others are met at the park during the event story.

Lepine-Pauline obtained Furina's permission to use the image of her close friend Chevalmarin. Navia explains in "Business Acumen From the Spina" that the enthusiasts who proposed the park are not all-round experts and mostly design the booths, so the Spina handles long-term operations and standard strategy guides for the activities.

Governance: Run on the ground by the Spina di Rosula under Navia, with Lepine-Pauline as host. Lepine-Pauline says the event and venue only got their approval after long paperwork, whereupon she asked Navia for help at once.

History: The park is the setting for Whirling Waltz (5.6, running 2025-05-09 to 2025-05-26). In the opening story "An Overnight Fantasyland" the Traveler and Paimon hear of it in the Court of Fontaine, learn it was raised in a single night, and are invited to join its crew. Navia then teaches the Traveler her time-slot method of planning, where each operating cycle has limited slots for upgrades, expansion and hiring.

The event's reward milestones are tied to total revenue earned by the park, culminating in the weapon Sequence of Solitude and other prizes. These are game rewards, not in-world facts.

The event ran in phases from 2025-05-09, 2025-05-11 and 2025-05-13. Players needed to have progressed through the Fontaine story to run it, and the three attractions are expanded through levels, staff hires and theme dishes. In-world, Navia describes the park as a sugar-free macaron: several areas were still being built when the Traveler arrived, and the Spina had hired only a limited number of craftsmen.

Atmosphere: Festive and slightly chaotic: colourful film sets, crowds of fans, the smells of the theme restaurant and constant small crises of a venue assembled in a night.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the park is an event location from 5.6. No later story uses it as a setting, and its permanent status is not documented.

41.comment: Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland: Whirling Waltz Convention
41.content: Whirling Waltz was a 5.6 flagship event in which the Traveler and Paimon, strolling the Court of Fontaine, are drawn into a film fan convention hosted at Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland. The same event story also touches on the arrival of visitors from Natlan in Fontaine. In-universe it is a one-off fan festival; it is not a permanent institution of Fontaine.

42.content:
Chioriya Boutique (also: Chioriya): Chioriya Boutique is a fashion shop and label owned by Chiori, an independent designer from Inazuma, on a busy street in the Quartier Lyonnais of the Court of Fontaine. It looks small, but passers-by stop to look in, and its clothes have a good reputation. Its owner has a blunt, lightning-quick manner with troublemakers. The wiki also records a nickname for it, the 'intelligence boutique', because customers talk freely about their business there.

Chiori is rarely in the shop while she is designing, and when she is there it usually means she is in a good mood.

Geography: The shop fronts one of the main thoroughfares of Quartier Lyonnais in the Court of Fontaine. A bell rings above the door when customers enter. The interior can be entered after starting the story quest Stained Spots.

The sign uses Fontaine script. Before Chiori's story quest the sign read 'Couture' (the French word for dressmaking), and after The Woven and the Cut it reads 'Chiori', a sign put up by Kirara and Navia.

Places: Inside, a table near the front door holds letters addressed to Chiori, and her work desk holds notes she has not sent.

Letters on the table are from Emilie (thanks for fragrance feedback, plus a sample of a Romaritime scent), Navia (an invitation to a Spina di Rosula party, asking that Eloffe be brought along), Kirara (a customer asking for a child's outfit, with sizes) and Chevreuse (a request to watch a judge's wife, who shops there). On the desk are Chiori's travel plans, noting a new clothing trend in Natlan and Snezhnayan winter-wear designs for reference, a letter to Chevreuse about a Maison Gardiennage employee overheard discussing a deal, and a letter to Charlotte about decorations for Monsieur Vérité that politely refuses interviews over tea.

People: Chiori owns the shop and designs the clothes. The staff the wiki names are Eloffe, Graciette, Trudaine and, inside, Laetitia.

Friends who write to her include Navia, Kirara, Emilie, Chevreuse and Charlotte.

Culture: The shop is a social and fashion hub. Well-dressed merchants and officials come to show off what they know as much as what they wear, and Chiori's profile treats the intelligence as something that arrives on its own rather than something she hunts for.

Chiori then decided to pass on hints to friends in the form of letters or a quiet word when someone's interests or Fontaine's safety are involved. She compares this to tailoring: placing each thread where it belongs. The brand itself grew from her wish to make a name in Fontaine, a name she first tried out in Inazuma while turning down a place at Ogura Textiles & Kimonos.

Chiori's profile adds that she draws her designs casually, brings the drafts to the boutique, copies them onto toile, and then the originals end up as tea-stained wrapping paper for taiyaki. The drafts are for customers to admire and for fashion magazines. The brand name itself came to her in Inazuma, when an offer from Ogura Textiles & Kimonos made her realise she did not want to work under someone else's shop name.

Dangers: Rowdy drunks sometimes burst in, as the profile's opening shows, and Chiori deals with them herself.

Atmosphere: A modest-looking shop on a busy street. The door bell chimes for each customer, the greeting is confident if not exactly enthusiastic, and customers speak admiringly of the handiwork.

Travel: The boutique is a marked point of interest in Quartier Lyonnais in the Court of Fontaine.

Quests: Chiori's story quest, When They Talk About Tonight (Cisoria Chapter Act I), runs through the shop in Stained Spots and The Woven and the Cut (4.5).

Status as of 7.1: Open and trading as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

43.content: Chiori's profile says that no one is sure when the shop gained the nickname 'intelligence boutique', and Chiori is as puzzled as anyone. She came to see that information flows through her door of its own accord, because well-dressed merchants and officials boast about what they know. She finds it distracting, but she began to pass on warnings as a favour. Letters on her table show the same pattern: Chevreuse, a law-enforcement friend, asks her to watch for a regular customer, and Chiori writes back about overheard talk of a deal.

44.content:
Clivus Capitolinus (also: Capitoline Hill, Capitoline Rise): Clivus Capitolinus is the hill at the heart of Capitolium, the inner city of ancient Remuria's capital. Its summit holds the Domus Aurea, the royal palace. The name also covers the cavern under the hill, which contains the Local Legend Cineas, called the Unreturned Envoy. It is named after the road up the Capitoline Hill in Rome.

The Traveler comes here in the final stretch of Canticles of Harmony (version 4.6), climbing past the hill's old palace to face Boethius inside Domus Aurea.

Geography: The hill belongs to the Sea of Bygone Eras. The surface area is divided into Capitolium and its Old Palace, with the Domus Aurea on top and the Sacellum Requietis inside that palace. A cavern runs beneath the hill. Capitolium itself is entered only through the Passage of Ianus from Machimos.

The approach to the palace is through golden aqueducts (the Alta Semita) and other fairways that once carried the symphony, near Collegium Phonascorum. Gradus ad Capitolium, the name of the quest, means roughly steps to the Capitol.

Places: Domus Aurea: the golden palace on the hill, with its upper-level throne room.
Capitolium: Old Palace: an older palace precinct that appears as part of the same map level.
