The cavern beneath: holds an engraving and the sealed-in vishap Cineas.

The engraving is found just north of Cineas, inside the cavern.

People: In its prime, Capitolium was a haven for artists and musicians where only the most outstanding were admitted, and a smaller number served the God King directly. In the present, the only resident is the vishap Cineas.

History: This was the centre of Remuria: the palace where Remus listened to every note of the empire and corrected any discord with a pluck of his strings, surrounded by theatres and palaces with carved beams and domes. After the great wave, the whole hill sank.

An engraving in the cavern records Boethius ordering Dragonborn envoys to be received to discuss cooperation. The rest has been struck out, and below it come scratched lines repeating "Traitor", followed by a line addressed to "xenoproles" telling them to "sink into this immortal prison with us". Cassiodor says an envoy from Fontaine was imprisoned here by Boethius.

Read with Scylla's account, the engraving suggests Boethius used the language of diplomacy against the Dragonborn side, as Scylla says he did when he claimed to have ordered the legions to stop resisting and then turned on them. This is an inference, since no text says so directly about Cineas.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet since the Requiem. The Domus Aurea above is silent and Cineas remains in the cavern, where he can be fought but need not be.

The score Confutatis for the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box lies near Cineas. The hill is part of the explorable area after the 4.6 quests.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems patrol Domus Aurea and its approaches. Cineas is a powerful Primordial Bathysmal Vishap Local Legend; he does not have to be fought to obtain Confutatis.

Atmosphere: Hushed grandeur. The hill looks like a processional way that has stopped mid-ceremony, and the cavern below feels like a cell, with scratched words on the wall.

45.comment: Clivus Capitolinus: Cineas, the Unreturned Envoy
45.content: A Primordial Bathysmal Vishap, a Local Legend whose title calls him an envoy who never returned. Osse (Cassiodor) tells the Traveler that an envoy from Fontaine was once imprisoned in this area by Boethius. The cavern engraving is the best surviving hint of how that happened; no source gives Cineas's own words.

46.content:
Collegium Phonascorum (also: College of Music Teachers, Court of Harmonious Rhythm): The Collegium Phonascorum (Latin, roughly "college of music teachers") was the educational centre of Remuria, set in the inner city Capitolium under the sea off Fontaine. There the Harmosts and music lecturers taught Remurians about the symphony of Phobos. Notes left among its ruins record a Harmost's reasoning about music, will and fate, and show how a learned institution fed a brutal ideology.

Introduced in 4.6. The notes divide all things into Substance, Property, Quality and Relation, and conclude that people shaped by Fortuna must be eradicated. The notes are unsigned, so whether this was official doctrine is not stated.

Geography: A subarea of Capitolium, near the Alta Semita and the approach to the Domus Aurea. Two golden Auric Anglerfish drift near it and have trapped a creature that Monsieur Os remarks on.

It lay inside the inner city, which could be entered only through the Initium Iani and the Passage of Ianus.

Culture: Remuria's power rested on music. The Collegium taught that the symphony of Phobos, a composite of mortal melodies, could challenge the order of Fortuna, the fate that governs mortals and gods alike. Lecturers were the Harmosts themselves and other teachers.

Harmost's Notes (II) explains the Remurian philosophy in musical terms. Musica Humana (the music of a person) should match Musica Mundana (the music of the world); the "Piercing of the Ego" (to play one's own music) means piercing Substance and Quality and so controlling one's own will. The notes treat the Quadrant of Qualities as memories, wishes, soul and persona.

The notes hold that even gods and mortals are fragile, like taut strings, and so the instruments' ratios must be adjusted "to avoid profaning the melody of morality", blending mortal melodies into the symphony called Phobos. If Phobos stopped, everything would collapse, and all would sink to dreamless dreams under Fortuna.

History: Canon records the Collegium only through this text and its Latin name. The notes were presumably written while Remuria still stood. The notes argue that people who stand apart from Phobos "cannot be regarded as humans equal to us", a line of thought that echoes the Remurian war against the northern tribes; canon does not say who wrote the notes or whether they were official teaching.

The notes reason that distance from Phobos is betrayal; the louder a mortal's music and the firmer a mortal's wish, the firmer Fortuna's order becomes. They argue that such people have no real choice, only a path fated for them, and conclude on grounds of "morality and rationality" that they should be eradicated like plagues and wildfires, else Fortuna's symphony will grow to a deafening roar and no one will ever again be able to choose rebellion.

Quests: Part of the area is used in Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction: Part II, a child quest of Gradus ad Capitolium. Monsieur Os comments on the two Auric Anglerfish near it.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and silent as of 7.1, a sunken place whose lessons now serve only as record.

Dangers: Two Auric Anglerfish near the ruin; beyond it the Domus Aurea is guarded by Praetorian Golems.

Atmosphere: A hall of broken columns and silent instruments, still faintly resonant with fragments of painted music. The mood is solemn and a little chilling because of the notes.

47.content: An unsigned lecture note recording Aurelius's fourfold division of phenomena: Substance, Property, Quality and Relation, with Quality as the "Quadrant of Qualities" of memories, wishes, soul and persona. It describes the Piercing of the Ego, argues for tuning the human symphony into Phobos, and ends in a call for eradication of those it deems merely fated players of Fortuna's score.

48.content:
Coupon Cafeteria (also: Meropide cafeteria): The Coupon Cafeteria is the canteen of the Fortress of Meropide, in its Administrative Area, where convicts gather for daily meals. Each prisoner may claim one free Welfare Meal a day from the clockwork meka Bran.

Sigewinne and the chef Cuistot help prepare the meals. The supervisor, Wolsey, sells dishes and recipes for Credit Coupons, the Fortress's currency. Its description stresses that the Welfare Meal is the one thing in the Fortress where equality need not be bought with coupons.

Places: Located in the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide, under the Court of Fontaine's justice system. Bran stands at the Welfare Meal point and Wolsey keeps the counter.

Wolsey's menu is small and priced in coupons, covering dishes such as Trout Amandine, Barbeque Ribs, Coffee Bavarois and Haggis, plus their recipes.

People: Wolsey is the supervisor and shopkeeper. Bran is a robotic meka employee, built on a harvester meka body with its Arkhe alignment disabled; it was repaired by Wolsey after being left in the abandoned Production Zone and then given a job here.

Wolsey says Welfare Meals are meant to bring surprise to monotonous lives and admits convicts have asked for better odds of a good meal; he defends giving weaker cooks a chance.

Culture: A Welfare Meal comes with a fortune slip and a random dish of variable quality, from delicious to suspicious. Bran enforces the rule strictly: only one per person per day under the cafeteria regulations.

Possible Welfare Meal dishes include Fish and Chips, Fontainian Onion Soup, Lasagna, Haggis, Steak and Trout Amandine; the dish may be delicious, normal or suspicious in quality.

Atmosphere: Institutional but oddly cheerful: a canteen queue, a deadpan robot and a gamble of a lunch.

Status as of 7.1: Operating at the cutoff (7.1).

49.content: A free daily meal from Bran in the Coupon Cafeteria, with a fortune slip. One per person per day; unused ones vanish at daily reset.

50.content:
Court of Fontaine (also: City of the Arts, Cour de Fontaine): The Court of Fontaine is the capital of Fontaine, a Belle Epoque-style city of fountains, cobbled avenues, boutiques, cafes and theatres standing high above the surrounding waters. It was once the court of the God of Justice; since the events of the Archon Quest "Masquerade of the Guilty" (4.2) it has been under Chief Justice Neuvillette, who runs the nation from the Palais Mermonia at the city's summit. The Steambird, a newspaper read across Teyvat, is based here, and the city is nicknamed the "City of the Arts".

Official text describes it as a city that "alone stands above all waters", whose people live lives as orderly and predictable as the aquabus timetable under the Palais' gaze. Beneath the elegant streets lies Fleuve Cendre, an undercity in the old sewers that the Court long left to its own devices.

Geography: The city sits in the Court of Fontaine Region on raised ground above the lake, ringed by water. Its quarters: the Palais Mermonia at the highest point; the Court Region Waterway Hub in the centre, holding the aquabus Main Station; Quartier Lyonnais, a street of shops on the northeastern side; Quartier Narbonnais on the southwestern side; Vasari Passage, shop-lined streets at the bottom of the city leading to a large fountain; and Fleuve Cendre in the sewers below. The Opera Epiclese stands offshore on the island of Erinnyes.

Mont Automnequi lies between the Court and Romaritime Harbor. Tour guide Elphane says a submerged old city of the Court lies in the nearby waters, its convoluted underwater ruins open to well-equipped explorers.

Places: - **Palais Mermonia**: the administrative heart, seat of the four Maisons and the Marechaussee Phantom, holding Neuvillette's office and Furina's former residence.
- **Court Region Waterway Hub**: the aquabus Main Station (Clementine, Navia and suspended Callas Lines); its top floor connects to the Palais.
- **Vasari Passage**: the main shopping streets and Statue Plaza, with Cafe Lutece, Damoville Purveyor (general goods), Beaumont Workshop (the blacksmith) and the Hotel Bouffes d'ete.
- **Quartier Lyonnais**: the Adventurers' Guild branch (Katheryne), Chioriya Boutique, clockmakers and Bertin's House of Curiosities.
- **Quartier Narbonnais**: The Steambird's offices, the restaurant Hotel Debord, the Salon Caritat, and the latest fashion and perfume.
- **Fleuve Cendre**: the undercity of outcasts, under the Spina di Rosula's de facto rule.

The city contains a Statue of the Seven; it and Snezhnograd are the only main cities that do. Cafe Lutece, the most popular cafe in Vasari Passage, invites patrons to discuss any topic except death. Beaumont Workshop, the most renowned forge in the city, uses fully automated forging machines instead of hammer and anvil. Leschots Clockwork Workshop (Livre, maker of clockwork toys, with Freminet commissioned for designs) and Lepaute Horlogerie (his brother Caron, a clockmaker) are rival shops. Bertin's House of Curiosities is technically a fashion workshop whose owner collects curios for inspiration. Chiori, a designer from Inazuma, runs Chioriya Boutique.

The Salon Caritat is an advocacy society that holds symposia on law, with recent topics such as the Maison Gardiennage's budget overruns and environmental pollution. A small rented rehearsal space in Vasari Passage was used by an amateur troupe staging the musical "The Little Oceanid". The Hotel Bouffes d'ete, a luxury hotel legally owned by the Harbinger Arlecchino, is the House of the Hearth's base in Fontaine, where Lyney, Lynette and Freminet live.

Governance: All of Fontaine's administration is handled at the Palais Mermonia, which Fontainians regard as essentially the highest authority in the land. It houses the Maison Ordalie (judiciary), Maison Gestion (documents and administration), Maison Cardinalice (finance) and Maison Gardiennage (law enforcement, with the Gardes and Gardemeks), plus the Melusine-staffed Marechaussee Phantom. Trials are held at the Opera Epiclese. Since Furina abdicated, Neuvillette handles the affairs that used to belong to the Archon's title, though not the title itself.

Security is tight: a person with a criminal record still flagged "Fiche S" by the Maison Gardiennage is placed under surveillance from the moment they arrive in the city, according to the aquabus guide. The Court has always known about Fleuve Cendre but historically treated it as a grey area outside its jurisdiction; today the Spina di Rosula mediates between the undercity and the Court. The Fortress of Meropide is likewise legally outside the Court's jurisdiction.

Sedene, a Melusine officer of the Marechaussee Phantom, keeps the front desk at the Palais. About four hundred years ago, after Neuvillette brought the Melusines into the city, distrust of them led to the framing and death of the Melusine Carole and to Vautrin's vengeance; four centuries later, when a Melusine named Kiara was threatened, she was kept inside the Palais Mermonia for her safety while Neuvillette investigated personally. The Court once banned unauthorised possession of certain heavy construction tools, apparently because Fleuve Cendre's residents used them as weapons.

People: Fashionable citizens, newsies and Kamera-carrying reporters, Gardes on patrol, Gestion clerks, and Melusines working at the Palais and on the aquabuses. Notable figures who live or work here: Neuvillette; Furina, now an ordinary actress; Charlotte of The Steambird; Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol; Clorinde, the Champion Duelist; Navia and the Spina di Rosula; Chiori; and the Hearth's Lyney, Lynette and Freminet.

Fleuve Cendre houses ex-convicts from Meropide seeking a fresh start, the destitute and outlaws; Chevreuse and Freminet grew up there, as did the historical Champion Duelist Marfisa. Mona writes an astrology column for The Steambird. Escoffier was head chef of the Hotel Debord before her conviction. The Court's women are reputedly beautiful, and legend says the ladies of the Court wept when the harpist Sojourner left without a farewell.

Culture: The Court is Fontaine's centre of art, fashion, cuisine and spectacle: theatre and trials at the Opera Epiclese, magic shows, cafes where people argue philosophy, boutiques and perfume, and an insatiable appetite for The Steambird's news and gossip. Hotel Debord's owner believes "art is the best seasoning for good food" and invites artists to perform while guests dine.

The Steambird runs a "Tales of Humanity" column for readers' submissions and commissions. City life also has a bureaucratic, litigious streak: one dishonest merchant once tried to trademark Neuvillette's name with two prominent lawyers, and the whole city was in uproar (as the aquabus guide tells it).

History: The Court served for centuries as the court of the Hydro Archon, the God of Justice: Egeria, then for five hundred years Focalors, whose public face was Furina. About four hundred years ago Neuvillette became Iudex and brought the Melusines into city life. In 4.2 Furina was put on trial at the Opera Epiclese; the truth of the prophecy came out, Focalors was executed by the Oratrice, the prophesied flood swept Fontaine without dissolving anyone, and the Court passed to Neuvillette's administration.

Hundreds of years ago the Court turned the city's sewers into an undercity for society's "shadows" and for labourers displaced as technology advanced, then left it largely unmanaged. Before the cataclysm, the outlaw Eduardo Baker ruled Fleuve Cendre with a protection racket until the Maison Gardiennage raided it in the "purge of Fleuve Cendre" and sentenced him to exile in the Great Red Sand; his henchmen freed him on the way, and he and his allies occupied Poisson. Centuries ago, by a tour guide's account, the Palais hired half the workers in the Court to build the Opera Epiclese, whose surplus materials piled into a small hill on the shore. The aquabus network was later built with Callas of the Spina di Rosula's funding.

Hotel Debord was founded by two chefs from Fleuve Cendre, Modeste and Savelli; its legendary Gateau Debord relied on a secret Remurian ingredient that destroyed Modeste's sense of taste and drove him to suicide, and Savelli took the blame to protect his name. The restaurant fell into disrepute and took decades to recover. In the recent past, under head chef Escoffier, a lumiline incident (secretly caused by another chef) ended with her taking responsibility and serving time in the Fortress of Meropide.

Atmosphere: Fountains everywhere, aquabuses gliding along raised water rails, the smell of fresh coffee at the station, newsies calling the latest headline, Kamera flashes, and shop windows full of clockwork and couture. Elegance above, damp and danger below: Fleuve Cendre is dirty, poorly ventilated and short on sunlight, and most residents there carry a weapon openly.

Dangers: The surface city is orderly and heavily policed; its dangers are social (scandal, lawsuits, swindlers, being dragged into a trial) rather than monstrous. Fleuve Cendre is rougher: theft is routine and violence common, although under the Spina di Rosula armed conflict is punished severely and illegal funding is harder to obtain.

Travel: Most visitors arrive by aquabus: the Clementine Line from Romaritime Harbor, or the Navia Line from Marcotte Station on Erinnyes. Melusine guides narrate the trips (Aeval on the Clementine Line, Elphane on the Navia Line). Fleuve Cendre is reached by two entrances in the city, one beside Cafe Lutece and one across the street from Damoville Purveyor. The Waterway Hub's lift also stops at a floor connected to the Palais Mermonia.

The Callas Line, once linking the Court to the Fontaine Research Institute, has been suspended since the explosion that levelled the old Institute; after foiling Romeuf's plot against the Clementine Line, Navia decided to rebuild it and add stops to the other lines.

Quests: The city is the hub of Archon Quest Chapter IV (4.0-4.2), from the Traveler's arrival and Lyney's trial through Furina's trial in "Masquerade of the Guilty". Many story, world and event quests are set here, including Navia's story quest ("Where the Roses Bloom"), Chiori's ("Stained Spots", "The Woven and the Cut") and the Fontinalia film festival events ("Roses and Muskets", 4.3; "Sunny Summer Fontinalia", 6.7).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Court of Fontaine is at peace. Fontaine has no Hydro Archon; Chief Justice Neuvillette administers the nation from the Palais Mermonia and judges trials himself now that the Oratrice no longer works. Furina has left the Palais and lives in the city as an ordinary human and actress.

Fontainians, made "true humans" by Neuvillette in 4.2, no longer dissolve in Primordial Seawater. The House of the Hearth still keeps its hotel here. The Archon Quest has since moved on to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1).

51.content:
The Palais Mermonia stands at the highest point of the Court of Fontaine and is where all of Fontaine's administrative affairs are handled; to Fontainians it is effectively the highest authority in the land. The Maison Gardiennage, Maison Gestion, Maison Cardinalice, Maison Ordalie and Marechaussee Phantom all work from here, and it holds Iudex Neuvillette's office and Furina's former residence. Even in the Archon's day, the real work was done by human and Melusine officials here.

In "Masquerade of the Guilty" the Traveler visited the Palais repeatedly, overhearing Neuvillette and Furina argue over the Poisson victims and the prophecy before Neuvillette concluded that only a trial would make her talk.

52.content:
Fleuve Cendre ("Ashen River") is a settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine, home to ex-convicts, outlaws, orphans and the poor. The Spina di Rosula is its de facto government: it mediates disputes, handles relations with the Court, gives aid and jobs, and punishes armed conflict harshly. Life there is damp, cramped and dangerous, and most residents openly carry weapons. Many Spina members live here, and it serves as the Spina's secondary base (its main base is Poisson).

The Court created the undercity centuries ago for society's "shadows" and long treated it as a lawless grey area. Before the cataclysm the outlaw Eduardo Baker ran a protection racket there with a bronze pipe, until the Maison Gardiennage's "purge of Fleuve Cendre" sent him toward exile. The Spina funds residents' futures on its own terms; it sponsored Areta's medical studies at the Akademiya on condition she return to work as the undercity's doctor. Chevreuse and Freminet grew up here.

53.content: Vasari Passage, at the bottom of the Court of Fontaine, is a set of shop-lined streets leading to a large fountain and the Statue Plaza. It holds Cafe Lutece (coffee, snacks and open philosophical debate on any subject except death), Damoville Purveyor, the automated forge Beaumont Workshop and the Hotel Bouffes d'ete. Gardes, Gestion clerks, newsies and photographers frequent it.

54.comment: Court of Fontaine: Quartier Lyonnais and Quartier Narbonnais
54.content: Quartier Lyonnais, on the city's northeastern side, is a street of shops with the Fontaine branch of the Adventurers' Guild, Chioriya Boutique, Leschots Clockwork Workshop, Lepaute Horlogerie and Bertin's House of Curiosities. Quartier Narbonnais, on the southwestern side, is the place for the newest fashion and perfume and is home to The Steambird's offices (chief editor Euphrasie), the Hotel Debord and the Salon Caritat.

55.comment: Court of Fontaine: Aquabus and the Court Region Waterway Hub
55.content:
Aquabuses run on raised aquarails from the Main Station in the Court Region Waterway Hub. The Clementine Line goes to Romaritime Harbor, the Navia Line to Marcotte Station on Erinnyes (for the Opera Epiclese), and the Callas Line to the Fontaine Research Institute, suspended "due to force majeure" since the Institute's explosion. Callas of the Spina di Rosula funded the system to improve relations between Poisson and the Court, splitting the Spina when Romeuf's faction objected; the lines bear the names of Callas, his late wife Clementine and their daughter Navia.

Before 4.2, the guides credited Indemnitium, energy that a Palais report linked to trials, with powering the aquabuses and the city. After the prophecy was resolved, Romeuf's faction plotted to collapse the Clementine Line's supports onto Poisson; Navia and the Traveler foiled it, and Navia then resolved to rebuild the Callas Line and add stops to the other lines.

56.content: Hotel Debord is a famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais whose owner, Vaneigem, holds that art is the best seasoning and invites performers to entertain diners; its interior is designed so every seat can see the stage. It was founded by Modeste and Savelli, two chefs from Fleuve Cendre, and its recipes are kept in the Codex Debord, reserved for its head chefs. Escoffier was head chef until a food-safety case sent her to the Fortress of Meropide; Savanna kept the kitchen together afterwards.

57.comment: Court of Fontaine: Furina's Trial and the Flood
57.content:
In 4.2, after Primordial Seawater erupted at Poisson, Neuvillette, the Traveler and allies lured Furina into a staged trial at the Opera Epiclese. The trial exposed that she was not a god, the Oratrice condemned "the Hydro Archon" to death, the All-Devouring Narwhal burst into the opera house, and Focalors, the real Archon hidden in the Oratrice, accepted the execution so that Neuvillette regained the Hydro Dragon's authority and absolved Fontaine's people. When the prophesied flood came, no one dissolved, and Wriothesley's ship the Wingalet rescued people caught in the water. Afterwards The Steambird printed free copies to calm the city, and Furina left the Palais and the Opera.

In the days before the trial, Paimon asked the Court's people what they would do if the flood came: Sedene, at Hotel Debord, said she would keep her routine, and Charlotte said she would stay and keep reporting. A small riot broke out at the Opera Epiclese when audience members accused Furina of ignoring the "prophecy crisis".

58.comment: Court of Fontaine: Fontinalia Film Festival in the Court
58.content: The Fontinalia Festival honours the Lochknights' search for the Oceanids; Furina turned it into a carnival where children shout "Trial or treat!" for candy. During the 4.3 event "Roses and Muskets" the Fontaine Film Association added the Fontinalia Film Festival, whose top prize is the "Furina Award", and The Two Musketeers (produced by Xavier, directed by Furina) won the first one. The name was never changed after her abdication. At a later festival (Sunny Summer Fontinalia, 6.7) the award went to "Great Detective Hurlock", directed by Lepine-Pauline and starring Charlotte, over Furina's "A Homecoming", starring Columbina; new awards for directing, costume design and Kamera work were added.

59.content:
Court of Fontaine Region (also: Court Region): The Court of Fontaine Region is the central map area of Fontaine. It holds the capital, the Court of Fontaine, where justice is a public spectacle; the open waters of Salacia Plain; the sunken Institute of Natural Philosophy; the hidden Annapausis; and the Opera Epiclese courthouse on the island of Erinnyes.

Much of Fontaine's Archon Quest is set around the capital and the Opera, and a lift behind the Opera leads down to River Talionis and the Fortress of Meropide.

Geography: The region is both a city and an expanse of sea. The capital stands above the water; Salacia Plain is a calm open sea with clear water; the sunken Institute of Natural Philosophy lies beneath it. Erinnyes is an island carrying the Opera Epiclese, the Fountain of Lucine and Marcotte Station.

Salacia Plain is described officially as a calm and serene stretch of open sea whose scintillating surface hides memories and secrets. A mysterious power from a statue there lets the Traveler move freely in the water, swimming with Angelic Sea Hares and hearing Blubberbeasts.

Places: - **Court of Fontaine**: the capital (its own entry). Districts and sites tagged to it include Quartier Lyonnais, Quartier Narbonnais, Vasari Passage, Fleuve Cendre, the Palais Mermonia, Café Lutece, Hotel Debord, Hotel Bouffes d'ete, the Steambird newspaper, Lepaute Horlogerie and Leschots Clockwork Workshop.
- **Opera Epiclese**: a vast opera house used as Fontaine's main courthouse, on the island of Erinnyes. Besides trials it hosts performances such as magic shows.
- **Institute of Natural Philosophy**: a dilapidated underwater research facility, once the base of a group led by Director Dwight Lasker.
- **Annapausis**: a location unlocked during the quest The Narzissenkreuz Adventure; its viewpoint is titled 'Narzissenkreuz Kingdom'.
- **Salacia Plain**: a calm stretch of open, crystal-clear sea.

- **Fountain of Lucine**: on Erinnyes; newlyweds still toss coins into it to wish for peaceful, happy lives.
- **River Talionis**: the waterway reached by the lift behind the Opera, leading to the Fortress of Meropide.
- **Thalatta Submarine Canyon**, **Alain Guillotin's Resting Place**, **Marcotte Station** and the **Court Region Waterway Hub** (an aquabus station) are other marked sites.

People: The capital's people include Neuvillette, the Iudex who presides over trials; other judges from the Palais Mermonia; members of the Gardes; Opera staff; and ordinary Fontainians and Melusines. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, met at the location of the same name, features in the world quest series In the Wake of Narcissus.

The Opera has a receptionist and a few named staff. Performers such as Lyney give magic shows there. In the quest An Overnight Fantasyland, Charlotte explains that cases can be assigned to judges other than Neuvillette.

Governance: The Opera Epiclese is the symbol of Fontaine's trials and judgment. The Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale sits behind the stage below the judge's seat. The Fortress of Meropide, reached from behind the Opera, is technically autonomous from Fontaine's legal system but serves as its prison.

History: Official text says the Opera has stood on Erinnyes since the first diluvian period, as a symbol of the new era's commitment to the rule of law. The Institute of Natural Philosophy holds precursors of modern Fontainian technology and the earliest experiments of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo; its ancient logs and notes include natural-history excerpts about Oceanids and Egeria.

An investigative report in the Institute records suspicion of group activity among its leaders around a so-called 'Master', with no evidence yet of aggression. Natural-history excerpts there retell the legend of Egeria's first tear and the first Oceanid.

The excerpts' author concedes the text may be thought unscientific, and notes that sceptics place the Oceanids' origin before Egeria and the realm of Remuria. The text says Oceanids were charged with understanding every form of life; those too unsuited to the continent's water systems stay in Fontaine to soothe human emotions. It adds that Oceanids multiply without pairing: after gaining enough understanding and emotion, one asks the Hydro Archon or an elder for permission to claim an abstract 'thing' and divides into little Oceanids.

Atmosphere: Theatrical: the Opera's official blurb says the true and the fantastical, the comedic and the tragic, find a stage there equally. Salacia Plain is calm and clear, and the sunken Institute is a dilapidated underwater ruin.

Dangers: The sunken Institute's enemies include Hydro Slimes, Area Alert Mek - Ousia, Armored and Sternshield Crabs, Hunter's Rays, a Ruin Guard at the entrance to its last room and a Thundercraven Rifthound Whelp.

Travel: The Court Region Waterway Hub is a marked aquabus site. Underwater exploration features here include Pneumousia Blocks and Relays, Accelerated Aquaring, Currents and High-Pressure Water Vents. Annapausis is unmarked on the map until The Narzissenkreuz Adventure; the Institute is opened by the quest Aqueous Tidemarks.

Quests: A Tea Party Most Thorny (Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act III, 4.1) is set in this region and ends with the Opera's rear lift opening to the Fortress of Meropide. World-quest series anchored here include The Narzissenkreuz Adventure, Ann's Story, Aqueous Tidemarks, the Toy War quests, Their Childhood and In the Wake of Narcissus, whose first part, Search in the Algae Sea, starts at the Ordo.

The region also hosts many commissions, anecdotes and the Tea Party Re-Invitation quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Court of Fontaine Region is intact and in everyday use.

Annapausis and the Institute of Natural Philosophy remain explorable, and the Opera remains the nation's courthouse.

60.comment: Court of Fontaine Region: Opera Epiclese
60.content:
A large opera house on Erinnyes that doubles as Fontaine's main courthouse. Trials are staged there; the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale sits below the judge's seat. A lift behind the building goes down to River Talionis and the Fortress of Meropide.

Neuvillette presides at the judge's seat, but other judges from the Palais Mermonia can be assigned. The building also hosts shows by performers such as Lyney.

61.comment: Court of Fontaine Region: Institute of Natural Philosophy
61.content:
A sunken research facility that once belonged to an organisation of the same name led by Director Dwight Lasker. Its ruined halls keep early forms of Fontainian technology and the first experiments of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The Traveler first explores it in Aqueous Tidemarks while chasing a treasure promised by an overenthusiastic Fontainian.

Its logs include a natural-history text with a legend of Egeria's tears and the first Oceanid, and an investigative report on a suspected 'Master'.

62.content: Annapausis is unlocked in The Narzissenkreuz Adventure and is not labelled on the map before that. A viewpoint calls it the 'Narzissenkreuz Kingdom'. A fountain southwest of the castle stands by a statue of Princess Lyris.

key: Court of Fontaine Aquabus Main Station
63.content:
Court Region Waterway Hub (also: Court of Fontaine Aquabus Main Station, Aquabus Main Station): The Court Region Waterway Hub is the aquabus main station in the centre of the Court of Fontaine. It serves the Clementine Line to Romaritime Harbor, the Navia Line to the Opera Epiclese and Marcotte Station, and the Callas Line to the Fontaine Research Institute.

The Callas Line is suspended indefinitely according to the station notice, so only the other two lines run for travellers.

Places: The hub has several floors: the main hall on the ground floor, the Clementine Line platform on 2F, the Navia Line on 3F and Palais Mermonia on 4F. An information clerk and a maintenance worker staff the main hall.

A notice board near the 2F elevator lists the lines. The Navia Line terminus is Marcotte Station, in the Erinnyes area.

People: Named staff include the information clerk Sylvie, maintenance worker Pruniere and guide Grosley; Esteban, a stenographer, is on the Palais Mermonia floor. Melusine guides narrate the ride.

History: The system was built under Callas, father of Navia, with the Court and the Research Institute, to improve relations between the Court and Poisson; the lines carry the names Clementine (his late wife), Navia and Callas. The Callas Line was lost when an explosion struck the Research Institute.

After the Prophecy of Fontaine, a plot by Romeuf's faction against the Clementine Line was foiled by the Traveler and Navia, who then resolved to rebuild the Callas Line and add stops.

Travel: Riders call an aquabus from the bench if none waits. The Clementine Line goes to Romaritime Harbor and the Navia Line to Marcotte Station.

Status as of 7.1: Active at the cutoff (7.1) with two lines running.

64.content:
Damoville Purveyor: Damoville Purveyor is a general goods shop in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine, run by Boucicaut.

Its supplies restock daily. Players who reach Reputation Rank 4 in Fontaine gain a permanent 10 percent discount here (a gameplay benefit).

Places: The shop is in the Vasari Passage, the same district of the Court of Fontaine as Beaumont Workshop.

It is classed as a general goods shop rather than a specialist one.

People: Boucicaut is the only named person. Canon gives no personal history for him.

Atmosphere: A plain general store for picking up supplies.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

The wiki suggests the shop's name may allude to a historical dressmaker to French royalty; treat this as an etymology guess only.

65.content:
Denouement of Sin: Denouement of Sin is a Domain of Blessing in the Belleau Region of Fontaine, near Romaritime Harbor. In the domain text it is a remote, deserted valley where legend says the first Lochknight hid among the Lochfolk, training harshly in an attempt to atone for a sin beyond redemption. Now only cold wind blows and clockwork meka left without orders still patrol.

Clearing it yields artifacts: Marechaussee Hunter, Golden Troupe, Resolution of Sojourner and Defender's Will.

Geography: A hollow among caverns on the shore of a lake, set in a deserted valley with long chill winds. It lies in the Belleau Region, with Romaritime Harbor as its sub-area.

Its description says the caverns around the lakeshore became home to the escaped constructs after the accident at the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering.

Dangers: Ousia-aligned clockwork meka, runaway constructs of the types called Recon Log, Arithmetic Enhancer, Suppression Specialist, Construction Specialist, Geological Survey and Annihilation Specialist meks.

In-game, the domain's Ley Line Disorder boosts the party's CRIT DMG whenever a character gains or loses HP, so healers help; this is a game mechanic and not part of the story.

Clearing level IV is recommended at around level 90 characters per the wiki; four tiers of difficulty exist (recommended levels 59, 69, 80 and 90). Rewards include artifacts from the sets above only; none are unique to this domain's story.

Atmosphere: Still and lonely: a land that has "returned to deathly silence", with cold wind blowing through an empty valley and constructs waiting for orders that will never come.

History: Fontaine lore as hinted by the domain text: the first Lochknight chose exile among the Lochfolk, seeking penance through training. Nothing more is given about when or why.

The meka were abandoned after the Research Institute accident. Canon identifies this domain only through that text.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as a permanent artifact domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

66.content:
Domus Aurea (also: The Domus Aurea, Golden Palace of Remuria, royal palace of Remuria): Domus Aurea ("Golden House") was the royal palace of the kingdom of Remuria. King Remus, the Sebastos and God King, had it made from his ship Fortuna and designed it as a giant instrument on which the Grand Symphony, Phobos, could be played. It is the "heart" of Phobos and is protected by that power. It lies on the hill of Clivus Capitolinus in Capitolium, deep in the Sea of Bygone Eras, and looks strangely well preserved for something thousands of years sunk.

In Version 4.6 the Traveler and Paimon fight their way in with Scylla and Cassiodor to stop the Remurian Harmost Boethius, who had used Phobos to steal the souls of the people of Petrichor. The palace was the place where Phobos was finally destroyed.

Geography: Seen from outside, the palace resembles a giant harp, with pipes extending outwards that once broadcast the symphony to the four corners of Remuria. Inside it feels less like a palace than the guts of an enormous machine. Its main levels are a lower level and an upper level; the upper level holds the throne room, the Sacellum Requietis, and a podium with the great harp.

Golden aqueducts (the Alta Semita) once carried the will of Phobos through Remuria; they lie broken and have to be rebuilt before the gates open. The old book History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria describes a golden palace of towering copper pillars at the heart of Capitolium, with the king resting in its centre and hearing every note of the empire.

Places: Gates of Domus Aurea: they open only when the broken golden aqueducts are reconnected and the old symphony is played, matching what the score said.
Central chamber: where Boethius made his stand.
Sacellum Requietis: the throne room on the upper level.
The podium and harp: where the final Requiem is played.

Murals painted with the power of the symphony, like those in the Faded Castle, stand near the Alta Semita on the approach. A viewpoint here, "The End of An Ancient Dream", quotes Remus's last line about a dream where mortals had free will.

People: Remus ruled here and is known by titles such as Sebastos, God King and Imperator. Boethius and Cassiodor were two of his four Harmosts. Scylla, the Prince of Vishaps, was Remus's friend and the one to whom he entrusted his final plan. The Traveler can only see Remus in memories.

History: Remus took Sybilla's wisdom and his own power to make Phobos, which would let humanity take charge of its own fate against the prophesied destruction. The palace was its stage. Phobos took on a will built from the worst desires of the ascended Remurians, who had put their souls into immortal golem bodies, and it led them into war on the other peoples of Fontaine. Remus tried to end it with a secret Requiem, a self-destruct order for the symphony, to be carried out with Scylla; Scylla was lured into a trap and sealed, and the Requiem sank Remuria in a flood.

Millennia later, Boethius, whose soul was bound to the shattered Phobos, awakened it and invited Cassiodor to Domus Aurea to take part in a ritual to "take on flesh", a new body for himself as a new Sebastos and a new power over the world. His plan was to gather every will scattered through the waters.

Cassiodor appeared to agree, joined Phobos, and betrayed Boethius from within, trapping Boethius and the symphony in one body. Phobos then spoke for itself, claimed to be the sum of every Remurian wish, and said it had devoured Boethius. Cassiodor asked the Traveler to destroy him together with Phobos, and he faded. The Traveler then rode a lift to the podium and played the final Requiem on the harp, sending the freed souls to the sea. Scylla later left to roam the waters.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet after the Requiem. Phobos is gone for good, the souls it held have left, and the people of Petrichor are back to normal.

The palace still stands. Two viewpoints, one of them titled "Domus Requiem", become available after the story, and a soundtrack that reuses the Requiem motif plays at the harp.

Atmosphere: Gold, machinery and a slow echo of music: choral swells, humming pipes and water moving through ancient channels. The air feels like something that has only just stopped playing. Where the old music was warm, the corridors now carry a bruised, mournful note.

67.comment: Domus Aurea: Golden Aqueducts and the Gates of Domus Aurea
67.content: In Remuria the will of Phobos flowed along golden aqueducts into every corner of the empire. In Gradus ad Capitolium Scylla tells the Traveler that rebuilding the broken section before the palace will open its gates. They collect lost fragments of the symphony in the area, restore the paths, release stored Ichor, and play the symphony together; the gates swing open.

68.comment: Domus Aurea: Boethius's Ritual in Domus Aurea
68.content: Boethius claims the palace lets him affect the present world directly because it is so close to the heart of Phobos, and Cassiodor fears that if the ritual succeeded, Boethius could pull the whole surface into his delusions and revert Fontaine to its ancient appearance. In the fight he appears in three forms: as a statue named "The Immortal Sebastos's Second Coming", as the "Bleeding Idol", and as Phobos, "Discordant Symphony". He rejects the people of Fontaine as inferior and sees the souls he trapped as a tool for Remuria's return.

69.content: Remus's Requiem was the self-destruct order of the Grand Symphony. In his original plan he would unleash it with his own life, while Scylla controlled the unleashed primordial power in the palace and turned the Remurians back into flesh-and-blood people. Scylla's seal ruined the plan. In the present, Scylla's Ichor body still holds the Requiem; the Traveler plays it on the harp and the current of freed souls rises towards the surface, led by a golden bee.

70.content:
Dryas Wood (also: Dryas Pine Forest): Dryas Wood is a small hollow in Fontaine between the Fontaine Research Institute and Erinnyes Forest. It used to be the Institute's "backyard", where plant nurseries stood, and it is said that the potioneer who devised the "Pure Water" formula once lived here in seclusion. It is now abandoned.

Its main role in canon is as the setting of the world quest Villains (4.1), in which a girl named Blanche searches the hollow for her brother, who picked up the Pure Water formula in the wilderness after the Institute's explosion. The visitors find an old cabin that speaks.

Geography: A small, sheltered hollow nestled between the old Fontaine Research Institute site and the edge of Erinnyes Forest. Rainbow Rose grows here as a local specialty.

A potioneer's cabin stands in the hollow. Nothing remains of the nurseries that once filled it, and the place looks long unused.

History: The hollow served as the Institute's backyard and held assorted plant nurseries. After the Institute's explosion, many things were scattered across the wilderness, which is how Blanche's brother came by the Pure Water formula.

Tradition names a talented but withdrawn potion and alchemy prodigy at the Institute, sidelined because the Institute's focus lay elsewhere, who moved into seclusion in the mountains and invented several remarkable potions. That tale is told by an antagonist in the quest and is framed as legend. The potioneer is never named.

In the quest the cabin itself claims that its previous occupant received Pure Water as a reward from a "World of Purity" and grew special fruit with it; the Traveler's party treats this as a falsehood. The legend told later is of discarded potions forming a pond from which a small flower grew, which some say was the Hydro Archon's doing. Treat both versions as unverified stories.

Atmosphere: Quiet, overgrown and forgotten: a secluded hideaway close to ruined research grounds, with an empty cabin and no sign of the nurseries.

Quests: Villains (World Quest, 4.1, Fontaine Research Institute region) takes place here. Its reward includes the Pure Water formula.

Characters in the quest include Blanche and the Fruity Order operatives who go by fruit and flower code names ("Guileless Wolfhook", "Ruthless Calla Lily", "Trendy Zaytun Peach", "Tricky Bulle Fruit"). Do not add detail beyond what the quest shows.

Travel: Lies between the Institute region and the edge of Erinnyes Forest.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned as of 7.1; no change is recorded since its introduction in 4.1.

71.content: "Pure Water" is a potion formula credited to a potioneer of the Fontaine Research Institute who is said to have lived in seclusion at Dryas Wood. Copies were scattered after the Institute exploded; in the quest Villains the formula is deciphered and treated as the Institute's inheritance, to be sent to the new Fontaine Research Institute. The quest also notes the potion sells well in the Fortress of Meropide.

72.content:
East Slopes of Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnequi East): The East Slopes of Mont Automnequi are the eastern side of Mont Automnequi, a mountain in Fontaine that spans two regions. This half belongs to the Morte Region; the western half is in the Belleau Region. It was added in Version 4.2.

The area is where the world quest "Cupid's Lover" begins, part of the Narcissus chain, "In the Wake of Narcissus".

Geography: Mont Automnequi is described as a mountain spanning the Belleau and Morte Regions. The East Slopes are the Morte-side subarea, with the West Slopes as the Belleau-side counterpart. The name probably comes from the French words for autumn and equinox (the wiki's inference on the West Slopes page). The wiki gives no official description of the east side's terrain.

Places: The Orthant of Souls is a set of mysterious ruins reached in "Cupid's Lover". A stone riddle slate marks it, and a seal must be found first. Inside, the Traveler descends to a lower floor by lift and works through Energy Flow devices, an underwater chamber and Xenochromatic Jellyfish that trigger mechanisms. Recon Log Meks and Geological Survey Meks guard it. Solving the puzzle yields a "Soul" piece.

The slate's text calls the place the Orthant of Souls, the Shrine of Souls and the Room of Souls, with lines about accompanying someone in eternal rest. A 4-star weapon, Nymph's Constancy, can be picked up beside the slate. Part of the ruin floods or drains when Energy Flow is released, turning the surrounding area into dry land.

The quest has two versions depending on whether the Traveler began "Search in the Algae Sea" first, and it runs concurrently with the quests "Meteoric Lance" and "Muse's Mother" before leading to "Thalia and Melpomene". The wider Narcissus chain's plot is not resolved in this entry.

Quests: "Cupid's Lover" (4.2) belongs to "Search in the Algae Sea" within "In the Wake of Narcissus". Paimon and the Traveler find signs that someone else got there first, such as a pocket watch on the ground, and the slate names the place the Orthant of Souls. Ann, Seymour and a caterpillar are listed among the quest's characters. The wider plot belongs to the quest's own entry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an accessible slope with its ruin and quest content unchanged.

73.content:
Echoes of the Deep Tides: Echoes of the Deep Tides is a weapon-material domain of underwater caves in the Court of Fontaine Region. Bandits and smugglers use the caves, beyond the Maison Gardiennage patrol routes, as hideouts, and have stolen clockwork meka. Its flavor text recalls a God King who dreamed of an empire of harmonious music above the waves, whose pride sank with him.

Clearing it gives weapon ascension materials (the Robotic Ruse, Artisanship and Curious Contraptions sets) at the Court of Fontaine Region.

Geography: Cave systems beneath the waves of the Court of Fontaine Region, remote from regular guard patrols.

The flavor text hints at a ruin from Remuria: an old hall whose golden melodies are silent and echo only with the cold music of the tides.

History: The domain's legend speaks of a time before the Sovereign of the Waters had returned from confinement, when another God King dreamed of building a prosperous musical empire on the waves, which failed through human arrogance.

The text does not name the places or people involved; the Remuria and Egeria links are readers' connections to the God King and Sovereign mentioned.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders (Scouts and Hydro Potioneers), Fatui agents (Pyro Agent, Electro Cicin Mage) and Pneuma-aligned clockwork meka.

The domain has four difficulty tiers (recommended levels 15, 36, 59 and 80). Its Ley Line Disorder gives a Hydro DMG bonus after Hydro-related reactions, a game mechanic. Weekday rewards rotate between the three material series named above.

Atmosphere: Damp, echoing caves with the ring of lost music and the clutter of an underworld hideout.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent weapon domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

74.content:
Elton Trench (also: Graveyard of Ships): Elton Trench is a deep underwater trench in Fontaine, in the Beryl Region between the beast-mountain of Elynas and Mont Automnequi. It is the final resting place of the old Fontaine Navy, which sank here fighting the great beast Elynas about 500 years ago. Its water is oddly bright, so divers misjudge its depth, yet the shipwrecks littering its bottom warn them off; local legends call the nearby waters haunted, which also makes it a good hiding place for anyone who wants secrecy.

The trench is probably named for Admiral Basil Elton, who led that last voyage in the white ironclad flagship Sponsian. It is part of the Beryl Region's map level "Source of All Waters: The Great Fontaine Lake".

Geography: An underwater subarea of the Beryl Region, lying between the surface remains of Elynas to the north and the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi. The water is bright for its depth. The wrecks of the Navy's fleet are scattered along the trench, which a Fontaine viewpoint text (as cited on the Sponsian page) calls the "Graveyard of Ships". Nearby, on a beach by Mont Automnequi's western slopes, one half of the Sponsian lies wrecked on shore.

Underwater, features include Pneumousia Blocks and Relays, Accelerated Aquaring and Recovery Orbs, and Xenochromatic creatures; local specialties are Beryl Conch and Romaritime Flower. A ghostly apparition of the Sponsian's front half is seen around the trench and Salacia Plain.

History: About 500 years ago, during the cataclysm, the great beast Elynas appeared and fouled Fontaine's land and waters. Fontaine's Armada, with the repaired Sponsian at its head and Admiral Basil Elton aboard, set out in what would be its last battle. The fleet pursued Elynas for roughly 35 days, drawing monsters from the Abyss, and the ship was split in half in the final charge. The rest of the fleet also sank, and the remains are strewn across the trench.

A damaged diary recovered from the wreckage records the chase day by day: ruins where Elynas had passed, a trail of blood, a battered ship drifting wherever winds and currents took it, and a last fragment reading "Fontaine expects that everyone will do their duty". After the battle the Navy ceased to exist. Basil's First Mate, Nathaniel Pickman, spent years pressing the Court of Fontaine to salvage and rebuild the Sponsian; the families of the fallen suspected he was merely fishing for glory. Later stage plays reconstructed the final battle from Pickman's records.

The Navy's flagship was the pride of an age when armoured warships with heavy cannons and ramming prows were the darlings of the Court of Fontaine. The one keepsake left of the Admiral is her blue and white sword, remembered in the weapon Tidal Shadow, a standard-model officer's blade forged for the Navy's flagship captains. Elynas itself, bleeding from unexplained wounds, eventually died; its colossal remains became the mountains of the Beryl Region and the cradle of the Melusines.

Atmosphere: Dim, pale water with a deceptive glow, broken masts and hulls looming out of the murk, a sense of a crowd that never left. Divers feel alarm bells go off once the wrecks come into view. Ghostly legends hang over the surrounding waters.

Dangers: Armored Crabs, Sternshield Crabs, Blubberbeasts, and Underwater Patrol and Survey Meks patrol the trench. The Abyssal monsters that harried the fleet are long gone, but the wreck-strewn depths are still easy to misjudge.

Travel: Reached by diving from the Beryl Region shore near the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi or from Salacia Plain. The depth is easy to underestimate because of the light.

Quests: The trench has no quests of its own. In the world quest The Lone Phantom Sail the Melusine Ahes, a self-styled Sponsian archaeologist, uses an old military conch to call the ghostly half-ship and leads the Traveler and Paimon from Salacia Plain along the clues to the wreck on the shore.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the trench is a silent graveyard; no recent event has changed it.

Ahes visits the beach wreck daily, and the Sponsian's captain has entrusted the wreckage to her. She means to restore the ship's logbook and piece Basil's story together.

75.comment: Elton Trench: The Sponsian and the Fontaine Armada
75.content:
The Sponsian was the white ironclad flagship of Fontaine's Navy, an armoured warship with heavy cannons and a ramming prow. Its name came from the First Mate, Nathaniel Pickman, who suggested the name of a usurper; Basil Elton first called it awful and then adopted it, saying she liked the "unreal reality" of it. In the last battle it was split in half: one half lies on the shore near Mont Automnequi, and the Traveler speculates the other was swallowed by Elynas. Of the crew, only Basil, Pickman, the Chief Engineer and volunteers stayed to the end; the Second Mate had taken many crew home. A machine aboard read zero chance of survival. All their fates are dead, missing or unknown.

Wreckage is also scattered as ballast, crates and a smashed lifeboat along the coast, signs that the ship dumped weight in an emergency manoeuvre to rise from danger. The crew spoke of "boys and girls", which the quest suggests may have been an affectionate nickname.

76.comment: Elton Trench: Ahes and the Phantom Sail
76.content: Ahes is a Melusine who studies the Sponsian's wreck. She learned from another Melusine, Verenata, that the Traveler had glimpsed the ghost ship while under the effect of a "Truesight Potion". With an old military communications conch found in a sunken wreck, she sends tuned signals that make the phantom front half of the ship appear. At the end of the trail, the Traveler recounts Basil's last moments and hears her voice, described as sorrowful, and Ahes wins the captain's recognition as keeper of the wreckage. Ahes's claim that the ship responds like a whale to song is her own belief.

77.content:
Erinnyes Forest: Erinnyes Forest is a green, lake-filled area on the island of Erinnyes in Fontaine. Its landmarks are the Weeping Willow of the Lake, the Roots of Erinnyes (the water veins whose centre is called Hauteclaire), the lake Loch Urania and Lumidouce Harbor, a port built on a waterfall. The world-quest series The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes deals with cleansing its polluted waters.

It is the same island as the Opera Epiclese, the Fountain of Lucine and Marcotte Station. Official text says the Fontaine Research Institute's ruins lie on the north side of the island, and the depths of Erinnyes are considered ill-advised to explore by Neuvillette.

Geography: Forest and lakes make up the region. A large willow tree grows at the centre of a lake, its roots reaching down into the water. Beneath the forest lie caverns and water veins, many connecting to the willow, collectively the Roots of Erinnyes. Lumidouce Harbor clings to the side of a waterfall, in the same fashion as Romaritime Harbor.

Dryas Wood, a small hollow between the Institute region and this forest, once served as the Institute's 'backyard' with plant nurseries.

The forest's notable items are the Foggy Forest Branch and the Drained Conch Cup; its local specialties are Lakelight Lily, Lumidouce Bell, Rainbow Rose and Romaritime Flower. Urville appears in Lumidouce Harbor by day after the Morte quest Wish-Fulfilling Treasure Hunt.

Places: - **Weeping Willow of the Lake**: the big willow at the lake's centre; its health is tied to the water veins. Before the veins are cleansed the lake looks sickly yellow; afterwards it turns bright blue.
- **Roots of Erinnyes**: subterranean caverns and water veins, serving as an information system whose central part is called Hauteclaire.
- **Loch Urania**: a lake with a large water vortex that forms a bubble at the top; tainted by Contaminated Bacterial Mats until cleansed.
- **Lumidouce Harbor**: a coastal elevator and lookout on a waterfall; a vital trading port.
- **Foggy Forest Path**, **Freminet's Temporary Camp** and a place called The Rusty Rudder are also marked.

Lumidouce Harbor handles a large volume of international trade, including tea from Qiaoying Village and spices from Sumeru. Named NPCs include Cassigneul, Kimpel, Chourei and Xing Cheng; a few, such as Chaussivert, Fusilier and Lemarcq, appear only after the quest An Expected Lie.

People: Lumidouce Harbor has a dozen or so named NPCs. Pahsiv, a Melusine, appears in the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quests. Freminet has a temporary camp marked here.

Culture: The harbour is a trading port, linked through tea from Qiaoying Village and spices from Sumeru. The forest's own folklore concerns the water veins and a Local Legend, Mageblade Corrouge, who can be found in the Roots after the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quests.

Atmosphere: Foggy paths, lakes and a great willow. Before cleansing, the lake and willow look sick and Loch Urania produces high winds and a dark sky even by day; afterwards the winds die and the sky clears.

Reed pipes sound when dew bubbles pop, and jellyfish-shaped devices carry visitors upward.

Dangers: Common enemies are hilichurls, slimes, Clockwork Meka, a Pyro Whopperflower and treasure hoarders; elites include Lawachurls, Hydro Hilichurl Rogues, a Blazing Axe Mitachurl and a Hydro Abyss Mage. Contaminated Bacterial Mats and autocannons are environmental hazards.

Travel: Lumidouce Harbor is the island's trading port, and Marcotte Station is also on the island. Exploration puzzles use the Xenochromatic Ball Octopus to clear mats, disable cannons, push Dew Bubbles and open floating crystal flowers.

Quests: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes is a world-quest series: Foggy Forest Path, Wilting Weeping Willow, Furious Mouth of the Spring and Within the Depths of Erinnyes. Furious Mouth of the Spring starts at Loch Urania and includes a fight with an enraged vishap. Other quests listed here include Flower, Feathers, and Bullets, Free Verse, Impromptu Poem of the Crimson Dawn, Miraculous Crown, Prince's Country, Sightlines and Camera Tricks and Neuvillette: Standing in the Rain.

Foggy Forest Path, Wilting Weeping Willow and Furious Mouth of the Spring run concurrently; the latter two each have three versions depending on how many Teardrop Keys the player holds.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the willow and lake are healthy again after the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quests.

Nothing newer than 4.2 was found for this forest.

78.comment: Erinnyes Forest: Roots of Erinnyes and Hauteclaire
78.content:
The Roots of Erinnyes are subterranean caverns and water veins whose waters serve as an information system. The centre is called Hauteclaire. Many veins connect to the Weeping Willow of the Lake.

Neuvillette considers exploration of the depths of Erinnyes ill-advised.

After the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quests, the Local Legend Mageblade Corrouge, a Hat Jellyfish, can be found in the Roots.

79.content: A coastal elevator and lookout built on a waterfall like Romaritime Harbor. It is a vital trading port for Fontaine, handling tea from Qiaoying Village and spices from Sumeru.

80.content:
Faded Castle (also: The Faded Castle, golden castellum): The Faded Castle is a sunken ruin in the Nostoi Region that was once part of ancient Remuria. The Harmosts and scholars of Remuria lived there, maintaining archives and researching music theory and fate. The castle holds the portal to the Sea of Bygone Eras, an even deeper region where the main Remurian ruins lie. The Traveler first enters it during the 4.6 World Quest The Shadow Over Petrichor.

In Cassiodor's words it was the "golden castellum", where he and many companions recorded old plays, music scores and every story, real or imagined, in the hope of using them to master fate. Later the castle became the base of Boethius's Golden Troupe. Cassiodor, who sealed it to protect Fontaine, is the one who lets the Traveler in.

Geography: The castle has several levels: an upper level, a middle level, a lower level with a pool, and an exhibition hall. Paintings of Domus Aurea hang in the middle level. Stages and murals use the power of the symphony, and the way into the Sea of Bygone Eras is a portal in the castle.

Hidden rooms lie behind Mysterious Bookshelves full of grimoires, which are activated with melodies from the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box. A library on the middle level and a mural stage play a role in Underwater Nocturne.

Places: Library and bookshelves: grimoires infused with the symphony's power.
Mural stage: a score-shaped mural that must be played with a blank score; this releases Boethius's shadow.
Lower-level pool: next to a bookshelf hiding the Harmost's Notes.
Higher level: where the Vicarius's report is kept.
Portal: leads down to the Sea of Bygone Eras.

People: The Harmosts, including Cassiodor, lived and worked here. The cat Osse is Cassiodor's spirit, speaking from the present. Boethius appears as a shadow rising from the mural. Praetorian Golems guard it.

History: In Remuria's golden age the Harmosts kept records of plays, scores and stories here. After the empire fell, Boethius gathered the survivors of Remuria into the castle as the Golden Troupe to resurrect the dead empire. Cassiodor opposed him, because the plan meant destroying the new nation of Fontaine and stealing its people's souls, and sealed the passage to the surface.

Cassiodor says he and his colleagues lived here when a new nation had just been born and "the possibilities were yet endless", organising the classics and researching music theory and magic to tame its perilous power. Item text for the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, as cited on the wiki, says Boethius's survivors gathered here to research reviving the empire.

In 4.6, as Boethius reawakens Phobos, Cassiodor removes the seal and the Traveler and Paimon enter. Boethius appears from the mural, announces that he will wait in Domus Aurea, and says the souls of Petrichor's people will be released if Cassiodor stays resolute when the time comes.

Hirtius, vicarius of Legio VI Rithimi Versi, wrote a report of the northern tribes under Euergetia's authority. It describes tribes of the north as clan societies, a polis called Lugdunensis ruled by a "holy king", and Aremorica, whose former ruler Cunoricus knelt to the empire some twenty years earlier and whose current ruler Erinnyes lacks any divine gifts, in Hirtius's view. A note by Marius Servius suggests that the name Erinnyes is a mis-transcription of a title meaning "high ruler".

Quests: The Shadow Over Petrichor leads the Traveler to the castle; Underwater Nocturne is set inside it. The player collects grimoires, a blank score and performs the symphony on the mural, which produces the score Tuba Mirum.

The first quest also yields the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box and the score Locus Amoenus. Lost grimoires opened shelves with secrets; three sets of research notes under the name Ruggiero are found in the castle, with no further explanation in the sources read.

Status as of 7.1: The castle is now open. The seal is gone, and Phobos has been silenced, so the portal leads to quiet ruins.

Unsolved: its role in the Golden Troupe's history is only hinted at.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems (elite), Fontemer Aberrants, and the boss-class "Statue of Marble and Brass".

Atmosphere: Faded gold, drifting water, closed books and music that nobody is playing. It feels like a theatre waiting after the last performance.

81.content: Unsigned notes by a Harmost behind a bookshelf by the lower pool, partly based on the real treatise De institutione musica. They classify music into three kinds: Musica Mundana, the order of everything, Musica Humana, the music of mortals and gods, and Musica Instrumentalis, played by instruments. The writer links the first to Fortuna and says mortals and gods can replace the world's music with their own, and that musicless people cannot be considered human. The notes mention that Euergetia will explain astrological signs.

82.comment: Faded Castle: Investigation of the Northern Barbarians
82.content: Report by Hirtius, vicarius of Legio VI Rithimi Versi, on the tribes of the northern border, for the use of future officers. Marius Servius adds notes. It records the "Mistress of All Waters" as a label forced on diverse gods by Aremorica's leader and contains many erased pages.

key: The Fall of the Faded Castle
83.comment: Faded Castle: The Fall of the Faded Castle
83.content: Three poems in a book with this title, found in Fontaine from Version 4.2. They tell of a black ship and a dark-robed figure, a golden castle by a lake with a frightened master, and a red fog from which its guests and master fall. They read as legend rather than record, and the wiki ties the master to Boethius and the bees to Phobos.

84.content:
Faded Theater: Faded Theater is an artifact domain in Petrichor, in the Nostoi Region of Fontaine. Its flavor text says that the prophet and the ruler, heroes and fell dragons, the grand opera of the golden age once played out here; now the only players on the stage are monsters of unknown provenance.

Clearing it grants artifacts: Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy, Unfinished Reverie, Brave Heart and Scholar.

Geography: A ruined theater-stage in Petrichor within the Nostoi Region.

The text ties the place to Fontaine's golden age (the Remuria period), with the prophet (Sybilla), the ruler (Remus) and fell dragons (Scylla) as the subjects of its opera. It is the domain text that links these; no further description of the building exists.

History: Fontaine's golden-age opera, as the domain frames it, was staged here with a prophet, a ruler, heroes and dragons as characters.

Nothing explains when the stage was abandoned or how the golems came to guard it.

Dangers: Rock Shield hilichurls and Mitachurls, slimes and Pyro Shooters, with Praetorian Golems as the strongest foes.

Gameplay note: the domain's Ley Line Disorder rewards a character with an all-element and Physical DMG bonus whenever their Bond of Life rises or falls; this is a game mechanic.

There are four difficulty tiers (recommended levels 59, 69, 80 and 90); later tiers field up to three Praetorian Golems at once, and the final waves include large slimes.

Atmosphere: An empty, once-splendid stage: faded grandeur, silence, and stone guardians in place of actors.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent artifact domain as of 7.1, added in 4.6; no story events are tied to it.

85.content:
Fleuve Cendre (also: Court of Fontaine: Fleuve Cendre, Ashen River, Fleuve cendré, the undercity of Fontaine): Fleuve Cendre ("Ashen River") is the undercity of Fontaine: a damp, poorly lit settlement in the sewers beneath the Court of Fontaine. Societal outcasts live here: ex-convicts, active criminals, the destitute, orphans and manual labourers whom the surface no longer needs. The Court of Fontaine has long treated it as a grey legal area outside its jurisdiction. Today the Spina di Rosula, led by Navia, is its de facto government.

It is the home district of several well-known Fontainians: Navia, Freminet, Chevreuse and the champion duelist Marfisa are all said to have been born or raised here. Many residents served time in the Fortress of Meropide and came here for a fresh start, sometimes with their families.

Geography: A sewer-level settlement with little sunlight, poor air circulation and cramped living space; the air is dirty and damp. It lies below the Court of Fontaine and is reached from two access points in the Court: one beside Cafe Lutece on the west side and one across the street from Damoville Purveyor on the east.

The pipes and passages of the undercity are part of the geography of childhood for its residents; Navia's character story recalls her hiding in the pipes during games with the local children.

Places: L'or noir is a bar owned by the Spina di Rosula; its bartender Tetreaux also helps residents with supplies and household matters. A message board there carries local notices. There is a general goods store (Bracari) and a travelling merchant (Crossa), and a doctor, Areta.

The Spina di Rosula keeps a stronghold in Fleuve Cendre (its secondary base, with Poisson as its headquarters), and the Archon Quest scene in which the Traveler learns about Navia's father Callas takes place there.

People: Open-world residents include Areta (doctor), Bracari (store manager), Tetreaux (bartender), Lelienne, Aurele, Hugues, Lisette, Verut, Vitruvia, Faustier, Potier (seen at night) and the Spina's Consigliere. After the world quest A Fontainian Message, the Spina enforcers Luca ("The Fisherman") and Sonny ("The White Glove") appear here.

Areta's medical studies at the Akademiya were funded by the Spina on condition that she return to work in Fleuve Cendre after graduating and she was offered a salaried post; this shows how the Spina helps people while expecting loyalty in return. Notable people raised here include Navia, Freminet, Chevreuse and Marfisa.

Governance: Historically the Court of Fontaine had no real jurisdiction here. The Spina di Rosula now mediates conflicts, manages relations with the Court and keeps order. Residents say it watches everyone "like hawks"; illegal funding is harder to find, and anyone who starts an armed fight can be "sent away to start a new life in the ocean" by the Spina.

The Spina also provides practical help (supplies, household affairs, financial aid and jobs). Navia, as its second president after her father Callas, is addressed here as "Boss".

Culture: Poor but close-knit. Parents are often too busy making ends meet to watch their children, who are left to their own devices. Most people keep a weapon, often a gun, and few bother to hide it. Locals are wary of outsiders and quick to say that anything left in the open will be stolen.

Navia's birthday mail (dated 2026-08-16) mentions a party held in Fleuve Cendre, with food and drink paid for by the Spina; the mail is a light, in-world glimpse of the community's festivities.

History: Hundreds of years ago, to "improve" the city, the Court of Fontaine turned its sewers into an undercity for society's "shadows". Many manual labourers ended up here as technology reduced the demand for their work. The early inhabitants believed their diligence might win them the right to live on the surface and turn the Ashen River into somewhere as beautiful as the world above.

The Court always knew about the undercity but never managed it, and for a time it was lawless and overrun with gangs. Before the cataclysm (about 500 years ago) the outlaw Eduardo Baker became its protector and head of a protection racket, using a bronze pipe called the "Ferryman" to defeat crocodiles and enforce order; his words are quoted in the weapon's text: "Let all that the sun shines upon belong to them, and let the Fleuve Cendre belong to us."

During Eduardo's rule the Maison Gardiennage raided Fleuve Cendre in what became known as the purge of Fleuve Cendre. Eduardo and his entourage were arrested and sentenced to exile in the Great Red Sand. En route, his henchmen freed him and, with allies near Mont Automnequi, he occupied Poisson, which led to the Siege of Poisson. The Court later banned unauthorised possession of construction tools such as the Dockhand's Assistant and Prospector's Drill, which the weapon texts imply were used as hidden weapons.

Atmosphere: Dripping pipes, grey light and the constant damp. The mood is wary rather than hopeless: people share what little they have, know each other's business, and laugh in the bar. Tetreaux's line, that knowing who was killed is as easy as knowing what clothes you are wearing, sums up how normal violence feels.

Dangers: Weapons are common, theft is routine, and violence is a daily possibility. Armed conflict is discouraged and punished by the Spina, so most trouble is petty or hidden rather than open warfare.

Travel: Enter through the two access points in the Court of Fontaine (beside Cafe Lutece, and across the street from Damoville Purveyor). Fleuve Cendre has its own teleport waypoint underground.

Quests: Fleuve Cendre appears in Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act II, As Light Rain Falls Without Reason (where the Traveler visits the Spina's stronghold and learns about Callas), in the world quest A Fontainian Message (Luca and Sonny), and again when plans to trap Furina are discussed in the aftermath of the Poisson flood (Masquerade of the Guilty).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fleuve Cendre remains a poor, damp undercity under the Spina di Rosula's watch. No later canon changes its state.

The Court of Fontaine still does not manage it directly. Navia continues to lead the Spina from Poisson and the Court, and its members still run L'or noir and the local relief work.

86.comment: Fleuve Cendre: Eduardo Baker and the Purge of Fleuve Cendre
86.content:
Eduardo Baker was an outlaw leader of Fleuve Cendre before the cataclysm. He protected merchants from gangs, settled local disputes and blessed newlyweds, using a bronze pipe he called the "Ferryman". He was among those arrested in the purge of Fleuve Cendre and was being taken to exile in the desert when his henchmen freed him. The wiki adds that he ran taverns in Fleuve Cendre where the stage performers who became Parsifal the Great (and her sister Josephine) got their start. His son Jakob (later Jakob Ingold) was born there.

Eduardo's group then occupied Poisson and took Maison Gardiennage guards hostage; the reporter Karl Ingold photographed the key figures before the Siege of Poisson. Eduardo presumably died in that siege, though canon does not state his fate; the Marechaussee Hunters ended the incident.

87.comment: Fleuve Cendre: The Spina di Rosula in Fleuve Cendre
87.content: The Spina di Rosula is a citizens' organisation of Fontaine that helps ordinary people and investigates matters the Gardes will not or cannot handle. It was founded by Callas and is now led by his daughter Navia. In Fleuve Cendre it runs the bar L'or noir, a stronghold and relief services, and is the practical authority.

88.content:
Foggy Forest Path (also: Foggy Forest Path subarea): The Foggy Forest Path is a subarea in the southern part of Erinnyes Forest, by the water, where mist hangs among the trees and a glowing blue tree stands out. It is the setting of the world quest "Foggy Forest Path", part of "The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes", added in Version 4.2.

The path is hinted at by inscribed stone tablets at Marcotte Station. At its end an altar, three reed-pipe puzzles and a tree lead to a meeting with a Melusine called Pahsiv.

Geography: Located at the southern edge of Erinnyes Forest beside the water, the path is shrouded in fog. A large tree with a blue glow dominates the area, and an altar stands near it. The surrounding forest belongs to the wider Erinnyes Forest, which has its own entry.

Places: Carved stone tablets at a fountain in Marcotte Station, scratched out except for a few words mentioning "clear dew" and the Foggy Forest Path. The Mysterious Altar deeper in, whose inscription is likewise defaced and mentions "clear dew" and "three". The glowing tree, on which three orbs appear once the altar's puzzles are done.

Quests: In "Foggy Forest Path" (4.2), Paimon notices the damaged tablets at Marcotte Station and hopes for hidden treasure. The Traveler completes three Harmonious Reed Pipe puzzles in the area, which makes three orbs appear on the tree. The item on the altar proves to be a drop of water, and a Melusine speaks to them, using only the words "Pahsiv" and "Melusine". Paimon works out that "Pahsiv" means yes and "Melusine" means no, and since the Melusine likes the name, Paimon calls her Pahsiv. She also says "Erinnyes". The quest leads on to "Within the Depths of Erinnyes".

The quest has three versions depending on how many Teardrop Keys the Traveler holds. The wiki marks the first step (searching for the path after reading the tablet) as needing verification. The rest of the story belongs to the Wild Fairy of Erinnyes quest chain.

The quest begins either by reading the tablet at Marcotte Station or by completing the concurrent quests "Wilting Weeping Willow" or "Furious Mouth of the Spring". Its rewards include Primogems, Mora and Hero's Wit. Whether the drop of water is a key, a person or both is left ambiguous: Pahsiv answers "Pahsiv" when asked if it is a key and when asked if she is not a person, which Paimon can only interpret as meaning yes.

Atmosphere: Quiet, cool and damp: drifting fog, the sound of water, a blue light among dark trunks, and half-erased carvings that suggest someone wanted the place forgotten.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area is unchanged and accessible.

89.content:
Fontaine (also: Nation of Justice, Fontainian): Fontaine is the nation of Hydro and justice, a "terrestrial sea" on a raised plateau at the centre of Teyvat, said to be the source of all the continent's waters. Its capital, the Court of Fontaine, is a Belle Epoque-style city of fountains, aquabuses, clockwork meka and theatres, and Fontainians pride themselves on art, elegance and technology. Trials at the Opera Epiclese are public spectacle. Since 4.2 Fontaine has had no Archon: the Iudex Neuvillette, secretly the Hydro Dragon, runs its affairs.

The nation once worshipped the Hydro Archon (Egeria, then Focalors, whom the public knew as Furina). For five hundred years it lived under a prophecy that its people would dissolve into the sea; that crisis was resolved in the Archon Quest "Masquerade of the Guilty". Other peoples live here too, notably the Melusines, and the Oceanids once did.

Geography: The whole continental plate is elevated well above neighbouring nations and edged by a waterfall thousands of metres high.
