Areas: the Court of Fontaine Region (the capital, the island of Erinnyes with the Opera Epiclese), the Belleau and Beryl Regions (the mountain-sized remains of Elynas, with Merusea Village beneath), the Liffey Region (Fortress of Meropide offshore), the Fontaine Research Institute Region, the Morte Region and Erinnyes Forest, and in the south the Nostoi Region (Petrichor) and the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Most of Fontaine's waters can be dived and explored underwater; the Nostoi Region is the exception because it lies off the raised plate. The Sea of Bygone Eras, south of the "Great Terrestrial Lake", hides sunken Remurian ruins. Beneath everything lies the Primordial Sea, whose largest opening is sealed under the Fortress of Meropide; smaller pools exist beneath the Tower of Ipsissimus and elsewhere. Release order: Court, Belleau and Beryl (4.0); Liffey, the Research Institute area and Meropide (4.1); Morte and Erinnyes Forest (4.2); Nostoi and the Sea of Bygone Eras (4.6).

Government: The Palais Mermonia, at the highest point of the capital, is the seat of all administration and effectively the highest authority. It houses the Maisons: Ordalie (the judiciary, headed by the Chief Justice or Iudex, Neuvillette), Gestion (documents and administration), Cardinalice (financial approvals) and Gardiennage (law enforcement, with the Gardes and Gardemeks). Even when Furina reigned, the real work was done by humans and Melusines in the Palais. Since her abdication Neuvillette handles all affairs that once belonged to the Archon's title.

The Maison Gardiennage has two special branches: the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol (captain Chevreuse), which apprehends violent criminals with muskets and few rules on uniform, and the Marechaussee Phantom, an investigative force led by Neuvillette and staffed mostly by Melusines for their sharp senses. The Gardes are captained by Grosrochard. Bureaucracy is famously slow: replacing one typewriter keycap can need several rounds of approvals. Fontaine's law code holds many odd statutes; Neuvillette lists bans on releasing flying objects in the first three days of a month and on naming pets after Furina, and adds that the rule requiring Melusines to be called "she" rather than "it" was his own.

Other judges from the Palais can be assigned to preside over trials; Neuvillette does not hear every case. Champion Duelists, chosen from Fontaine's best fighters, let an accused person defend their honour by duel instead of trial; winning means acquittal, losing means standing trial, and a duel is fatal only if the accused will not yield. Clorinde is the strongest current Champion Duelist. The Fortress of Meropide is legally outside the Court's jurisdiction.

Religion: Fontaine worshipped the Hydro Archon, God of Justice: first Egeria, the "Mistress of Many Waters", and then Focalors. For five centuries the public face of the god was Furina, flamboyant and theatrical, who sat in a box at trials. There is a Statue of the Seven inside the Court of Fontaine itself; Snezhnograd is the only other main city with one. Since 4.2 there is no Hydro Archon and the throne cannot be refilled.

Faith and justice were bound together: the Oratrice turned the people's belief in justice into energy (Indemnitium). The Fontinalia Festival commemorates the legendary Lochknights' search for the Oceanids and the return of Egeria. Melusines regard Neuvillette as their ideal father, and the public has long noticed his fondness for them, but he is not worshipped.

Economy: Fontaine runs on unusual energy. For centuries the Court and Erinnyes were powered by Indemnitium from the Oratrice, while machines run on the Pneuma-Ousia Arkhe system devised by Alain Guillotin, founder of the Fontaine Research Institute. The Research Institute is a pure research body (unlike Sumeru's Akademiya it neither governs nor teaches) and produces most mechanical inventions, including the soda Fonta. The Fortress of Meropide is the largest clockwork meka factory. The aquabus network (Clementine, Navia and the disused Callas lines) was funded by Callas of the Spina di Rosula. The Steambird is read across Teyvat.

After 4.2 the Opera stopped producing Indemnitium; Neuvillette, now in full command of Pneumousia, substitutes for it, which is one reason he cannot easily leave the nation. The Research Institute is notorious at home for long-winded technicians and money trouble, and its old campus was levelled by Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment. Fontaine also exports culture: the Kamera comes from here, Xinyan says rock 'n' roll originated here, and Xingqiu's novel "A Legend of Sword" is very popular. Fontaine engineers including Xavier helped design Inazuma's Mikage Furnace.

Military: Fontaine has no standing army in the present story; order is kept by the Gardes, Gardemeks, the Special Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom. Historically it had a navy: about five hundred years ago the Fontaine Armada under former admiral Basil Elton chased the great beast Elynas for 35 days and rammed it, dying to the last crew member while mortally wounding it. The old Marechaussee Hunters, monster hunters founded by Cassiodor after Remuria's fall, survive only as family traditions; Clorinde is a successor.

History: After an ancient flood drowned the first civilisation, the god Remus founded Remuria, a musical empire ruling the waters, which sank about 2,000 years ago. Egeria then became Hydro Archon, united the surviving tribes and gave Fontaine its laws. By turning Oceanids into humans with Primordial Seawater she committed a "sin" in Celestia's eyes, and a prophecy foretold that Fontaine's people would dissolve back into the sea. Egeria died in the cataclysm 500 years ago; her successor Focalors spent five centuries on a secret plan, fulfilled in 4.2.

About 400 years ago Neuvillette became Iudex, invited by an anonymous letter from Focalors, and the Melusines, born from the remains of Elynas, entered Fontainian society. In the Archon Quest (4.0-4.2), serial disappearances, Childe's wrongful conviction, a breach at Meropide's sluice gate and a Primordial Sea surge at Poisson that killed 12 people led to Furina's trial, where the truth emerged (see the prophecy entry).

Customs: Trials are theatre: citizens buy tickets to watch prosecution, defence and twists at the Opera Epiclese, which also hosts magic shows and plays. Fontainians love newspapers, gossip, fashion, film and fine food. The Fontinalia Festival, honouring the Lochknights, once had people in costume raise golden cups and ask door to door for pure water; Furina turned it into a carnival where children shout "Trial or treat!" for candy.

Since 4.3 Fontinalia also hosts the Fontinalia Film Festival, whose top prize is still the "Furina Award" even after her abdication. Lakelight Lilies are traditionally given to people setting out on long journeys, from a legend that Egeria gave one to the last Lochknight. The Lochknights' tales are retold in plays, poems and films. The Steambird awards the La Verite Prize, Fontaine's most prestigious media honour, at the Opera Epiclese. The demonym is Fontainian.

The Steambird's "Tales of Humanity" column is where locals post commissions. The Court of Fontaine is nicknamed the "City of the Arts". Melusines value scrap mechanical parts as currency in Merusea Village. Fontaine's legal system is notoriously complicated, as even Yanfei remarks.

Foreign relations: Snezhnaya: Arlecchino's Fatui stayed in Fontaine during the crisis, nominally to help, and joined the Poisson rescue; Neuvillette later gave Arlecchino the Hydro Gnosis as a "diplomatic gift", and she negotiated a gradual withdrawal of her operatives. Sumeru: Marcotte Station is a main entry point for travellers from Sumeru; Remus came from there, and Egeria's body became the Amrita in Sumeru's desert. Natlan: the Traveler left for Natlan from Romaritime Harbor. Inazuma: designer Chiori runs a boutique in the Court.

During limited-time Lantern Rite events, Neuvillette has spent his time off in Liyue. In 7.1 Fontainians are seen abroad in Snezhnaya: Charlotte reports from Snezhnograd and Lyney and Lynette visit the Korolevskiy Theater. Mona writes an astrology column for The Steambird.

Dangers: Clockwork meka gone wild, Fatui squads, Treasure Hoarders, hilichurls, Breacher Primuses and other monsters around Elynas, Tainted Hydro Phantasms, and the Fontemer wildlife of the deep. The Fortress of Meropide's searchlights pull swimmers who wander too close into the prison. Diluted Primordial Seawater has been sold as the drug Sinthe. The Research Institute ruins still float on unstable Arkhium. Before 4.2, contact with concentrated Primordial Seawater dissolved Fontainians outright.

Atmosphere: Cobbled avenues, fountains everywhere, aquabuses gliding on elevated water rails, newsboys and Kamera flashes, fashionable crowds outside boutiques and cafes, and a theatre audience's gasp at a courtroom twist. The countryside offers misty forests, mint-scented highlands of Beryl, Melusines bustling between village and city, and always the sound of water. Poisson and Fleuve Cendre show the poorer side; Meropide is industrial, metal-walled and self-contained.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Fontaine is at peace and has no Archon. In 4.2 the real Hydro Archon, Focalors, executed herself through the Oratrice, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne; Neuvillette regained the Hydro Dragon's authority and absolved Fontainians, who no longer dissolve in Primordial Seawater. Furina abdicated and now lives as an ordinary actress and director. Neuvillette runs the nation and judges trials himself.

The Oratrice no longer works. The Hydro Gnosis went to Arlecchino, and the Fatui hold it. Under her later deal with Neuvillette, the Fatui scale back operations while former House of the Hearth members are left alone. In 6.7 the Harbinger Sandrone, revived at the Research Institute, briefly ran the Wingalet before returning to Snezhnaya; the Archon Quest is now in Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1).

Navia has decided to rebuild the Callas aquabus line. The latest Furina Award went to "Great Detective Hurlock" (starring Charlotte), beating Musketeer Pictures' "A Homecoming", directed by Furina. People dissolved before 4.2, such as the Poisson victims, were not restored.

90.comment: Fontaine: Court of Fontaine and Erinnyes
90.content:
The Court of Fontaine was the court of the God of Justice and is now under Chief Justice Neuvillette. The Palais Mermonia, at its summit, holds Neuvillette's office, the Maisons and Furina's former residence. Districts include Quartier Lyonnais, Quartier Narbonnais (The Steambird's offices), Vasari Passage and the poorer lower quarter, Fleuve Cendre. The Opera Epiclese stands on the island of Erinnyes, reached by the Navia aquabus line via Marcotte Station; a lift behind it descends towards the Fortress of Meropide.

The capital is known for beautiful maidens, boutiques and cafes, and it contains a Statue of the Seven. The Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland, an amusement park of film-themed attractions that Navia's Spina di Rosula built on Lepine-Pauline's idea, appeared with the Whirling Waltz event in 5.6.

91.comment: Fontaine: The Opera Epiclese and the Oratrice
91.content:
Fontaine's main courthouse is an opera house. Trials there are public performances with tickets, and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a giant mechanical scale behind the judge's seat, used to deliver the final verdict, which the Iudex had to honour. It also turned the audience's belief in justice into Indemnitium, powering lamps and transport in the Court and Erinnyes.

The Oratrice was built by Focalors, who hid her divinity inside it; only a fraction of the Indemnitium ever reached the city, the rest being stored to execute a god. Since 4.2 it is inert and Neuvillette passes verdicts himself. Famous trials include Lyney's (4.0), Childe's wrongful conviction for the disappearances, and Furina's own.

92.content:
An autonomous undersea stronghold off the Liffey Region that serves as Fontaine's de facto prison and largest meka factory. Convicts are technically exiles; the Court only lends some Gardes. Inmates work for Credit Coupons, which replace Mora inside. Its Administrator, "the Duke", is Wriothesley, a former inmate who took the post after the previous administrator fled the duel Wriothesley had challenged him to; Sigewinne runs the infirmary.

It was built by repentant exiles whom Egeria forgave on condition they guard her secret: an opening to the Primordial Sea, sealed behind a sluice gate in the "forbidden zone". The Coupon system began as an economic experiment by the Harbinger Pantalone with a past administrator. About 400 years ago the convicted officer Vautrin founded the Mutual Aid Society here. During the 4.1 crisis Wriothesley secretly had a great ship, the Wingalet, built as a failsafe against the prophecy; it later helped rescue people during the flood.

93.content:
Beryl, across the water from the Court, is an ancient ruin-studded range where Egeria's followers once held picnics. Liffey holds the waters around Meropide and the Research Institute region its floating ruins. Morte ("dead") Region holds the Tower of Ipsissimus, and Erinnyes Forest (4.2) is a misty woodland. Romaritime Harbor is the main port.

The Nostoi Region (4.6) lies in the south, off the raised plate; Petrichor there is an island town of pure water and Remurian golem statues, led by a "Doge" and home of filmmaker Xavier. Lumidouce Harbor is a further coastal town; an aquabus line there has been rumoured.

94.content:
Elynas was a colossal beast that brought pollution to Fontaine during the cataclysm and was mortally wounded by the Fontaine Armada; its skeleton is now a mountain ridge in the Beryl Region, with Merusea Village hidden underwater inside it. The Melusines, a small amphibious all-female species, were born from its wounds about 400 years ago. Neuvillette brought them into society, where many work in the Marechaussee Phantom; they see him as their ideal father.

Melusines perceive colours and people differently from humans, which makes their art and cooking baffling to humans, and they are long-lived; Sigewinne and Kiara are among the first born. Early on, many humans feared them: about 400 years ago the Melusine Carole, framed by hardliners, took her own life to calm a riot, and her partner Vautrin avenged her and was sent to Meropide. The Maison Gardiennage's hat emblem was later redesigned to include Melusines in her memory.

95.comment: Fontaine: Remuria and the God King
95.content:
Before Egeria, the god Remus, who came from Sumeru after Gurabad's fall, founded Remuria above Fontaine's waters, teaching farming, building and above all music. His capital was Capitolium and his emblem the golden bee. Prophesied to perish utterly and return to the Primordial Sea, Remus purged Lochfolk, vishaps and "barbarian" tribes, shared power with four Harmosts and poured his people's souls into golem bodies of stone and golden Ichor. Remuria sank anyway; its ruins lie in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Remus' Grand Symphony, Phobos, was made from the life of Sybilla, the guardian of the Golden Bees; it fed the people's desire for bloodshed. Remus secretly conspired with the dragon Scylla to destroy it, Harmost Boethius saw this as betrayal and sealed Scylla, and the empire drowned in the resulting tsunami. Resistance came from the northern tribes and the Lochknights, led by the singer Erinnyes. Cassiodor later founded the Marechaussee Hunters to hunt Remuria's leftover monsters.

96.comment: Fontaine: Egeria, the Oceanids and the Original Sin
96.content:
Egeria was created as the new heart of the Primordial Sea after the Heavenly Principles took the Hydro Dragon's authority. Oceanids, said to spring from her tears, spread across Teyvat; when some longed to live on land, she poured Primordial Seawater into their veins, making them human. Celestia judged this unauthorised creation of life a sin, imprisoned her for a time and condemned her people. After Remuria's fall she ruled as Hydro Archon, then died at Tunigi Hollow in the cataclysm, her body becoming the Amrita.

Because their blood came from the Primordial Sea, Fontainians would dissolve on touching concentrated Primordial Seawater. After Egeria's death the Oceanids largely refused to accept Focalors and left Fontaine. Egeria chose Focalors, herself a humanised Oceanid, as successor, hoping she would find a way to deceive Celestia.

97.comment: Fontaine: The Prophecy and Focalors' Plan
97.content:
The prophecy said every Fontainian is born guilty, the waters will rise, the people will dissolve, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne. Focalors split herself: her divinity hid in the Oratrice while her humanity, Furina, played the Archon publicly for about 500 years without being told the full plan. In 4.2 Furina was tried and exposed as an ordinary Fontainian; the Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death and Focalors executed herself, destroying the throne.

Focalors had invited Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon, to Fontaine so that centuries as Iudex would teach him to care for humanity. With the authority restored, he absolved the people and remade them as true humans. He and the Traveler then subdued the All-Devouring Narwhal in the Primordial Sea, which Skirk later took away; its rampage flooded Fontaine as foretold, but no one dissolved and the waters receded. Skirk warned Neuvillette that the Gnosis was dangerous, and he gave it to Arlecchino.

98.comment: Fontaine: The Narzissenkreuz Era and the Siege of Poisson
98.content: Over five hundred years ago the outlaw Eduardo Baker fled to Poisson with hostages and the town was razed in the clash. His son Jakob and Rene de Petrichor, the mayor's son, went to the Narzissenkreuz Institute, which closed after the cataclysm and the first great flood. Later Rene founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo to survive a second flood he had predicted; Rene eventually became the being "Narzissenkreuz". About 400 years ago a battle with the Ordo at Elynas killed Mary-Ann Guillotin.

99.content:
The Knave, Arlecchino, head of the House of the Hearth orphanage in Fontaine, pressed Furina about the prophecy and once attacked her to check whether she carried the Gnosis, an encounter that left Furina traumatised. Her Fatui helped evacuate Poisson and build the "magic box" used to stage Furina's trial. Afterwards Neuvillette gave her the Hydro Gnosis.

In 4.6 Arlecchino returned and agreed with Neuvillette to withdraw her subordinates gradually and avoid special operations unless necessary; in return the authorities would not harass former House members. She later sent Sandrone's core to the Fontaine Research Institute after the Nod-Krai crisis.

100.content: In 6.7 (Luna VIII), released alongside a limited flagship event and still playable afterwards as a story quest, Fontaine celebrated a new Fontinalia Film Festival. The Harbinger Sandrone, unexpectedly revived at the Research Institute, rented the Wingalet from Wriothesley and hid aboard while Xavier filmed there, with Citlali as her front-desk cover. With the Traveler she laid to rest an amalgam of lost souls at the Tower of Ipsissimus, reunited with Columbina, visited Alain Guillotin's grave and hosted a tea party with Arlecchino, Columbina and Furina before returning to Snezhnaya.

key: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
101.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region
101.content:
Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region (also: Kinetic Energy Engineering Region): This is the area where the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering stands. Years ago the Institute's central laboratory was largely destroyed in an explosion linked to Edwin Eastinghouse's research into Arkhium, leaving huge Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies floating in the air. The organisation now works from a nearby New Fontaine Research Institute.

The region's boss is the Experimental Field Generator. The map blurb 'Variation of Debris and Metal' describes a pursuit of salvation that suddenly stopped, and an adventurer who never rests whether the destination is a castle in the sky or a deep-sea canyon.

Geography: The region lies on the northern side of the island of Erinnyes, next to Erinnyes Forest. It has the old Central Laboratory ruins, the New Institute and a scatter of former institute buildings: dormitories, an Institute of Clockwork Applications, an Executive Office, a Materials Office, an Academic Assembly Hall and a Game Venue. Dryas Wood is a small hollow between the Institute and Erinnyes Forest.

Floating Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies hang above the ruins. Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory, Bravais' Hidden Study, a Secret Vault and Kuisel's Clockwork Workshop are marked, and a Mary-Ann Memorial Park lies in the area.

Texts found around the area include notices from the Executive Office (a personnel-change announcement and a finance investigation notice), Materials Office memos, dormitory research notes, a paper-usage initiative and book-donation statistics at the New Institute, and the Research Notes of Master Ruggiero in Bravais' Hidden Study, which is one of the texts cited for the claim that 'Petrichor' means 'golem' in an ancient language.

Places: - **New Fontaine Research Institute**: the Institute's current seat since the explosion. It was formerly known as the Alain Guillotin Research Institute and hosted weekly lectures on critical projects.
- **Central Laboratory Ruins**: the wrecked heart of the old Institute.
- **Dryas Wood**: the Institute's old 'backyard' of plant nurseries; the potioneer who made 'Pure Water' is said to have lived in seclusion here.

- A stone tablet names the ancient Marechaussee Hunters and their deeds, which are unknown to the world.
- Notable item collectibles are the Cipher Letters (collecting all grants an achievement), the New Tide Anthology and the Initial Skill Sample No. 2 Development Plan, the last found in a hilichurl camp on the east edge.

People: Researchers, technicians and administrators of the Institute. According to the faction page, the co-administrators Raimondo and Choiseul now run it and Augustus Lovelace says it was a paradise for researchers before they took over. Edwin Eastinghouse, a Senior Technician, made the Prototype Cal. Breguet series of Clockwork Meka.

Culture: The Institute studies machines and energy; many inventions of Fontaine, including clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores by founder Alain Guillotin, come from it. Unlike the Sumeru Akademiya it does not educate or administer the public. It is controversial: Elphane finds its technicians' lectures ghastly, and the Mekafish it built to clean the water ended up killing fish, which Linorea resents.

History: One of the Institute's main aims was to find answers to the prophesied flood, and researchers believed harnessing Arkhium to defy gravity was the key. Eastinghouse's field generator overloaded, destroying most of the Institute and hurling blocks of water and ruins into the sky. After this the Institute rebuilt nearby and the Callas Line aquabus route was shut down.

The Poisson Tunnel was dug earlier by Institute machines. After the explosion the new Institute suffers money troubles; Salsa mentions plans for a 'Ruins Tour'. The quest Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble sees another explosion in the Central Laboratory ruins that scatters components of the Arkhium inhibitor.

Atmosphere: Wrecked laboratories with huge blocks of water hanging overhead. The quest describes dealing with the new Institute's administration as a long, mind-numbing procedure.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers, Clockwork Meka, Fontemer Aberrants, hilichurl camps, Frost and Wind Operatives and the Experimental Field Generator. In the quest, a second explosion scatters components of the large Arkhium inhibitor into the waters around the ruins.

Travel: The region adjoins Erinnyes Forest and Dryas Wood. The Callas Line aquabus route was shut after the explosion.

Quests: World quests include Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble (the start of the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles), In Search of Lost Time, Villains, Ardent Calibration, Buried Honor, Road to the Singularity, Science of Data Management and Treacherous Light of the Depths.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the old laboratories remain in ruins and the Institute operates from the New location.

No newer content than 4.1 was found for this area.

102.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region: Allogravity-Condensed Water Bodies
102.content: Large blocks of water left floating in the air after the explosion that devastated the Central Laboratory, in an institute whose research aimed to use Arkhium to defy gravity.

103.comment: Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region: New Fontaine Research Institute
103.content: The Institute's current building, built near the old ruins after the explosion. Former name: Alain Guillotin Research Institute. Raimondo and Choiseul run it as co-administrators in the quest Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble.

104.content:
Forbidden Zone: The Forbidden Zone is the hidden lowest part of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison. It is built over Primordial Water, and a giant sluice gate there was made to stop that water from flooding Fontaine. Only the Fortress's Administrator, Wriothesley, may enter, and he reaches it by a secret stair from his office.

Prisoners tend to go quiet when asked about it, though the guards confirm that it exists. For years almost nobody remembered why the Fortress had been built, and the zone holds the answer.

Geography: A hidden staircase opens beneath the Duke's Office in the Administrative Area, and the office's basement has a lift down to the zone. Three large isolation doors lead into a chamber with the sluice gate and a bank of dashboards. A glass-walled room off the Duke's basement overlooks a huge ship under construction.

After Masquerade of the Guilty (the end of Chapter IV) the door to that glass room stays open permanently, but the ship is no longer there.

Places: The main chamber holds the sluice gate and the dashboards. Wriothesley watched the readings for years without knowing what they measured. A secret works nearby holds the Wingalet, a huge vessel he had built as a lifeboat in case the Primordial Water broke through.

Wriothesley modelled the ship on the legendary golden ship Fortuna of ancient Remuria, using a factory's worth of labour, materials and technology. He showed the Traveler and Paimon the ship before telling them its purpose.

Governance: Entry belongs to the Administrator alone. Wriothesley became Administrator and kept the zone from the inmates; even many of the people who worked on the ship were not told what it was for.

History: When exiles were first sent to the seaside in the age of the Hydro Archon Egeria, they began building the Fortress under her guidance to guard a secret deep beneath the waves. Their community grew into a home for sinners, and over centuries the reason for its founding faded from memory. Wriothesley learned it from an elderly research historian. As the prophecy says, if the gate fails, Fontaine will drown and all will dissolve into the sea.

About a year before the Traveler arrived, Wriothesley noticed the dashboards creeping upward without knowing why. Freminet later traced Childe's route to a sewer opening and found the seawater there diluted with Primordial Water, which let Wriothesley work out what the gauges measured. Soon after, the water behind the gate burst through. Neuvillette pushed it back and resealed it in the vault, for the time being.

Wriothesley says the Fortress can do more than visitors expect, and treats the ship as a long-shot hedge: he told the Traveler that hope is often found at the end of a voyage, and that trying could not hurt. Lyney, sent to look into Childe's disappearance, had already established from the guards that a forbidden zone existed, even though prisoners refused to discuss it.

Dangers: Primordial Water dissolved Fontainians who touched it, until the change of 4.2. In 4.1 it was seeping into the sea around the Fortress, and the Fortress was evacuated 'upwards and outwards' during the breach.

Atmosphere: Heavy isolation doors, the hum of gauges and a sense of pressure from the water above and beyond. The Duke's quiet confidence makes it feel more like a closely kept secret than a prison cell.

Quests: Revealed in the Archon Quest Chapter IV, Act IV, in 'Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones', after the Traveler answers Wriothesley's riddles about the Fortress's hidden rules. The breach is in 'Calamitous Tread' (4.1).

Status as of 7.1: Its sluice gate was resealed by Neuvillette in 4.1.

What became of the chamber after the flood of the prophecy is not described in the sources read; treat it as unknown.

105.comment: Forbidden Zone: The Dashboards and the Sluice Gate
105.content: The gauges in the Forbidden Zone measure Primordial Water levels, though Wriothesley did not know this at first. He only knew they were rising. The Fortress was built with Egeria's help to hold back the Primordial Sea, so the gate stands between Fontaine and the flood that the prophecy foretells.

106.content:
Fort Charybdis Ruins (also: Fort Charybdis, Mysterious Ruins of Fort Charybdis): Fort Charybdis Ruins are the remains of a fort on an island in the eastern part of the Morte Region. Inside lies a hidden underground complex, the Orthant of Wishes, which holds one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage placed by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The fort's name is also spoken by Remurian golems in 4.6 as a place where their legions were told to fall back. Canon text about the fort itself is thin.

The fort was introduced in Version 4.2 with the Morte Region and the World Quest chain In the Wake of Narcissus. The area is linked to the Ordo's diary notes and a hymn that Boethius later quotes.

Geography: An island ruin on the east of the Morte Region. The visible fort is a ruin on top of a "Wilderness Cavern" level, below which lies the Orthant of Wishes, a puzzle-filled chamber with several floors, mechanisms, energy flow pipes and an underwater section.

The entrance is called the Mysterious Ruins. A looking glass inside leads to a small side chamber with a chest and a Thundercraven Rifthound.

Places: Orthant of Wishes: one of four seals, in a multi-floored chamber with a riddle slate that begins "Lo, this place is the Orthant of Wishes, the Temple of Wishes, the Room of Wishes".
Second floor: holds the diary and the engraved hymn excerpt.

People: No named inhabitants. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo's members left behind a diary; the Ordo's founder Jakob Ingold and their leader, the Master, appear in it. Caterpillar and Ann help the Traveler find the seals.

History: No source describes who built the fort or why. The Ordo later used the site as one of four seals for its Great Ritual; the diary of a member records that the party found "Remuria's ruins" at the indicated location and arranged an official construction project.

The diary says the Palais Mermonia confirmed the location and a construction team arrived, with Marechaussee Hunters hired for security. The Master and Mr. Ingold brought an Oceanid to a tower not yet finished; later they said the Master was performing the Great Ritual, tied to celestial bodies and the Primal Fire (Phlogiston). Workers began spreading uneasy rumours, and a faction led by a woman called Zenaida left the Ordo, but the writer later found by divination that those who had left were still inside the tower.

The excerpt on the second floor comes from a hymn titled "Echoes Hallowed and Humble", Movement 5. It praises will as what humans share with the noblest gods, and says those who command with their will will be obeyed by everyone else. In Gradus ad Capitolium Boethius quotes this verse as his own justification for demanding that the surface dwellers submit.

In The Last Day of Remuria the Remurian Este tells the soldiers of Legio IX that they ought to have retreated to Fort Charybdis, and the leader replies that they stayed behind as the rearguard while the main troops went there. A Fort Charybdis is therefore a named military position of the Remurian war, though the wiki does not say it is this ruin. The name matches the sea monster Charybdis, paired with Scylla in Greek myth, as the wiki's trivia notes.

Quests: In Meteoric Lance, part of Search in the Algae Sea, the Traveler enters the ruins, solves puzzles and reads the riddle slate to collect a wish piece for the seal. In both versions a man lies unconscious at the door and is taken to Lumidouce Harbor for treatment; the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's handiwork is suspected.

Quest gameplay includes raising a gate to a lift, an energy flow puzzle, a Seelie court, an underwater section and Xenochromatic Hunter's Ray tasks, ending with the obtained wish piece.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged since the 4.2 quest. The seal and the Ordo's apparatus remain.

Nothing newer than the 4.2 quest is known about the site.

Dangers: Clockwork mek guards (Underwater Patrol Mek, Recon Log Mek - Ousia), puzzle machinery, strong water currents, and the Ordo's lingering traps.

Atmosphere: Salt air and still stone, then a hum of machinery below. The mood is of an old military post made secret and then recycled for ritual.

107.comment: Fort Charybdis Ruins: Excerpt: Echoes Hallowed and Humble
107.content: An engraved hymn in the Mysterious Ruins, quoted as Movement 5, Stanza 3 of "Echoes Hallowed and Humble". It contrasts barbarians and witless water creatures with those whose strength comes from will, which they share with the noblest gods, and says the obedient rest bow down before those who command by will. A line in the Orthant of Memory, a different seal, quotes Movement 9, Stanza 37 of the same work, and Cassiodor quotes that second verse against Boethius in Fortune Plango Vulnera.

108.comment: Fort Charybdis Ruins: Someone's Diary (Ordo Construction Notes)
108.content: A member of the Ordo reports that the project was kept official, with Marechaussee Hunters hired for safety, while the Master prepared the Great Ritual with Mr. Ingold's help. Some members left, others remained in the tower. The writer ends by wanting to speak to Ingold in person.

109.content:
Fortress of Meropide (also: Meropide): The Fortress of Meropide is a metal-walled stronghold under the sea in Fontaine's Liffey Region. It serves as Fontaine's de facto prison: people convicted at trial are sent there to serve their sentences. It is also the nation's largest maker of clockwork meka. Legally it governs itself. Convicts there count as exiles, and the Court of Fontaine has no jurisdiction beyond lending some Gardes for security. Inside, Credit Coupons replace Mora. The Administrator is Wriothesley, a former inmate who holds the honorary title of "Duke". The Melusine Sigewinne runs the infirmary.

To ordinary Fontainians the name is a byword for punishment ("I'll punch you straight into the Fortress of Meropide"). Its real founding purpose was forgotten for centuries: it was built to guard a sealed opening to the Primordial Sea.

Geography: The Fortress lies on the seabed off the Liffey Region, ringed by searchlights. Convicts reach it from River Talionis, a reception wharf beneath the Opera Epiclese. A lift behind the opera house descends to the wharf, and a boat carries them through an underground tunnel to the Fortress. A second entrance is reached from Erinnyes. Inside, its levels run from the Reception Area and the Dormitory Block down to the Administrative Area, two levels of the Production Zone and the Abandoned Production Zone.

The Fortress's viewpoint is titled "The Copper Keep". Below the Duke's office, a stair leads to the "forbidden zone", where a great sluice gate holds back Primordial water. In the Abandoned Production Zone a notice says that work in the Geode Mine Shaft has been suspended and its connecting paths sealed.

Places: The Administrative Area is the hub, built around a central office. The Duke's Office stands at its centre. It has three floors: Wriothesley's office with a desk, sofa and tea table on top, and a basement with a lift to the forbidden zone. The Coupon Cafeteria serves meals. The Pankration Ring, reached by its own lift, is the Fortress's favourite entertainment. The infirmary, run by Sigewinne, is open to everyone at all hours. The Production Zone, two levels below the Administrative Area, is where inmates work.

Other fixtures are the Rag and Bone Shop (run by Alvard), the registration desk at reception and the dormitory cells. At the cafeteria the clockwork meka Bran hands out one free Welfare Meal per person per day. The meal is a surprise dish with a fortune slip, and the only thing in the Fortress that costs no Coupons. A room off the Duke's basement overlooks the dock where the Wingalet was built in secret.

People: Wriothesley, the Duke, rarely leaves the Fortress. He gets the information and resources he needs through his own network and treats inmates, guards and staff alike. Sigewinne, the Head Nurse, is a Melusine who came in as a convict and stayed after her sentence to care for everyone. The population is mostly inmates working off sentences, plus guards (some of them Gardes lent by the Court) and staff. Gardemeks also patrol.

Named residents include the receptionist Monglane, the guard Deakin (who escorted the Traveler in), the cafeteria supervisor Wolsey, the cook Cuistot, and Edwin Eastinghouse, a former senior researcher of the Fontaine Research Institute. Some inmates choose to stay after their sentences end, partly because his reforms made life bearable and partly for fear of being shunned outside.

Inmates sometimes form their own clubs. Some are benign, such as Vautrin's Mutual Aid Network. Others are predatory, such as the Beret Society. The researcher Jurieu, once Edwin Eastinghouse's assistant and now Wriothesley's technical consultant, works here with his assistant Lourvine on the Wingalet. The chef Escoffier once served a short sentence here: she insisted on taking responsibility for a food-safety incident with lumitide, which turned out to have been planted by Monica.

Governance: The Fortress is formally autonomous and self-governing. Criminals sent there are technically exiles from Fontaine, and the Court cannot even investigate inside without the administrator's consent. In 4.1 Neuvillette had to send the Traveler in undercover. The Administrator holds all authority. Wriothesley runs the place through Mora, manpower and the right people, and comes down hard on anyone who exploits others. The Fortress sells meka to the surface, and the Palais Mermonia is one of its best customers, so he gladly satisfies the Maison Gestion's strict paperwork.

The Fortress is said to have changed hands chaotically several times over the centuries. Through all of it, residents have kept an unspoken agreement never to harm the medical staff. Wriothesley came to power by challenging the previous, corrupt administrator. The Palais later granted him the title of Duke. The Fortress has a logistics agreement with the Spina di Rosula, which Wriothesley keeps to the terms he agreed with the late Callas.

Culture: Credit Coupons are the only currency inside, earned by work and spent on food, goods and comforts. Pankration bouts in the Ring are the main entertainment. Inmates get a monthly "free day" off, and pipe-cleaning days come round every month.
The Fortress keeps "hidden rules" that work as lessons rather than threats. An inmate who works three days in a row is served "mystery meat" at the next Welfare Meal. It is really a restorative dish Sigewinne cooks, but because Melusines perceive colour differently, it looks inedible to humans. An inmate who bets on both fighters in a Pankration match receives a bottle of blood-red liquid the next day. It is an experimental Fonta recipe Wriothesley judged of low value, sent to teach the worth of Coupons. A third rule, never explained in the Archon Quest, concerns Sigewinne and the people in the infirmary. Anyone rude to Sigewinne is said to be punished extra harshly.

In Wriothesley's youth Coupons bought far more: drugs, the winners of fixed fights, people's loyalty, even a killing. The Pankration Ring then had no fixed venue or rules. His reforms ended that. Today pankration is billed as good exercise, and anything from a Sternshield Crab to a clockwork meka may enter the Ring if special conditions are met.

History: In the age of the first Hydro Archon, Egeria, Fontaine exiled its criminals and refused them help. Some repented and begged for mercy. Egeria forgave them and set them to guard her secret beneath the waves, and they built the first fortress. Later generations of exiles kept working on it long after the first had died. The secret was an opening to the Primordial Sea, sealed behind a sluice gate in a "forbidden zone" that only the warden and trusted people may enter. Over the centuries almost everyone forgot why the Fortress existed.

About 400 years ago Neuvillette sentenced Vautrin, former head of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, to the Fortress for killings he committed to avenge the Melusine Carole. There Vautrin founded the Mutual Aid Network. Later the Melusine Sigewinne was sent here for breaking an ancient law against changing a creature into human form. She had altered her own body to look human so she could treat a sick human friend. She served her sentence and stayed as nurse. At some point the Fatui Harbinger Pantalone introduced the Credit Coupons, together with an administrator of the time, as an economic experiment. Wriothesley arrived as a teenage convict and later took over as administrator.

Wriothesley built his wealth in the old, rule-less Pankration Ring and by investing, until he held more Coupons than every other inmate combined. The administrator emptied his account in one night. Wriothesley turned that injustice into a rallying cause and publicly challenged the administrator to a duel, and no inmate or guard objected. The administrator fled before the duel, on the very day Wriothesley's sentence ended, so no one was left to sign his release. He walked into the central office and took over the duties.

Dangers: Before the Duke's reforms the Fortress was violent and corrupt, and canon still describes it as a place of conflicting interests that can corrupt people. Searchlights around the exterior catch swimmers who come too close and bring them in. The real danger lies below: Primordial water behind the sluice gate, which dissolved Fontainians on contact until 4.2. In 4.1 its concentration around the Fortress rose sharply, and Freminet collapsed after swimming through it.

Atmosphere: Industrial and enclosed: riveted metal walls, hissing pipes, the clang of the production lines, guards and Gardemeks on the walkways, and no sunlight. The infirmary is the warmest place in the Fortress. Wriothesley jokes that a real problem would be feeling water drip on your head.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter IV Acts III-IV (4.1) take place mostly here: the Traveler serves a 45-day "sentence" under false charges to look for Childe. Wriothesley's story quest, Cerberus Chapter Act I "Reborn in the Land of Grievances" (4.1), and the world quest series "Scenes from Life in Meropide" also take place here.
The Traveler first enters in "A Tea Party Most Thorny" and "Fortress of Meropide" (Act III). "Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones" and "Calamitous Tread" (Act IV) reveal and breach the sluice gate. Act V opens with the Traveler's release.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates as prison and factory under Wriothesley, with Sigewinne as Head Nurse.

Neuvillette resealed the breached sluice gate in 4.1. Since 4.2 Fontainians no longer dissolve in Primordial water. After the prophecy's flood the Wingalet went back into storage at the Fortress.

110.comment: Fortress of Meropide: Credit Coupons and the Welfare Meal
110.content:
Credit Coupons are the Fortress of Meropide's internal currency and replace Mora for every transaction inside. Inmates earn them through work and spend them at the Coupon Cafeteria, the Rag and Bone Shop and elsewhere. With enough Coupons one can order meals to taste. Everyone gets one free Welfare Meal a day from the meka Bran: a surprise dish of unpredictable quality plus a fortune slip. It is the one equality in the Fortress that need not be bought.

The text of the weapon Cashflow Supervision says the Fatui Harbinger Pantalone invented the Coupons and set them up in the Fortress as an experiment in his project of replacing Mora, a god-controlled currency, with a man-made one. A past administrator was his partner. Before Wriothesley's reforms, Coupons could buy drugs, fixed-fight results, loyalty and even murder.

111.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Forbidden Zone and the Sluice Gate
111.content:
Beneath the Duke's Office, behind three large isolation doors, is a chamber with a giant sluice gate and gauges. Only the Administrator may enter. Wriothesley had long wondered what lay behind it. Over the year before the Traveler's arrival its gauge crept into the red. After Freminet collapsed from Primordial Seawater in the waters near the Fortress, Wriothesley concluded the gate held back the Primordial Sea. Inmates with historians' backgrounds had also argued to him that the sea which once swallowed Remuria might someday return. Soon afterwards the gate burst. Wriothesley held the water with Cryo ice, Clorinde shot a control panel to drop the security gates, and Neuvillette arrived, pushed the water back and resealed the gate.

Wriothesley first noticed the gauge rising about a year before 4.1. After dealing with Fatui spies, he swam briefly in the surrounding sea, found his skin tinged red for a while, and told no one. Inmates were evacuated upward during the breach. The eruption beneath the Fortress was later cited at Furina's trial as evidence that the prophecy was coming true.

112.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Traveler's Imprisonment
112.content:
Childe, wrongly convicted by the Oratrice in the disappearances case, was sent to the Fortress and then vanished. The Knave asked for access, and Neuvillette, who has no jurisdiction inside, proposed a third party instead. He charged the Traveler and Paimon with eating a cake meant for Furina, and they were given 45 days. Wriothesley guided part of their tour himself. They found that a group of inmates who had come to follow Childe had invented a "hidden rule" about cannibals in the pipes to cover his escape: he had left through the pipes after hearing a "voice" again. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet were inside too, having got themselves imprisoned by staging a theft on the Knave's orders.

Wriothesley had already spotted and removed the Fatui's planted informants, and he watched the House of the Hearth siblings. When Lynette vanished from the infirmary, Lyney stormed his office and charged him, and Sigewinne felled Lyney with a tranquilliser dart. Clorinde, hired by Wriothesley for "side work", then brought in Freminet, who had collapsed from Primordial Seawater while tracing Childe's route. After the sluice gate was resealed, the Traveler served out the sentence, signed release papers with Monglane and felt a tremor from the surface: the Poisson disaster.

113.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Mutual Aid Network
113.content: The Mutual Aid Network is an inmates' society founded about 400 years ago by Vautrin, the exiled former captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. He never resorted to violence or abuse and urged the weaker convicts, mostly people jailed for minor crimes, to band together. Its badge is modelled on the Medal of Peace that Neuvillette gave him. Its three principles are helping others, promoting justice and accepting proper judgment. It encourages cleaning, exercise, tutoring and study, and asks members to face up to their crimes together. It still exists.

key: Reborn in the Land of Grievances
114.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Beret Society Incident
114.content: In Wriothesley's story quest, the Traveler returned to the Fortress and was shown the Beret Society, a club of apparently model prisoners whose berets marked them as reformed. Its founder Dougier secretly controlled the members through "censure": thorn-like clips hidden under the berets and a fear-inducing solution called "Aqua Doloris". He bribed an overseer, hid a real headquarters in the Production Zone, and gathered decommissioned Gardemeks for an all-out move against Wriothesley. With the inmate couple Avice and Faissolle's help, Wriothesley and the Traveler freed the members, destroyed the Gardemeks and subdued Dougier. Wriothesley then personally apologised to each member. The quest also shows contraband arriving in supply shipments, here a gem that stirred up bad memories.

115.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Wingalet at the Fortress
115.content: Expecting the gate to fail, Wriothesley secretly had a huge vessel built, inspired by Remurian legend (the golden Fortuna), with guidance from the researchers Jurieu and Lourvine and a factory's worth of labour, materials and technology. He kept it from the other inmates for fear of riots. When the prophecy's flood came, the Wingalet rose to the surface and rescued people. It was then returned to the Fortress, where Charlotte later interviewed Jurieu and Lourvine about it.

116.comment: Fortress of Meropide: The Wingalet at the Fontinalia Film Festival
116.content: During the limited-time event Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7), the idle Wingalet, expensive to maintain, was brought to the surface and rented out during the Fontinalia Film Festival to earn Mora and lift the morale of the inmates who maintain it. The renter was Sandrone, who paid a high fee without haggling and had a fishing permit and business license on her desk; she set up an aquarium aboard. At the end of the event Wriothesley asked her, as the ship's current captain, to leave some of the aquarium installations in place so the inmates who clean and maintain the Wingalet could enjoy them back at the Fortress.

117.content:
Fountain of Lucine (also: Fontaine de Lucine, Lucine Fountain): The Fountain of Lucine stands in front of the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine. Fontainians say all of the nation's water ultimately gathers there, and it is the origin of the habit of tossing coins into fountains to make wishes. It has listened to Fontainians' wishes for a very long time.

In play it is also an offering system: Hydro Sigils gathered across Fontaine can be thrown into it to raise its level and earn rewards, and at the top level extra streams of water rise from its six corners.

Geography: A large ornamental fountain on the plaza before the Opera Epiclese, in the Court of Fontaine Region. A water-themed inscription is carved on it; in paraphrase it asks that no spring or fountain ever run dry and that the torrent of life wash over the valley. Rainbow Rose and Romaritime Flower grow nearby as local specialties.

Ordinary Fontainians gather around it: the wiki lists a bard, a light novelist, a reporter, a traveling scholar and a member of the Gardes among the NPCs found here. Fully raised through offerings, the main jet grows stronger and six side streams run from its corners.

Culture: Fontainians throw coins into fountains to make wishes, a custom a loading-screen text says truly began with tossing Hydro Sigils into this fountain, which it calls the correct way to wish. Newlyweds traditionally wish for children here, according to the Archon Quest chapter set in the city.

Long ago wishing at the fountain was a ritual for Oceanids who longed for human life: blessed by the spring water, they would become human in the months after. This is told in the Finale of the Fontaine Archon Quest.

History: The Fontaine Archon Quest treats the fountain as the point where all water in Fontaine converges, even the water of tears. When people dissolved from contact with Primordial Sea water (Vigneire and the victims of the disappearance case), their consciousnesses also gathered here and formed an Oceanid. People sensitive to Hydro can hear it, and drinking Water from the Primordial Sea let the Traveler and Vacher meet it in the fountain. It had enough psychic force to nearly "drown" Vacher in his confrontation with it, after which he lost his mind and soon died of a panic attack.

After the quest "As Light Rain Falls Without Reason", Furina's crying voice, wondering how much longer this loneliness must last, can be heard from the fountain. HoYoLAB writing cited by the wiki says this came from Furina's thoughts during "The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur"; once that quest is complete the voice is gone.

Atmosphere: Splashing water, coins and Hydro Sigils glinting at the bottom, the Opera's steps behind it and the constant movement of Fontainians who come to wish, rest, perform or chat.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the fountain is intact and in ordinary use before the Opera Epiclese.

118.comment: Fountain of Lucine: Fountain of Lucine Offerings
118.content: Gameplay system: Hydro Sigils are offered in groups of thirty, and 1,500 are required to reach the top level, which gives the achievement Dew Song. Before 4.6 the level cap was 20, 30 and 40 in 4.0, 4.1 and 4.2-4.5 respectively.

119.content:
Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe (also: The World's Amniotic Fluid): Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe is a stretch of the Primordial Sea, the ancient water beneath Fontaine, reached only during the world quest Waking from the Great Dream (4.2). It is the arena where the Traveler, Paimon and Ann face Narzissenkreuz, the failed leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

The quest places the Traveler in an ocean current that leads to a giant Hydro figure. Its in-game viewpoint is titled "The World's Amniotic Fluid", with the line that this was once meant to be the cradle of all life again.

Geography: The place is water and current rather than land. The Traveler enters an ocean current, keeps moving ahead, and reaches a giant being, Narzissenkreuz, in a Hydro-filled arena. During the fight, rift-like cracks and a bubble the Holy Blade points toward appear in the water. Healing orbs occasionally rise in the arena.

Narzissenkreuz warns that anyone caught in the current faces a "cracking and leaking" of the self within the amniotic sea. The Traveler can break his hold on the arena by riding the current and using the quest-only Sword of Narzissenkreuz against him. Gameplay note: the quest teleport waypoint starts at the Tower of Ipsissimus and moves to the arena partway through.

History: Narzissenkreuz sought to bring about a new world and so avert the apocalypse of the Prophecy of Fontaine, and took control of the Primordial Sea for that purpose. In the quest he claims to be saving the world and demands the Holy Blade. After he falls, he says he has lost all control of the Primordial Sea and that the new world cannot be born.

Defeated, he admits that his plan has harmed many people and apologises when Ann presses him, though he still says his aims were lofty. He says that he wishes to go back to the time before the Narzissenkreuz heroes set out. Ann asks him to come back with them, and says the primordial waters are then to be resealed. He later vanishes in the quest Rowboat's Wake, according to the wiki.

The dialogue changes with the player's progress. If Masquerade of the Guilty is done, Narzissenkreuz says a "variable" has descended on the world and calls the Traveler its witness and recorder, and that the world has been saved nonetheless. If not, he speaks of the whale being put to flight and of a world still fated to be saved. He says Director Lyris, unable to grasp the present, holds onto the still-living Mary-Ann; Ann answers that her name is Ann.

Atmosphere: Vast, dreamlike and ominous: deep water without a shore, a voice announcing that the day of return has come, and a being that speaks of salvation while attacking. The mood is one of a half-formed world, grief and a failed dream rather than ordinary menace.

Dangers: Narzissenkreuz fights with Hydro attacks in the form of water-made fists, spears, hammers and swords, and calls down a "Rain of Blades". For the quest the party is limited to a trial Traveler. Fontaine-born people dissolve in pure Primordial Seawater, while non-Fontainians only gain greater sensitivity to Hydro, according to the Primordial Sea page.

Travel: There is no ordinary route. The quest sends the party into the Primordial Sea by current. The viewpoint is only available by entering the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's hidden chamber through a book in a set spot, and its Archive entry stays hidden until collected.

Quests: Waking from the Great Dream, the single world quest of the third act of In the Wake of Narcissus (after Savior's Wake and before Rowboat's Wake). Completing it grants the achievement An Immortal Emperor in a Mundane Universe.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the place is known only from this quest. Narzissenkreuz was defeated there, and the story afterwards moves on to the resealing of the water and his later disappearance.

120.comment: Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe: Narzissenkreuz's Defeat in the Primordial Sea
120.content: In the Primordial Sea, Narzissenkreuz called the Traveler an equal to a world, only after the Holy Blade had cut through the will around him. Beaten, he said the Holy Blade was not on his side and that his ordinary self had returned to its body. Ann, whose soul he said was made of two colours, forgave him in her own right.

121.content:
Geode Mine Shaft (also: Arkhium Crystal Geode Mine Shaft): The Geode Mine Shaft is an abandoned mine in the Fortress of Meropide's abandoned production zone, filled with Arkhium crystal and patrolled by Flying Energy Thieves. It is the escape route used in the world quest An Eye for an Eye.

Mining stopped after the Fontaine Research Institute accident. A locking research terminal at the shaft's front opens only with two people working together, and the way out is rigged with a hazard.

Geography: Reached from the abandoned production zone level of the Fortress, beyond sluice gates and a pipe, in a setting that looks nothing like the rest of the Fortress: no signs of ordinary buildings, only rock, tunnels and glittering crystal.

The walls are studded with Arkhium crystals, which Lanoire mistakes at first for gems. Caterpillar identifies them as Arkhium.

Arkhium mining here ended with the Fontaine Research Institute accident, and the mine has been left to the Flying Energy Thieves since.

Dangers: A Flying Energy Thief guards the shaft: a "trial product" that pursues anyone carrying an energy storage device and disables the device. The front research terminal needs such a device to start, so whoever activates it is chased.

A posted notice warns that the lock needs two people at once, that the energy storage unit has been removed from the terminal, and that the manufacturer is not liable for loss of control or explosions. It urges anyone to turn back, saying production-zone work is hard but not life-threatening. Its tone is bureaucratic and darkly sarcastic.

History: Arkhium mining here halted after the Fontaine Research Institute accident. Later, guards had Clynes install a lock like the one at the Rift of Erosion; Clynes mentioned having prepared a "surprise" there, and the notice at the terminal describes the Flying Energy Thief.

Quests: In An Eye for an Eye (4.1, chapter Unfinished Comedy), Caterpillar decides to take Lanoire out of the Fortress and back to her family via this shaft. The Traveler and Paimon help, race the Flying Energy Thief and open the way out. On the other side Lanoire sees the open outdoors for the first time.

Caterpillar says he can never be truly human but imitates human kindness, and that he believes his sins can never be absolved, which is why he acts. See his own entry rather than repeating his story here.

Status as of 7.1: Disused as a mine and known only as the route in the quest, as of 7.1.

122.comment: Geode Mine Shaft: Flying Energy Thief
122.content: A trial mechanism posted at the Geode Mine Shaft that hunts anyone carrying an energy storage device and disables it. According to the notice at the terminal it was never reviewed internally or by peers.

123.content:
Hidden Dwelling (also: Guillotin home): The Hidden Dwelling is the former home of Alain Guillotin and of his creations Sandrone and Pulonia. Its map description calls it a place where flowers and grasses flourish and time passes gently. It is a quiet house that bears witness to everything that unfolded in the 'home'. It becomes accessible in the 6.7 event story Those We Have Lost and stays open afterwards.

Sandrone, known to the Fatui as the Marionette, was brought to life here and later left. Alain Guillotin is the founder of the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering.

Geography: A house with a garden, a workshop area with a workbench, a fireplace with an old easy chair, a desk and Alain's bedroom, kept almost as it was when Sandrone left. In the event quest the party goes beneath Fontaine's waters, with the Wingalet as their base, and activates a water-insulating mechanism to reach it.

Flowers and grasses grow around it. The wiki's infobox places it in the Beryl Region of Fontaine, and it appears as a point of interest with its own interior map.

Places: The workbench is where both Sandrone and Pulonia were brought to life; later Sandrone worked on Pulonia there. A desk holds old maths toys and puzzles, among them the Pagoda Stack, a gear-moving puzzle. Alain's bedroom has a box with a hidden gear-locked compartment. By the fireplace sits an easy chair. The mechanical piano, which Alain once built, stood outside the house. A picture of Alain with Rene hangs in the house.

The Pagoda Stack puzzle (a variant of the Tower of Hanoi) can be replayed after the quest in easy (3 layers), normal (5 layers) and hard (7 layers) modes. After the event ended the piano that the Traveler had recovered was returned to its old place outside. With Sandrone as the active character, interacting with the piano plays a cutscene of her performing her theme.

Items kept here include Alain's drafts from his later years, letters Sandrone says she never bothered to sort, a Multidimensional Algorithmic Core Alain used to store information (only Sandrone and Pulonia can access it), and two pictures. One shows Alain and Rene at the Institute of Natural Philosophy before their falling-out. The other shows Sandrone as a newborn among the plants, with a message wishing her to grow and flourish like them. After Those We Have Kept both pictures return from the Wingalet to the dwelling.

People: Alain Guillotin lived here, growing bedridden in his last years. He taught Sandrone mechanics and let her take over his workbench. Sandrone and Pulonia are described as his prime creations. The three are said to have kept a quiet, repetitive but peaceful life here, which Sandrone later called a world where time did not exist.

Alain looked at the picture of himself and Rene by the fireplace with a mix of guilt and longing, and told Sandrone he sometimes regretted not stopping his friend. At the end of Those We Have Kept Sandrone says the home is as quiet and warm as ever and that she will tend its flowers more often.

Culture: The household turned on puzzles and music. Sandrone beat Alain at the games, so played with Pulonia instead, taught herself the piano because music is, to her, mathematics, composed her own pieces, and eventually got rid of the piano when Alain's illness made music hard to bear.

History: During Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7), Sandrone brings the Traveler and Paimon to the dwelling in the event quest Those We Have Lost to look for a gift Alain left behind. They find it in a hidden compartment in his bedroom. In the next quest, Those We Have Kept, the home is restored to a quiet state and Pulonia's body is returned to the workstation.

The quest also has Sandrone and the party face 'anomalies' in the house and sit down to tea together, and speak with Columbina. Pulonia's body stands inert after the second quest.

Dangers: No hazards are described. Sandrone only warns the Traveler to be careful with the old belongings and the dust.

Atmosphere: Still and gentle: flowers, fireplace and a dusty workshop. Sandrone's idle remarks as she wanders the house are brief, such as 'Old notes...', 'Pulonia...' and 'A warm hearth...'.

Travel: Freely accessible after Those We Have Lost. Teleport to the point of interest named Hidden Dwelling.

Quests: Those We Have Lost and Those We Have Kept, the second and third parts of Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7, a limited-time event).

Status as of 7.1: Quiet and open to visit as of 7.1.

Alain's piano stands outside again, Pulonia's inactive body is in the workstation, and the two pictures are back in the house.

124.comment: Hidden Dwelling: Alain's Gift and the Multidimensional Algorithmic Core
124.content: In Those We Have Lost, Sandrone searches Alain's bedroom for the 'Gift' he left. A box holds a hidden compartment locked with gears, which she opens. It contains a letter and a cube, the Multidimensional Algorithmic Core that Alain used to store information. Other things in the box, which Sandrone calls junk, include a picture of her as a baby among the plants.

125.content:
Hortus Euergetis: Hortus Euergetis (Latin, "Garden of Euergetis") is an underwater garden in Machimos, the outer city of Remuria in the Sea of Bygone Eras. It takes its name from Euergetia, a Harmost of Remuria who died in the kingdom's destruction. A short engraving at its waypoint, signed by Ouranides of Ouranopolis, wishes her peace and promises that flowers will always bloom for her here.

Introduced in Version 4.6 and visited in the quest The Last Day of Remuria. Hunter's Rays swim over it.

Geography: A subarea of Machimos, the outer city of the capital, near the Initium Iani, Caesareum Palace and Portus Anticus. The engraving sits on the upper north-east side of the teleport waypoint, at the base of a rock arch. The tall rock formations of Machimos are thought to be remnants of the old city.

Machimos was a city of temples, arenas, gilded walls and markets before it sank.

People: Euergetia, called the benefactrix, was one of the four Harmosts of Remuria and is remembered as kindhearted. Her friend Cassiodor (writing as Ouranides of Ouranopolis) treats her as a sister. Boethius, another Harmost, is said in the Faded Castle's notes to have wished to revive Remuria with her after her death but failed.

Euergetia ordered an investigation into the beliefs of the northern tribes, and used her power as a Harmost to let conquered people taste their homeland dishes in their imaginations. She entrusted the Legio VI to Boethius and an engraving at Caesareum Palace links her to the three chains forged with blood and bone to bind the dragon Scylla (the text leaves unclear whose blood and bone they were).

Culture: The epitaph is gentle and funerary, unlike the martial engravings elsewhere in Remuria's ruins: it prays that her melody find peace, that she sleep without grieving for the past or fearing the future, and that she laugh as before.

History: Canon does not describe the garden's origin; the name suggests it commemorates Euergetia. She died when Remuria was destroyed. The epitaph says her name and kindness may be forgotten, but flowers will still bloom for her here.

Quests: The Last Day of Remuria lists the garden among the quest's subareas. No dialogue is tied to the garden itself.

Status as of 7.1: A quiet sunken memorial as of 7.1; nothing in later content changes it.

The likely writer of the epitaph, Cassiodor, is present in the 4.6 quests as Monsieur Os (Cassiodor speaking through the cat Osse), so the friend who mourned Euergetia is still alive in the story, though no dialogue ties him to the garden.

Dangers: Hunter's Rays are the common enemy.

Atmosphere: Still water over a sunken garden; a calm, mournful place among harsher ruins, with a sense of private grief.

126.content: The engraving reads as a short elegy: it asks that the kindhearted Euergetia's melody find peace, calls her colleague, friend and sister, and says that though her beneficence and her name be forgotten, flowers will bloom for her here. It tells her to sleep and to weep no more, and to laugh as she once did.

127.content:
Hotel Bouffes d'ete (also: Hôtel Bouffes d'été, Hotel Bouffes d'été, the Hotel): Hotel Bouffes d'ete is a luxurious hotel in the Vasari Passage of the Court of Fontaine. It is legally owned by the Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino, called 'Father' by the orphans there, and is the base of her House of the Hearth in Fontaine. A children's home runs behind the hotel front. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet live there.

Its residents think of it as a family home. Its name means roughly 'Summer Bouffe Singers Hotel' in French.

Geography: In a corner of the Court of Fontaine in the Vasari Passage. Its story text mentions a grand hall with a phonograph, a small maintenance workroom and water-pumping equipment.

The wiki's map point is in the Vasari Passage. Sandrone's tea table is set up near the entrance for the 'Whispers by the Hearth' tea party.

People: Current residents the wiki names are Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Chapleau, Foltz and Heloir. Former residents include Filliol, Horrer, Jeambel, Landois, Lapouyade, Nanteuil, Sotto and Tadie. Arlecchino visits infrequently and is addressed as Father; the House's rule is that betrayal is not tolerated.

The house is full of children who share similar sad backgrounds and help each other as family would. Lyney was a newcomer and became the person around whom the Hotel's life turns. Freminet worked in maintenance there. The twins were recommended by the hotel's manager and still found the other children slow to accept them.

Lyney spends time with residents without prying into their pasts. He joined Freminet in the workroom after a water pump broke while Lynette used it. A Maison Gardiennage official, funded by Lyney, once fed information to the Hotel and covered up traces of some of its clandestine actions, until he was caught. Cats of the Hotel each have their own territory, and one called Rosseland likes Lyney's hat.

Governance: Arlecchino holds legal ownership and rules by her word. Orphans of the House carry the surnames Snezhevich and Snezhevna. The House's operations in Fontaine pursue what it calls a just cause but with radical methods, with Arlecchino's influence and her control over the inner workings of the Court of Fontaine preventing serious incidents, according to Lyney's profile.

After her duel with Lyney, Lynette and Freminet in Into the Sunlight (Ignis Purgatorius Chapter Act I), Arlecchino let former members Filliol and others take a memory-erasing potion instead of being killed. They left the House and, as Lynette overheard, appear to be living the lives they wanted.

Culture: Residents see the Hotel's festivals as the only warm events in their lives, since outside festivals feel cold and foreign to them. On its Founding Day the children decorate the hall with streamers, eat desserts and watch a magic show by Lyney, Lynette and Freminet.

In Lyney's Founding Day show, 'Father' herself appears from the magic box. She praised Lyney for keeping the secret as a good magic show should, cut cake for every child and joined them.

History: The Hotel is the House of the Hearth's known Fontaine base. The House traces back to an orphanage in Khaenri'ah and was later refounded by an earlier Knave. Arlecchino took over after Crucabena, and wanted the children to call her 'Father'. In Lyney's Character Stories the twins arrive at the Hotel after tragic years and settle in.

In Ignis Purgatorius Act I, two days after the duel, the Traveler returns to check on Lynette and Freminet, who are recovering at the Hotel. Lyney had earlier told the Traveler that Lynette and Freminet were recuperating at the Hotel.

Dangers: It is a Fatui front. Anyone who betrays the House faces death, though Arlecchino can spare people with a potion of her flame that erases their memories of the House.

Atmosphere: Luxurious yet lived-in. Children bustle about the halls, music plays from the phonograph, and the family atmosphere is warm until the Father arrives, when everyone straightens up.

Travel: A point of interest in the Vasari Passage. Sandrone's Portable Tea Table can be placed near the entrance to start the tea party quests Whispers by the Hearth and Tea Party Re-Invitation: House of the Hearth.

Quests: Appears in the Ignis Purgatorius Chapter (Arlecchino's story quest, requires the Archon Quest through Masquerade of the Guilty), in Lyney's profile, and in the tea party quests Whispers by the Hearth and its re-invitation.

Status as of 7.1: The House of the Hearth's Fontaine base, with Arlecchino as owner, as far as the sources read.

128.content: The wiki lists the Hotel's current residents as Chapleau, Foltz, Freminet, Heloir, Lynette and Lyney, and the former ones as Filliol, Horrer, Jeambel, Landois, Lapouyade, Nanteuil, Sotto and Tadie. The former residents are the group Arlecchino planned to 'execute' and later released as memory-wiped.

129.content:
Hotel Debord (also: Debord, Debord restaurant): Hotel Debord is a famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine. Its owner, Vaneigem, holds that art is the best seasoning for good food and often invites performers to entertain diners.

The interior is designed so guests can see performances from any seat. It was founded long ago by the chefs Modeste and Savelli, and is tied to the Gateau Debord and the head chef Escoffier.

Places: Downstairs are the dining hall, with the host Sanguinetti and the hostess Leone; upstairs hold more staff including Argalia, Rodamonte, Renaud and the boss Vaneigem. Sanguinetti sells food, ingredients and recipes, with daily restocks; Reputation Rank 4 in Fontaine gives a permanent 10 percent discount (gameplay).

A notice board advertises a dazzling night of "twin stars" revealing a secret, tying the restaurant to its stage shows.

People: Vaneigem owns it, Sanguinetti hosts and the critic Eloise dines in the hall. Savanna is the current head chef. Escoffier, a former head chef, was also Furina's chef, and Monica is a former chef.

The Codex Debord holds Modeste's original recipes and is limited to current and former head chefs, with copies made as needed.

History: Modeste and Savelli, two chefs from Fleuve Cendre, made Fontainian cuisine popular through ingredients found on their expeditions and founded the restaurant, which was soon a hit with wealthy diners. About ten years later they found a container in sunken Remurian ruins whose contents sharpened taste, and Modeste created the original Gateau Debord, limited to sixteen orders a day.

The ingredient eventually cost Modeste his sense of taste, and he took his own life in despair. Savelli, who learned the cause from a letter, took the blame for his death to protect both reputations. The restaurant's name fell for a time, but careful management restored it over decades.

Before the Traveler arrived, Escoffier led the kitchen after the hotel offered her its kitchen on learning she was Furina's chef; a cook-off left both the former head chef and the chosen successor judging her the better fit. A lumiline food-safety incident, actually caused by Monica, led Escoffier to take responsibility; she served a sentence in the Fortress of Meropide and Savanna took over. During the Treasured Above All story quest, Navia persuaded Escoffier to return, and afterwards she declined the post but agreed to visit periodically to check standards.

Atmosphere: Opulent and theatrical: dining as spectacle, with performers and a polished kitchen behind it.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1) under Savanna's management.

130.content: The legendary cake created by Modeste and later recreated by Escoffier. Originally limited to sixteen a day and queued for; it is regarded as the pinnacle of Fontaine desserts of its time.

key: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus
131.content:
Initium Iani (also: Entrance of the Passage of Ianus): Initium Iani (Latin, roughly "the beginning of Ianus") is the great gate between Machimos, Remuria's outer city, and Capitolium, its inner city. It leads to the Passage of Ianus, the only way between the two, and it was where the dragon Scylla was sealed. In The Last Day of Remuria, Scylla, freed after millennia, blasts it open so the Traveler, Paimon and Monsieur Os can reach the Domus Aurea.

Introduced in 4.6. The Remurian symphony ran through its golden waterways, which let Boethius's forces shut the gate and trap Scylla as he tried to break in.

Geography: A subarea at the edge of Machimos. Behind it a water current runs the full length of the Passage of Ianus into Capitolium. The gate is a stone door carved with seals, which fall away one by one when broken.

Stalactites hang in the corridor beyond and fall or block the way, so passage is a rushed swim. Machimos also includes Hortus Euergetis, Caesareum Palace and Portus Anticus.

People: Scylla, the vishap Dragon Prince, is tied to this place by his sealing and his breakout. Cassiodor (as Monsieur Os) explains its history. The Harmosts Boethius and Euergetia are credited with the original sealing.

Remus, the Sebastos, designed the symphony that flowed here; Scylla says the invasion was a plan with Remus. Legio VI held Caesareum Palace, where the chains were stored.

Governance: The gate was a military control point. Engravings at Caesareum Palace show Boethius ordering Portus Anticus and the Initium Iani sealed at once, seven defensive layers set and all routes of egress closed, and the Dragonborn destroyed on arrival. If the chieftain could not be slain, the chains were to be used to imprison him in the palace.

History: Remurian history: Scylla led the Dragonborn at the capital, wanting to pass this gate. Monsieur Os says Boethius and his legions used the symphony in the golden waterways to shut the gate and seal the evil dragon. Scylla's version differs: Boethius falsely claimed to have halted resistance on Remus's orders, then rose against him and turned his flesh to stone.

After Remuria sank, Scylla remained petrified for millennia. In The Last Day of Remuria the Traveler breaks three chains in Machimos and frees him. In Gradus ad Capitolium Scylla explains that shattering this gate used nearly all his remaining power, so the Domus Aurea must be opened by other means.

Quests: The Last Day of Remuria: Scylla, freed, calls the gate a glorified stone door and blasts through its seals while the group swims the Passage of Ianus. The Traveler must stay close to avoid falling stalactites.

Monsieur Os remarks that he once crossed between bodies freely so long as one was prepared in the inner city; with only his small cat body now, the group must take this road.

Status as of 7.1: Broken open by Scylla during the 4.6 quests; the door swung shut behind the group. No later content revisits it.

Dangers: Falling stalactites, current and the closing door; no sentinel remains.
