Atmosphere: A cold, vaulted entrance, then a tunnel of current and falling stone. The mood is of crossing a threshold between a defeated outer world and a sealed inner one.

132.comment: Initium Iani: The Engraving of Decimus
132.content: An engraving says that in his life he was Decimus, a humble slave, and today he is no different from the exalted Harmost, sunken to the bottom of the sea. The text does not name the Harmost or explain Decimus's role.

133.content:
Institute of Natural Philosophy (also: The Institute of Natural Philosophy, Submerged Ruins of the Institute, Liliacruces Forum ruins): The Institute of Natural Philosophy is a dilapidated underwater research facility that once belonged to an organisation of the same name led by Director Dwight Lasker. Much of its research is still preserved in the flooded ruin, including precursors of modern Fontainian technologies and the earliest experiments of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. The Traveler first reaches it in the Version 4.0 World Quest Aqueous Tidemarks.

Its notes show a scientific community that was proud, quarrelsome and worried: young prodigies, a secret group forming among its leaders, and a warning of toxins and tainted Oceanids after a great disaster.

Geography: Submerged ruins in the Court of Fontaine Region, divided into Outskirts, a Central Quartier and a Northern Quartier, with a deeper underground wing. The Traveler enters by diving and finds sealed doors, ancient logs, glass walls and laboratory rooms.

Mechanisms in the ruins include high-pressure water vents, current streams and pneumousia blocks and relays. Seelie, Fontemer seagrass and xenochromatic creatures can be found.

Places: Outskirts: where the Traveler and Virgil enter after the Liliacruces Forum site.
Central Quartier: with the underground area holding the Ancient Notes, a Hydroculus and a Ruin Guard.
Northern Quartier: further research areas.
Director's office: a locked place whose key Dwight left in a chest in the Narzissenkreuz Ordo; a few rifthounds were found inside.

In the vault, the Traveler meets a Ruin Grader called "Special" Ruin Grader, nicknamed the "Somewhat Uncooperative Research Subject", which regenerates when almost defeated.

People: Director Dwight Lasker; his childhood friends Basil Elton, Emanuel Guillotin and Karl Ingold; the young prodigies he recruited, including Coppelius, Alain Guillotin and Alain's assistant Carter Scherbius; and Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, who joined Alain's lab and later founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. In the present, the guide Virgil leads the Traveler.

Governance: A Director ran the Institute and decided funding and admission. Dwight's notes show him approving research, increasing investment, assigning researchers to labs and receiving reports about members.

History: The Institute was a research body led by Dwight Lasker. During a cataclysm about five hundred years ago Dwight closed it for the safety of its people and kept the young from going to fight, urging post-disaster reconstruction first.

After the flood period began, he picked land near the Fountain of Lucine to relocate, only to hear that an opera house would be built there. He later met a newly appointed Iudex and judged him far more reliable than "Leon and those other clowns". Alain introduced Rene and Jakob Ingold, who turned out to be Karl's adopted sons; Dwight enrolled them and assigned them to Alain's lab despite the unrest it caused among other researchers.

Alain's research on clockwork meka and Khaenri'ah war machines led to the invention of Arkhe energy systems, called Pneumousia energy, which Dwight called the greatest breakthrough in a century. Rene then asked to run a separate study on the Abyss, using Durin's blood, Elynas's remains and Dark Mud, to fight toxins left in Fontaine's water; Dwight approved it, since deformed Oceanids were appearing. Dwight also received a report that the leaders were forming a group around a "Master" and tasked his friend Emanuel to investigate.

A line in the Ordo's history says Rene gathered followers from this Institute, with Jakob performing tricks to convince people to join the new Ordo. Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin refused to join. Dwight's own fate is not recorded.

Culture: The surviving texts mix science with legend, for example the origin of the Oceanids from Egeria's tear. The Institute valued child prodigies; Dwight says it is its responsibility to support gifted and talented youths.

Quests: Aqueous Tidemarks (4.0): the Traveler follows Virgil to find the Liliacruces Forum's treasure, discovers the Institute, defeats clockwork meka and a Ruin Guard, solves a key puzzle, and fights a "special" Ruin Grader in a vault before breaking a glass wall and following a current.

The wiki lists the Institute as the subarea of the 4.2 World Quest Search in the Algae Sea, part of the Narzissenkreuz questline.

Status as of 7.1: Still flooded and abandoned. Its documents remain, and its oldest dangers are guarded by meka.

Nothing newer than 4.2 is known to have changed it.

Dangers: Hydro Slimes, Area Alert Mek - Ousia, armored and sternshield crabs, Hunter's Rays, a Ruin Guard, a Ruin Grader, and non-respawning Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps.

Atmosphere: Cold blue light, silt and ruined laboratory rooms. The viewpoint text calls the place "Sunken Glory". It feels like a proud institution caught mid-argument.

134.comment: Institute of Natural Philosophy: Ancient Notes of Director Dwight Lasker
134.content: A run of fragmentary notes, undated and out of order, written by the Director. They mention relocation, the opera house, a newly appointed Iudex, Alain's meka work, enrolments and the discovery of Pneumousia energy. The sequence of events here is partly reconstructed on the wiki.

135.comment: Institute of Natural Philosophy: Ancient Natural History Excerpts (Oceanids)
135.content: Excerpts of a natural-history text say that, by legend, Egeria shed the first tear and from it the first Oceanid was born, with the task of understanding all life. Oceanids differ greatly in intelligence and multiply by a mysterious "Helixsplit" after seeking permission from the Hydro Archon or an elder. A sceptical addendum notes that physical evidence suggests the Oceanids predate both Egeria and Remuria, and asks whether anyone dares explore their true origin.

136.comment: Institute of Natural Philosophy: Ancient Investigative Report (the Master)
136.content: A report in the deepest room mentions a suspected association among leaders and a "Master". The group is vigilant about outside investigation but not aggressive, so no official action was taken, and the writer suspects the Institute may be the hub.

137.content:
Lepaute Horlogerie: Lepaute Horlogerie is a clock shop in Quartier Lyonnais, owned by Caron. Horlogerie is French for clockmaking, and the shop stands near his older brother Livre's toy workshop.

Caron designs clocks and makes clockwork toys as a side business. Armand also appears at the shop.

Places: In Quartier Lyonnais, between Livre's workshop and the Fontaine branch of the Northland Bank on the same street.

People: Caron owns it. Armand is also found at the shop and stammers when he greets visitors; his role is not stated.

Caron's elder brother Livre owns Leschots Clockwork Workshop nearby.

History: During the Mega Meka Melee event in 4.0, Caron's new toy sparked a rivalry with Livre's workshop. In the final quest, The Toy War: An Armistice, the brothers speak openly; Caron says that although Bennett gave him key inspiration, Livre was the real reason he insisted on the adventurer toy.

The name Lepaute may allude to historical French clockmaking brothers, echoing Caron and his brother Livre; this is a wiki etymology guess.

Atmosphere: A clockmaker's shop with a rival workshop a few steps away.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

138.content:
Leschots Clockwork Workshop (also: Leschots's workshop, Leschots Clockwork Shop): Leschots Clockwork Workshop is a toy shop in Quartier Lyonnais run by Livre, who makes mechanical clockwork toys.

The workshop sells toy birds, puppets, clockwork horses, trumpet-blowing blubberbeasts and penguins. The penguin designs are consignments by Freminet, whom Livre admires.

Places: In Quartier Lyonnais, next to the Fontaine Northland Bank and Lepaute Horlogerie, run by his younger brother Caron.

People: Livre is the boss; Alberre and Arbon are staff. Freminet is commissioned for toy designs.

Livre once considered inviting Freminet to develop toys but did not press when the boy stayed silent.

History: In the Mega Meka Melee event (4.0), staff asked the Traveler to collect data for a Champion Duelist plan for a new toy line. The brothers' rivalry with Caron comes to a head in later acts and they talk openly in the final one.

The name Leschots may allude to Swiss watchmakers; the wiki mentions one who worked with the Jaquet-Droz automata makers. This is a guess, not canon.

Atmosphere: A toy shop full of clockwork creatures and a friendly sibling rivalry.

Status as of 7.1: Open at the cutoff (7.1).

139.content:
Liffey Region (also: Liffey): The Liffey Region is the part of Fontaine's map that holds the Fortress of Meropide, an underwater stronghold that serves as Fontaine's de facto prison and largest maker of Clockwork Meka. Its Administrator is Wriothesley, and the infirmary is run by Sigewinne. Foothills on the east side of Mont Esus also belong to the region.

Its boss is the Millennial Pearl Seahorse. The area is the setting for much of Archon Quest Chapter IV, Acts III to V, and a long run of world quests called Scenes from Life in Meropide.

Geography: The Fortress sits beneath the waters behind the Opera Epiclese and is reached by a lift down River Talionis. Around and inside it lie an Administrative Area, a Production Zone and an Abandoned Production Zone, a Forbidden Zone, a Geode Mine Shaft and a Dormitory Block. Mont Esus East is the eastern foothills of Mont Esus, which cannot currently be entered.

The Rift of Erosion lies west of the Dormitory Block and is described by an NPC as a potential danger. The Qualifications Review Representative Office and Bravais' Press Works are further marked buildings.

Places: - **Fortress of Meropide**: autonomous underwater stronghold; its own building entry gives full detail.
- **Administrative Area / The Duke's Office**: the offices of Administrator Wriothesley.
- **Production Zone and Abandoned Production Zone**: the factory parts of the Fortress; Clockwork Meka are made here.
- **Forbidden Zone**: a restricted area sealed since ancient times, closed to everyone except the warden and trusted people.
- **Pankration Ring**, **Coupon Cafeteria** and **Rag and Bone Shop** are other marked sites inside the Fortress.

- **Bravais' Press Works**: a marked workplace whose posted texts include Forging Press Device Operation Standards, a Maintenance Log and an Emergency Handbook (third edition).
- **Qualifications Review Representative Office**: a marked office whose notices include an External Reconstruction Support FAQ and a Project Proposal.
- **Mont Esus East**: foothills only.

People: Wriothesley is the Fortress's Administrator and Sigewinne, a Melusine nurse, works in its infirmary. Inmates, guards and staff appear throughout the Scenes from Life in Meropide quests. Outside the Fortress, Gardes provide some security support.

In the Archon Quest the Traveler enters as an 'inmate' on trumped-up charges; Act V recalls a 45-day sentence.

Governance: Technically an autonomous entity governing itself and outside Fontaine's legal system: criminals sent there are in effect exiles, and the Court of Fontaine only sends some Gardes to help with security. Wriothesley is its Administrator.

History: According to the wiki's compilation of the Fortress's lore, a group of exiled criminals first built it after Egeria began her rule in Fontaine. Shunned by society, some of them begged for mercy; Egeria heard them and told them to help protect her secret beneath the waves. The 'secret' was an entrance to the Primordial Sea, which they sealed and labelled the Forbidden Zone.

The wiki says later groups of exiles continued the work even after the first group had died.

In Archon Quest Chapter IV, Neuvillette sends the Traveler to the Fortress on trumped-up charges to investigate (Act III, 4.1). At the start of Act V (4.2), when the Traveler's 45-day stay ends and the prison shakes, Wriothesley says the seal Neuvillette placed earlier would not fail, so the tremor must come from the surface. In Act IV, Calamitous Tread, the Traveler passes through the Infirmary, cafeteria, dormitories, an office and the Forbidden Zone.

Atmosphere: The official map blurb calls the Fortress a metal-walled fastness that has kept a great many secrets over long years.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers, Treasure Hoarders and Clockwork Meka; the Frost and Wind Operatives and Fatui Pyro Agents are elite foes. The Millennial Pearl Seahorse is the region's boss.

Travel: The lift behind the Opera Epiclese down to River Talionis is unlocked in A Tea Party Most Thorny (4.1). The wiki lists several ways to enter the Fortress for the first time; the Archon Quest sends the Traveler in as an 'inmate'.

Quests: Archon Quest quests filed under the region include Fortress of Meropide (Act III), Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, Calamitous Tread (Act IV), and Deluge of Wrathful Waters (Act V's first quest). The wiki also lists the Scenes from Life in Meropide series, Both Brains and Brawn, Underground Crime, Into the Sunlight, A Moment's Respite, The Proud 'Beret Society' and Wriothesley: Quite the Win.

Part of the Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles, such as Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble, also touches this region.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Fortress still operates under Wriothesley and Sigewinne.

Nothing newer than 4.2 was found for this area.

140.content:
A restricted area at the heart of the Fortress, closed to everyone except the warden and trusted individuals. The wiki's lore text says it hides an entrance to the Primordial Sea that the first exiles sealed at Egeria's request. A separate Rift of Erosion lies west of the Dormitory Block and is called a potential danger.

At the start of Act V Wriothesley reminds the Traveler that the seal Neuvillette placed earlier would not fail, and says the tremor they felt came from the surface.

141.content: The eastern foothills of Mont Esus, a mountain that is currently inaccessible. It belongs to the Liffey Region.

142.content:
Loch Urania (also: Urania Lake): Loch Urania is a lake in Erinnyes Forest, Fontaine, containing a large water vortex that forms a big bubble at the top. It starts out tainted by contaminated bacterial mats; clearing them calms the water and the sky.

It is the starting place of the world quest Furious Mouth of the Spring, part of The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes, where an enraged vishap and a small Melusine called Pahsiv guard a "key".

Geography: A lake in Erinnyes Forest with a giant vortex whose top forms a bubble. An altar sits near the "mouth of the spring" in the water, with a vishap lying beside it.

While tainted, strong high-speed winds push travellers away and the sky is dark even in daytime. The contaminated cores can only be cleansed with the abilities of Xenochromatic Creatures; after the lake is cleared the winds fade and the sky brightens.

Cleansing the two Contaminated Bacterial Mats in the water is one way to start Furious Mouth of the Spring; completing the nearby quests Foggy Forest Path or Wilting Weeping Willow also starts it.

Dangers: The enraged Primordial Bathysmal Vishap by the altar attacks anyone who disturbs the altar. Before cleansing, the winds make approaching difficult.

The vishap is a guardian of the key rather than a villain: Pahsiv says a "purple thing" stole a key and left it fainted, and she calms it with a touch.

Quests: Furious Mouth of the Spring (World Quest, 4.2) begins here. The Traveler subdues the vishap and meets Pahsiv, who speaks in a few repeated words. She asks for help gathering three keys (misty path to the south, the spring to the north, willows to the east) and taking them to the square in the west, to protect Erinnyes. The quest has variants depending on how many Teardrop Keys the player already has.

Pahsiv calls Erinnyes her home, though Melusine are normally associated with the Court of Fontaine and Merusea Village. She mentions a "visitor" who teaches her language and wisdom; the visitor's identity belongs to the later Erinnyes questline.

Status as of 7.1: Calm and navigable once cleansed; no later change is recorded as of 7.1.

143.content: Pahsiv is the name Paimon gives a small Melusine met at Loch Urania who speaks in short fragments ("Pahsiv" works as yes and "Melusine" as no in her usage). She guards keys with the vishap and asks the Traveler to help protect Erinnyes. She is a quest character; do not expand her beyond the quest.

144.content:
Lumidouce Harbor (also: Port de Lumidouce): Lumidouce Harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built into the side of a waterfall in Fontaine's Erinnyes Forest, much like Romaritime Harbor. It is a vital trading port for Fontaine, handling a large volume of international cargo, including tea from Qiaoying Village in Liyue and spices from Sumeru. For some years it has been underfunded and worn down, with its planned expansion and aquabus line stalled.

It also serves as a transfer point for illegal goods, and a few underground groups hold influence among the docks.

Geography: The harbor is a coastal elevator and observation deck built on the side of a waterfall. A run-down tavern, "The Rusty Rudder", stands a short distance northwest of it, and the lower levels and the ships there are where underground trading takes place.

Because the harbor has neglected its routine hydrological surveys, its maps of the complex underwater terrain are out of date, which makes it harder for navigators to guide ships safely.

Places: The main deck and elevator are where most harbor staff work. "The Rusty Rudder" tavern is where employees gather after work and where shady dealings are arranged. A noticeboard next to Cassigneul carries staff complaints, trade adverts and notices.

Below the harbor, around Chaussivert's ship, is where the underground trade is arranged. The follow-up world quest sends the Traveler to Nacker's hideout in the Fort Charybdis ruins.

People: Cassigneul is the Lumidouce Harbor General Manager and handles the staff's complaints; she has promised to pay salaries from her own pocket if she has to. Others include the traders and staff Afsoon, Chourei, Crapet, Hilmer, Jalade, Kimpel, Mermet, Xing Cheng and, after An Expected Lie, Chaussivert, Fusilier and Lemarcq.

Chaussivert is a self-proclaimed "Harbor-Watcher" with a strict personal code; he refuses dirty money and is said to run the largest underground trading operation. His position has weakened since he lost his entire crew except Lemarcq. Mr. Doutey, the former overseer, wanted to expand the port but left, apparently for a posting elsewhere.

Governance: Day-to-day administration falls to Cassigneul, who took over from Doutey; the Maison Cardinalice is the body whose promised works (expansion, the aquabus line) have not started. The Spina di Rosula watches the balance of power among the underground groups and grew worried when senior members of the Club di Pantaloni Novita crime organisation were all arrested.

Don Pesci and De Niro families, as well as the former Club di Pantaloni Novita, are named as underground factions that hold or held sway at the harbor.

History: Until a few years before 4.2, Mr. Doutey oversaw the harbor and planned to expand it for ever-increasing trade. A fourth aquabus line connecting it to the Court of Fontaine was also designed, but was suspended after the death of Callas, its chief financial backer. Around then an unnamed event (probably related) led many employees, most of the navigators and Doutey himself to leave, and Cassigneul was assigned to replace him.

In the roughly three years since, the harbor has been in crisis, mostly for lack of investment. The share of foreign ships has risen, hinting at a trade imbalance, and cargo is increasing while infrastructure is not. Neither the expansion nor the revival of the line has progressed, despite the Maison Cardinalice's assurances of an imminent start to work.

Engineers are idle and discontented, and some seek jobs elsewhere, for example with Hautemontagne at Yilong Wharf. Navigators are overworked and underpaid, and a posting here is called "practically a black hole for career progression." Staff also complain of a lack of nearby recreation and shops.

Atmosphere: Working at the harbor is currently very safe and uneventful, perhaps because there are so few jobs, and the busy trade of a major port sits uneasily beside idle engineers and unfinished plans. The in-game viewpoint is titled "A Distant Harbor"; the sound of the waterfall surrounds the elevators and decks.

Dangers: Chiefly smuggling and crooked deals rather than open fighting. The harbor has been a key transfer point for illicit goods, such as imitation Sinthe. According to Chaussivert, bribery, fraud and betrayal have declined recently.

Travel: The harbor lies in Erinnyes Forest. No aquabus runs there yet: the Lumidouce Harbor line is planned but unbuilt. Tea from Liyue's Qiaoying Village and spices from Sumeru pass through it.

Quests: The world quests An Expected Plan and An Expected Lie (both 4.2) begin here and follow the Traveler and Chaussivert's crew in tracing a suspicious shipment and the missing researcher Nacker; they continue the Fontaine Research Institute story. Several quests and noticeboard threads touch on the harbor's trade and smuggling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lumidouce Harbor is still a stagnant but working port. No later canon changes its state.

Its expansion and aquabus line remain stalled, and staff are still short. Cassigneul keeps the harbor running on promises and her own pocket.

145.comment: Lumidouce Harbor: Chaussivert and the Harbor-Watcher's Crew
145.content:
Chaussivert is the self-styled "Harbor-Watcher" of Lumidouce Harbor, a man of strict honesty who refuses dirty money. In An Expected Plan the Traveler meets him while chasing Nacker, who nearly blew up the Fontaine Research Institute; Chaussivert had been asked to smuggle someone out of Fontaine and refused. After the Traveler beats him in a scuffle, he helps track the shipment with his crew. He later loses his crew, apart from Lemarcq.

The quest chain ends with the capture of Nacker and the discovery that the researcher Edwin Eastinghouse, believed dead, was still alive. Chaussivert and Lemarcq are compensated by the Institute and return to the harbor.

146.content: "The Rusty Rudder" is a run-down tavern northwest of Lumidouce Harbor where shady deals are made and people who are down on their luck gather. Harbor employees also drink there after work.

147.content:
Marcotte Station: Marcotte Station is the terminus of the aquabus Navia Line, serving the Erinnyes area.

Riders from the Court Region Waterway Hub take the Navia Line, run by Elphane, to reach it. The Opera Epiclese is the other stop on the same line.

Travel: It is reached by the Navia Line from the Court of Fontaine main station; the line was named for Navia and its planning followed her mother's death.

The Aquabus page notes that two further planned lines were never built.

Status as of 7.1: Active at the cutoff (7.1).

Quests associated with the area are listed under Marcotte Station on the wiki; canon gives few other details.

148.content:
Mary-Ann Memorial Park: Mary-Ann Memorial Park is a small, once scenic park just south of the Central Laboratory Ruins, in the area of Fontaine given over to the Fontaine Research Institute. Most of its buildings were destroyed by the explosion that levelled the old Institute. Beneath its shallow pond lies Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory.

The park is where researchers pick through surviving papers in the quest "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble" and where malfunctioning meka attack in "A Letter".

Geography: Lies directly south of the Central Laboratory Ruins in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region. It is a park laid out around a shallow pond, with broken machines, pipes, canvas sheets and storage drums strewn across it. Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory is under the pond.

Nacker explains that the park was hit by the first shock waves of the explosion, which is why most of its structures are gone. The surviving debris includes wrecked equipment, old copies of the newspaper The Steambird and financial reports that are long out of date.

People: Nacker, a former senior researcher who survived the disaster, leads the party through the park in the quest, together with the reporter Chronie and the Traveler. Chronie notes that before "Edwin's big screw-up" Nacker had been second only to Edwin Eastinghouse at the Institute.

Nacker answers that nothing like his past status remains; he calls himself someone lucky to have survived the project and one of the culprits who turned the Central Laboratory into what it is. His job now is to retrieve assets, and he rates his own worth by that work.

History: The park's own origins are not told. It was damaged in the Institute explosion; the quest of 4.1 sends Nacker, Chronie and the Traveler to look for paper assets that may have survived. They find mostly detritus, plus one set of experimental results for a miniaturized personal recording device that Nacker expects will interest Maillardet, who has long wanted tiny gramophones inside Artificed Dancers.

The wiki suggests the park was dedicated to Mary-Ann Guillotin, sister of the Institute's founder Alain Guillotin. This is an inference, not a stated fact.

Quests: "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble" (Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles, 4.1) passes through the park while recovering assets. "A Letter" (4.1) sends the Traveler here to defeat three malfunctioning Recon Log Mek - Ousia before heading to the Academic Assembly Hall. The Daily Commission "Ardent Calibration" (4.1 to 4.2 per the wiki) is also set here.

Chronie loses her bag to a strange-looking meka in the park, and the Traveler defeats it; she asks why such meka move at times and stop at others. Nacker says anyone who might answer is indisposed.

"A Letter" begins at the New Fontaine Research Institute, where Choiseul refuses to hand a document to Iaune of the Maison Gestion because the letter delivery regulations forbid it. Iaune, whom the Traveler once helped, thanks them; Choiseul notes that the Traveler is an Honorary Senior Researcher of the Institute. The Traveler is sent to the park to clear malfunctioning meka and then photographs the Academic Assembly Hall for Iaune.

Dangers: Malfunctioning clockwork meka, such as Recon Log Meks, roam the ruined grounds.

Atmosphere: Half a park and half a ruin: a pond and plants beside twisted pipes and crates, with a stillness left behind by the blast.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the park remains ruined and can be explored in the game. No rebuilding of the park or of the Central Laboratory is documented.

149.comment: Mary-Ann Memorial Park: Bossuet's Abandoned Laboratory
149.content: An abandoned laboratory beneath the shallow pond of Mary-Ann Memorial Park. The wiki gives no description of its purpose or history beyond its location, so it should be treated as an unexplained corner of the Institute's grounds.

150.content:
Administrative Area (also: Meropide Administrative Area, Fortress of Meropide Administrative Area): The Administrative Area is the central hub of the Fortress of Meropide, the undersea prison-factory in Fontaine. The Duke's Office, belonging to the Administrator Wriothesley, stands at its centre. The Fortress's teleport waypoint is here, across from the office. Guards, inmates, shopkeepers and the doctor all pass through it.

Credit Coupons are the only currency, and the area contains the places where they are spent.

Geography: It lies below the Dormitory Block and above the Production Zone. The Duke's Office stands in its middle, and a waypoint opens across from it once the Fortress's first quest is under way. A lift from the area leads to the Pankration Ring.

The Fortress's map levels are the Reception Area, Dormitory Block, Administrative Area, Production Zone (upper and lower) and Abandoned Production Zone. The wiki lists both the Dormitory Block and the Administrative Area as map levels of this page.

Places: The Duke's Office has three floors: the Duke's own office on top with a desk, sofa and tea table, and a basement with a lift to the Forbidden Zone and a door onto a glass-walled room overlooking the secret ship. The Coupon Cafeteria serves meals and the free daily Welfare Meal. The Rag and Bone Shop is owned by Alvard. The Pankration Ring is the Fortress's entertainment venue.

Near the waypoint three notices hang on the wall: one offers 10 Coupons for Welfare Meals and fortune slips (apply at Supply Warehouse 2), one calls for people to join in destroying the loudspeaker, and one grumbles about a day wasted and a bowl of Minty Bean Soup. Maupoli's job is tearing down notices like these.

Inside the area a blackboard, table and bookshelf change after the quest An Eye for an Eye: before, the blackboard shows basic knowledge that children could understand and the table holds story books, detective novels and papers from the Fontaine Research Institute; afterwards the blackboard shows economic principles and some sociology and the table holds books on economics. A pressed purple flower in the storybook is replaced by a faint scent.

People: Named NPCs include Alvard (Rag and Bone Shop owner), Arderne (doctor), Bran (Coupon Cafeteria staff, a clockwork meka), Wolsey (cafeteria supervisor), Monglane (receptionist), guards Camden, Estienne, Galvana, Galvaryet and Goncourt, Millereau (Mutual Aid Network advertiser), and Edwin Eastinghouse, a former senior researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute.

Others in the area are Nakul (researcher), Nizami (bodyguard), Nacker (former Fontaine Research Institute researcher), Darcy (called 'Dirty Face'), Carranza, Fourmon, Lutz, Meilhat, Ottnit and Rosolino, as well as unnamed convicts. 'Tricky Bulle Fruit', a former Fruity Order operative, and 'Intrepid Valberry' are also listed.

Governance: Wriothesley governs the Fortress from the central office. The Fortress is formally autonomous and runs on Coupons rather than Mora. The area is where the Coupon economy is felt: the cafeteria and the Rag and Bone Shop are here.

Culture: Notices by the waypoint show daily inmate life: bargains for Welfare Meals, grumbling about food and a call to wreck the loudspeaker. Pankration bouts are held in the Ring, and Millereau advertises the Mutual Aid Network in the area.

History: The area is the setting for the Traveler's 45-day sentence in Chapter IV Acts III-IV and the Fortress is also the setting of Wriothesley's story quest (4.1). In Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, Wriothesley opens the hidden stair in his office to the Forbidden Zone.

Dangers: No specific hazards are described here. Guards are posted in the area, and Pankration bouts take place in the Ring.

Atmosphere: Industrial and busy, with notices on the walls and a loudspeaker. The Duke's door is often shut tight, yet its map description says he knows everything that happens in the Fortress.

Travel: Reached through the Fortress's reception, via a waypoint that appears in the first Fortress quest, or by being caught by searchlights outside. It connects downward by lift to the Production Zone.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of 7.1, with Wriothesley as Administrator.

151.content: Three notices hang by the waypoint. A ten-Coupon offer for Welfare Meals and fortune slips points to Supply Warehouse 2. A second reads 'Join us, and destroy the loudspeaker!' A third grumbles about wasting a day on a bowl of disgusting Minty Bean Soup. Maupoli, whose job it is to take the notices down, thanks the Traveler for doing it and hands over 30 Coupons.

152.content:
Production Zone (also: Meropide Production Zone, Fortress of Meropide Production Zone): The Production Zone is the work area of the Fortress of Meropide. It has two levels below the Administrative Area, joined by a lift in the east of the Fortress. Inmates work here, and further below, through a lift in the lower level, lies the Abandoned Production Zone.

The Fortress is described as Fontaine's largest maker of clockwork meka.

Geography: An Upper Level and a Lower Level, connected by a lift. A pool of water with wooden crates sits in the centre of the Production Zone. The Lower Level has a teleport waypoint and a lift down to the Abandoned Production Zone.

The Abandoned Production Zone has four paths whose doors are controlled by a central drive valve. They lead to Supply Warehouse 1, the Geode Mine Shaft, the Energy Storage Warehouse and Supply Warehouse 2. A notice says all work related to the Geode Mine Shaft has been suspended and the connecting paths sealed. Opening one for official business requires a technical expert to operate the drive valve.

Places: Upper Level residents include Clynes, Grainville, Irus and Nelly. The Lower Level has Lechlade and Maupoil. A pool at the centre has three empty wooden crates; Grainville thanks anyone who clears them, because keeping the place clean counts as maintaining order, and gives Coupons.

During evacuation in Calamitous Tread, guards at the Lower Level lift tell people to leave immediately and go up and out.

In Wriothesley's story quest he deduces that Dougier bribed an overseer and heads to the Production Zone with the Traveler. They find an unconscious guard and some society members here, and one of them points them to the Beret Society's real headquarters, where Gardemeks and signs of missing clockwork meka confirm Wriothesley's suspicions.

People: The wiki's NPC list, without titles, is Clynes, Grainville, Irus, Nelly (Upper Level), Lechlade and Maupoil (Lower Level).

Governance: Under the Administrator's authority. Inmates earn Credit Coupons by working.

Culture: Work is how inmates earn their Coupons, and Grainville's thanks show the Fortress's habit of rewarding small tasks with Coupons.

History: The zone appears in the world only from 4.1. The Abandoned Production Zone is closed off, with the Geode Mine Shaft suspended.

Dangers: No hazards are listed on the zone's page. During the Cerberus Chapter, Beret Society members were found here, and during the breach in Calamitous Tread guards at the Lower Level lift ordered everyone to evacuate upward and outward.

Atmosphere: Industrial and enclosed, a factory floor with water standing in the middle of it.

Travel: Take the lift in the east of the Fortress down from the Administrative Area.

Quests: Appears in Reborn in the Land of Grievances (Wriothesley's Cerberus Chapter Act I) and in the Archon Quest evacuation in Calamitous Tread (4.1).

Status as of 7.1: Operating as the Fortress's factory floor as of 7.1.

153.content: Grainville asks the Traveler to clear three empty wooden crates from the water in the middle of the zone, telling them that a sanitary environment is part of maintaining order. As thanks, he gives a Common Chest with 2 Primogems and 30 Credit Coupons.

154.content:
Merusea Village (also: home of the Melusines, Melusine village): Merusea Village is the home of the Melusines, the small amphibious all-female people of Fontaine. It lies underwater, inside the body of the dead beast Elynas, and the game calls it "an adorable and mysterious village where even the chimneys bubble". It has no official leader. Very few humans ever visit, but those who do tend to enjoy it.

The village can be entered only from underwater, by diving near Elynas' skull or in the pool just above the Beryl Region Statue of the Seven. Most Melusines live here, though many who work in the Court of Fontaine now live in the city.

Geography: Merusea Village has a northern zone (on land, where most villagers are found) and a southern zone (underwater), within the colossal remains of Elynas that fill nearly all of the Beryl Region. Local plants include the Romaritime Flower and Beryl Conch.

Elynas' skeleton and body are far larger than those of the dragon Orobashi. The Melusines' homes and the village itself are inside his remains.

Places: The village has human-inspired structures made long ago by the Melusines: street lamps (installed because visitors found the space darker than they were used to) and swing sets. A vendor, Xana, trades goods for mechanical "components".

Melusines treat scrap mechanical parts as currency because of their abundance and prettiness; they exchange them for goods and give them to each other as tokens of thanks.

People: Residents include Serene, Cosanzeana, Flo, Iara, Laume, Lutine, Rufina, Sedile, Sluasi, Verenata and Virda on land, and Glaisti, Granna, Puca and Thirona underwater. Xana is the vendor. Mamere, the artist, is a Melusine from here who could hear Elynas.

Serene, one of the older Melusines, regards herself as the village's "big sister" and takes responsibility for daily affairs. Melusines generally have strong senses and a sense of justice, and are not strong fighters; some are skilled with rifles.

Governance: There is no official leader. Serene handles day-to-day matters informally.

Culture: Melusines eat Tidalga but also enjoy human food, and adore the Breacher Primuses that share Elynas' body. They respect Neuvillette as their ideal "father". A Newsstand Board notice in the Court of Fontaine says bathing in the waters around the village is calming and leaves skin soft and smooth.

A world quest in 6.3, A Gift From the Sea Spirits, shows the villagers secretly preparing a handmade outfit as a gift for Neuvillette, who often sends gifts to everyone in the village. Every Melusine is born with a different token, a mechanical memento.

History: About 400 years ago, in the battle between the Marechaussee Hunters and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo inside Elynas' remains, an explosion killed many and drove the mechanical parts of clockwork meka through the beast's body. The Melusines were born from those wounds, and Elynas, who was dead but still conscious, regarded them as his daughters and taught them how to make a home: Merusea Village.

According to Carole, the Melusines lived in the village for almost twenty years before they met Neuvillette, who answered their wish and brought them to the Court of Fontaine. Fontainians were wary of Melusines at first, and Neuvillette's reforms and Carole's death led people to trust them.

Later the Melusines could no longer hear Elynas, except Mamere. In the Ancient Colors quests, Jakob (by then an Iniquitous Baptist) tried to revive Elynas by collecting his blood, which Elynas did not want because his revival would crush the Melusines' homes. The Traveler stopped him, and Elynas thanked them.

Atmosphere: Bubbling chimneys, handmade street lamps and swing sets: the village feels gentle, secluded and a little strange. It was dark enough that the Melusines added lamps for human visitors, who tend to enjoy their stay.

Dangers: The village is safe for Melusines, since Breacher Primuses do not attack them, but the waters around Elynas' remains hold Breacher Primuses and Consecrated Beasts. Jakob's attempts to restart Elynas' heart once threatened the village.

Travel: Only from underwater: dive near Elynas' skull or into the pool above the Beryl Region Statue of the Seven. Humans seldom come.

Quests: Ancient Colors (4.0), also called Seymour's Story: Prologue, centres on Mamere, her friend the clockwork meka Seymour and Elynas. A Gift From the Sea Spirits (6.3) follows the villagers' present for Neuvillette. Melusines also feature in many Court of Fontaine quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Merusea Village remains a hidden, peaceful Melusine home with no leader. No later canon changes its state.

Elynas remains dead and his heart has not been restarted. Many Melusines live and work in the Court, and some visit the village on holiday.

155.content:
Elynas is the vast creature whose remains hold Merusea Village. The Melusines call him "Father". An Abyss-infused creation of Rhinedottir (per the wiki's reading of the quest), he loved exploring the world but realised that his happiness hurt others, and he let himself die. After death he kept his consciousness and craved company. He thinks of the Melusines as his children, though most can no longer hear his voice.

During the cataclysm the Fontaine Armada pursued him for about 35 days before he bled out. The wiki records that Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold later entered his body and Jakob took his blood, which made him an Iniquitous Baptist. Elynas considered them friends. The Breacher Primuses protect his body like cells.

156.content: Serene is an indigo-skinned Melusine with short brown hair and red eyes, one of the older villagers, who sees herself as the others' big sister. Her open-world dialogue shows her helping with everyone's troubles.

157.content:
Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnéqui, Automnequi): Mont Automnequi is one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, a mountain that straddles two regions: its west slopes lie in the Belleau Region and its east slopes in the Morte Region. Much of Fontaine is covered by water, but this is one of the places where mountain and forest show through. From its heights one can look across to the ridge of Elynas and the lakes beneath which the Melusines' homeland is hidden.

A tunnel, the Poisson Tunnel, was dug through the west side so that the Clementine Line of the aquabus system could pass, a feat of the Fontaine Research Institute.

Geography: Mont Automnequi spans the Belleau Region (the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi, released in 4.0) and the Morte Region (the East Slopes, released in 4.2). The west side faces the coast where half of the wrecked Sponsian lies, with the Elton Trench just offshore and the ridge of Elynas across the water.

Local specialties on the west slopes are Lumidouce Bell and Rainbow Rose. The east side belongs to the Morte Region, whose name is French for "dead"; that region as a whole offers Condessence Crystal, Spring of the First Dewdrop, Lumidouce Bell, Rainbow Rose and Romaritime Flower. The wiki gives no separate lore for the east slopes.

Places: Poisson Tunnel on the west slopes; a stretch of coast where wreckage of the Sponsian can be found; and, nearby, the Elton Trench offshore. The viewpoint "View From Mont Automnequi" stands on the west slopes.

Wooden-and-masonry dwellings called Automnequi's Watch stand on the west slopes; they are a common countryside building in Fontaine, easy to maintain and build, and do not need specialists to repair.

People: The only NPC the wiki lists on the west slopes is Antoine. Treasure Hoarders also roam there.

History: The Fontaine Research Institute brought in huge engineering devices to bore the Poisson Tunnel, which the official map text calls one of the biggest challenges in building the aquabus lines. The wiki records that new machines, including the "Golden Vessel", were developed for the job.

The tunnel's success pushed a new generation of clockwork technology, including the Construction Specialist Mek, which was modelled on the Golden Vessel. During construction on the Clementine Line, engineers had to stay near the tunnel to repair malfunctioning clockwork meka at any time, so they built houses patterned on local dwellings; the houses, Automnequi's Watch, are said to have withstood intense earthquakes and stand upright years after the engineers left.

Long before she became Admiral, Basil Elton (who lived about 500 years ago) is said to have driven off an Emperor of Fire and Iron that was attacking a ship, sending it back to the depths; that creature is the boss of the west slopes. One half of her flagship Sponsian, wrecked in the fleet's last battle against Elynas, lies on a beach nearby.

Atmosphere: Broad vistas of lakes, sea and the ridge of Elynas, rugged slopes of mountain and forest unusual in a land mostly covered by water, and clockwork meks and the engineers' tunnel as reminders of Fontaine's technology.

Dangers: Hilichurls (including Hilichurl Berserkers), Large Hydro Slimes, Treasure Hoarders of several kinds, and clockwork Meks (Area Alert, Geological Survey, Suppression Specialist and Recon Log). Elite foes on the west slopes are Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Hydro Hilichurl Rogues and Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasms, and the Emperor of Fire and Iron is the area's boss.

Travel: The Clementine Line aquabus passes through the Poisson Tunnel under the west slopes. The mountain itself spans the Belleau Region and the Morte Region.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing new has been reported on the mountain; it remains accessible and quiet.

158.comment: Mont Automnequi: Poisson Tunnel and the Clementine Line
158.content: The Poisson Tunnel carves through the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi so the Clementine Line of the aquabus network can run. The Fontaine Research Institute bored it with huge engines including the legendary "Golden Vessel", and the project led to the Construction Specialist Mek and a new generation of clockwork technology.

159.content: A traditional country dwelling mixing wood and masonry, seen on the west side of Mont Automnequi and in Fontaine's countryside generally. It is far less durable than the large Tearstone buildings or the slag-cement houses of the Court of Fontaine, but is easy to repair. Engineers building the Clementine Line tunnel built these houses patterned on local homes, and they stand to this day.

160.content:
Mont Esus (also: Esus): Mont Esus is a very large mountain in Fontaine, north-west of the Court of Fontaine. It appears in the in-game expedition menu but cannot be visited. What players can see is its foothills by the sea close to Palais Mermonia, a gentle landscape of wide flower fields, and its eastern foothills, which form the Mont Esus East subarea.

Fontaine's official expedition text speaks of a magnificent palace, now gone, that once stood among the flowers.

Geography: The mountain lies north-west of the Court of Fontaine. Its foothills run down to the sea near Palais Mermonia, where a gentle breeze crosses broad fields of flowers. The eastern foothills are reachable as the Mont Esus East subarea of the Liffey Region. The mountain itself is the only expedition location in the game that is not accessible.

According to the wiki, the mountain's backdrop is higher than the Celestial Nail on Dragonspine and gives a view across most of Teyvat, from Mondstadt to Nod-Krai, except Inazuma. Treat this as an observation of the in-game scenery rather than a stated fact.

Mont Esus East consists of the eastern foothills of the mountain and sits in the Liffey Region; its wiki page keeps "before" and "after" images dated to Version 4.6, so the area was visibly changed then, but the pages read do not say how or why. The wiki lists a fishing point there but no lore text.

Places: The flowery meadows by the foothills are where the viewpoint "Memories of Mont Esus" stands (a windmill turns lazily in the breeze); it appears after completing the Court of Fontaine Region quest "Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste". The Mont Esus East foothills are a separate subarea.

History: According to ancient records cited in the expedition text, a magnificent palace was once built here. It was named after the flowers and meant to sing praises of love and to nurture abandoned orphans above the countless waters. The high tower of old no longer stands, but the flowers remain as fragrant as ever.

The palace is not named in the text, and no source ties it to a specific institution; do not state which one it was.

Atmosphere: Gentle breezes, flower fields stretching to the sea, a lazy windmill, and a sense of peaceful memory. The viewpoint text says the relaxed mood makes people dwell on pleasant memories; it adds that Salsa once painted the scenery here.

Travel: The mountain cannot be entered. The viewpoint over the foothills is in the Court of Fontaine Region, and the eastern foothills belong to the Liffey Region as Mont Esus East.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mont Esus is still a distant, inaccessible peak. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content changed that.

161.comment: Mont Esus: Memories of Mont Esus (viewpoint)
161.content: A viewpoint in the Court of Fontaine Region among flowery meadows, with a windmill whose arms creak and turn in the breeze. It unlocks after completing the quest "Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste (Court of Fontaine Region)". The text says Salsa once painted the scenery, and that the peaceful atmosphere draws people to their happiest memories.

162.content:
Mont Esus East (also: East Foothills of Mont Esus): Mont Esus East is the eastern foothills of Mont Esus in the Liffey Region of Fontaine. Mont Esus itself is a huge mountain north-west of the Court of Fontaine that the player cannot reach, so these foothills are the part that can be explored. The area came with Version 4.1.

Two stories touch it: a world quest about Fatui towers and camps, and a scene in Arlecchino's story quest set among forgotten ruins.

Geography: The foothills sit on the eastern side of the mountain. A tall observation tower and several Fatui camps stand in the area, with a broken bridge and a cliff noted in the Fatui's own deployment plan. The wiki records that the area's appearance changed after Version 4.6.

Wiki trivia claims Mont Esus is the highest mountain in Teyvat and offers a view across most of the continent. That comes from the wiki's reading of the map, not an in-game text, so do not treat it as established.

Places: The Fatui observation tower, climbed at the start of "In Search of Lost Time: West"; the camps around it; and the nameless ruins that Arlecchino shows the Traveler.

People: Fatui soldiers of the 34th Independent Investigative Squad hold the camps. A squad directive found in the tower assigns soldiers to a camp south of the broken bridge and to a highland camp near the cliff. Shumilov is among the characters listed for the world quest, which also mentions an absent Captain Malinovskyi.

History: The ruins were once a grand building. In "Into the Sunlight" (4.1), Arlecchino, the Knave, brings the Traveler here because this is where she killed Clervie and then Clervie's mother, Crucabena, before she became a Harbinger and before Lyney, Lynette and Freminet joined the House of the Hearth. She explains that the House takes in war orphans from all over Teyvat, and that how they are raised depends on whoever is in charge. The Traveler then faces her in a quest domain, and the quest ends with a visit to friends at the Hotel Bouffes d'ete.

Quests: "In Search of Lost Time: West" (a world quest) begins by ascending the tower, where Fatui soldiers are stationed. The Traveler finds clues in nearby camps and examines a terminal. "Into the Sunlight" is the last part of "When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out" in the Ignis Purgatorius Chapter, and the wiki lists this subarea as its start location.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the foothills are accessible, while Mont Esus itself stays out of reach.

163.content:
Morte Region (also: Morte): The Morte Region is the eastern waters of Fontaine's map. Its centrepiece is the Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Sealed Ruined Tower or the Tower of Gestalt, built by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo as its base. The area also has Fort Charybdis Ruins on an island, the east slopes of Mont Automnequi, four Orthants and, reached through the story, a place called the Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe in the Primordial Sea.

It was added in 4.2 with the world-quest chapter In the Wake of Narcissus. The name is French for 'dead'.

Geography: Open water and small islands surround the tower. Mont Automnequi runs through the Belleau and Morte regions, and the east slopes belong here. Fort Charybdis Ruins stand on an island in the east. Four Orthants, linked to the Seals of Chymical Marriage, are scattered around.

Local specialties are Condessence Crystal, Lumidouce Bell, Rainbow Rose, Romaritime Flower and Spring of the First Dewdrop.

Places: - **Tower of Ipsissimus**: the Ordo's tower. It is not labelled on the map until In the Wake of Narcissus begins. After the quest Savior's Wake, the tower sinks and stays submerged. Its map blurb reads: 'We must reach the lowest level before the arrival of the apocalypse.'
- **Fort Charybdis Ruins**: the ruins of a fort on an island in the eastern part of the region.
- **East Slopes of Mont Automnequi**: the eastern side of the mountain.
- **Orthants of Memory, Persona, Souls and Wishes**: four marked points. The Orthant of Memory holds one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage.

- **Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe**: a location within the Primordial Sea where the Traveler fights Narzissenkreuz in Waking from the Great Dream; the viewpoint is titled 'The World's Amniotic Fluid'.
- A floating raft east of the tower is where Urville starts Wish-Fulfilling Treasure Hunt; he later returns to a place called The Rusty Rudder.

People: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo's members (Ann, Caterpillar, Seymour, Al, Jak and others) are met in the Court region and in the tower; Jakob is the final opponent of the tower's descent. Urville and Nadia appear near the tower in Wish-Fulfilling Treasure Hunt. A boat with a Fatui banner, found after the quest Questions and Answers, holds scribbled orders to retrieve the remains of the 'Curve' lie detector before anyone in Fontaine does.

History: The tower was built by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo as its base. In the quest chain In the Wake of Narcissus (4.2), the Traveler joins the Ordo's investigation (Search in the Algae Sea), breaks four seals and enters the tower; descends it in Savior's Wake until reaching and breaking the seal over the Primordial Sea; and finally faces the being Narzissenkreuz in Waking from the Great Dream.

Search in the Algae Sea ends with a fight against Jakob in the tower's lower level. In Savior's Wake the Traveler fights waves of clockwork meka after breaking the seal over the Primordial Sea. In Waking from the Great Dream the opponent is labelled 'Narzissenkreuz - Incomplete Order of the New Cosmos' and the Traveler is given a holy blade (the Sword of Narzissenkreuz) to fight it.

After Waking from the Great Dream the chain continues with Rowboat's Wake, and Wish-Fulfilling Treasure Hunt is available after it. The tower's earlier pre-quest dialogue with Nadia and Urville can be heard on its north side before the chain is finished.

Atmosphere: The tower's levels are built around puzzles with optical couplers, and Ann accompanies the Traveler through the upper levels. The Primordial Sea site is titled 'The World's Amniotic Fluid' in its viewpoint.

Dangers: Clockwork meka in the tower and Narzissenkreuz in the Primordial Sea (both quest enemies). Contaminated Bacterial Mats and autocannons are hazards in the area.

Travel: A Teleport Waypoint labelled 'Exploring the Tower of Gestalt' follows the Traveler down the tower and to the arena. The tower is not marked on the map until the quest chain starts.

Quests: In the Wake of Narcissus: Search in the Algae Sea (Act I, starts at the Ordo in the Court region), Savior's Wake (Act II) and Waking from the Great Dream (Act III), then Rowboat's Wake. Others filed here: Wish-Fulfilling Treasure Hunt, An Expected Lie, A Very Fishy Encounter, An Invasion on Hold, Cupid's Lover, Muse's Mother, Meteoric Lance and Thalia and Melpomene.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tower is permanently submerged and the Ordo story is complete.

The region remains explorable for salvage and fishing; no newer content was found.

164.content:
Built by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and used as their base. In Savior's Wake the Traveler decodes a puzzle on one level, goes down, decodes another and then reaches the bottom level, beyond which lies a seal over the Primordial Sea. After the quest Savior's Wake it sinks permanently.

The map shows 'Exploring the Tower of Gestalt' as a waypoint. Ann accompanies the Traveler through the upper and middle levels.

165.comment: Morte Region: Orthants and Seals of Chymical Marriage
165.content: Four named points in Morte (Memory, Persona, Souls, Wishes). The wiki says the Orthant of Memory holds one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage broken during Search in the Algae Sea; the quests Cupid's Lover, Muse's Mother, Meteoric Lance and Thalia and Melpomene go with the seals.

166.content: A world quest started by talking to Urville on a floating raft east of the tower. Urville and Nadia gather lost items; the Traveler salvages items, drives off ball octopuses and finds clues to the treasure.

167.content:
New Fontaine Research Institute (also: The New Fontaine Research Institute, Alain Guillotin Research Institute): The New Fontaine Research Institute is where the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering works now. It was built near the ruins of the Central Laboratory after the Arkhium explosion there. Before the disaster the Institute was known as the Alain Guillotin Research Institute and hosted weekly lectures about critical projects. Its staff here include a Material Collation team, a fish-type clockwork meka research team and a Fonta vending machine.

The Institute studies machines and energy, unlike the Akademiya, and has no authority over the people of Fontaine nor does it educate them. According to the NPC Salsa it has financial problems.

Geography: The Institute sits in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region, close to the Central Laboratory Ruins that float in the sky above. The quest names the Institute's Qualifications Review Representative Office, Academic Assembly Hall, Executive Office and Materials Office.

A Fonta vending machine stands beside Heinry. After the quest Both Brains and Brawn, players can fill the Pankration Fonta Cup there.

Places: The Qualifications Review Representative Office is on the ground floor, where the quest begins. The Institute is rebuilding the Bossuet Library, formerly the Alain Guillotin Memorial Library, which was destroyed in the accident, and has asked the public to donate books. Donation records lie in a pile of books under a shelf with a ladder.

Research teams the NPCs mention include Material Collation, Fish-Type Clockwork Meka Research, a Finances Office (No. 5) and a Department of Statistics and Mathematics. A notice on a desk complains that paper use has been unusually high for three months, with a warning that paper is for research, not for wrapping snacks, propping up desks or horseplay, and that gambling with it is banned.

The donation paperwork is a running joke. The Statistics and Mathematics department is mistakenly asked to log book donations, and its staff, Juglar, Dupre and Bottin, file them in dry exchanges. The donations include a historical-criticism book, a boxed set of sword novels bought by mistake, a Steambird annual set, a negotiation manual from the Fortress of Meropide, and ten volumes on kinetic theory from a donor thanking the Institute. After the quest Villains, an anonymous donor returns a formula for 'Pure Water'.

People: Named staff are Chisseray (Material Collation Team Director), Damestier (Fish-Type Clockwork Meka Research Team Director), Lanty (Finances Office No. 5 Director), Vuillermoz (researcher), Denichere and Heinry (whose titles advertise Fonta), and, after the quest, Choiseul (Administrative Officer) and Raimondo (Senior Technician). Broglie (hydrology researcher) and Sevigne appear after later quests.

Augustus Lovelace says the Institute was once a paradise for researchers until Raimondo and Choiseul took over. Nacker, a researcher who worked with Edwin Eastinghouse, caused a smaller explosion at the ruins. The two men, Edwin and Nacker, were fired and sent to the Fortress of Meropide.

Governance: Unlike the Sumeru Akademiya, the Institute does not govern or educate; it researches machines and energy. It is run by administrators such as Choiseul and Raimondo, whose management has been criticised. Its inventions, many from Alain Guillotin, include clockwork mechanisms and kinetic cores.

Salsa says the Institute has financial problems and that the building is not as pretty as the old ruins. She also says the ruins have been rebuilt and the Institute is considering a 'Ruins Tour' for outsiders. The Institute is controversial in Fontaine, since it is said to avoid responsibility.

Culture: Researchers are earnest but bureaucratic: memos, departmental turf wars and dry humour fill the interactable texts. The Institute is a place for research and a 'temple of science', as the paper memo puts it.

History: The Institute's old campus at the Central Laboratory was levelled when the Arkhium core in a field generator led by Edwin Eastinghouse overloaded. The blast sent blocks of condensed water and ruins into the sky. The Institute set up a new site near the ruins, and the Callas Line was shut down. In Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles (4.1) the Traveler helps survey and stabilise the ruins and earns the title Honorary Senior Researcher.

A second, accidental explosion followed Nacker's tampering. Nacker, once in Edwin's Arkhium research group, was believed by Raimondo to be selling an Arkhium core. The Traveler shut down the prototype generator and installed inhibitors to stabilise the Arkhium traces. They later traced Nacker, who had a new benefactor named Concini, and learned that Edwin was also alive and continuing Arkhium research.

Dangers: No danger is listed for the Institute itself. The Central Laboratory Ruins nearby held out-of-control meka and unstable Arkhium, until the Traveler installed inhibitors to stabilise the Arkhium traces.

Atmosphere: Paperwork, a Fonta vending machine and bickering memos between departments, as the interactable texts show.

Travel: Marked as a subarea in the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering Region.

Quests: World quest series Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles (4.1): Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble, and the two errands to retrieve anchors at the Institute Dormitories and the Institute of Clockwork Applications. Also Both Brains and Brawn, Villains, In Search of Lost Time and Treacherous Light of the Depths for NPCs and interactables.

Status as of 7.1: The Institute's working headquarters as of 7.1.

168.comment: New Fontaine Research Institute: Chronie's Special Report
168.content: An annotated copy of Chronie's 'Special Report' lies on a table near Raimondo. The report claims the Institute is hiding that the old Central Laboratory ruins remain unsafe and that a researcher, named as Nacker, died in a second explosion. Two memos attached disagree: one finder asks if it is true, while the Institute's reply calls it categorically false and says it has handed the matter to Maison Gardiennage.

169.content:
Northland Bank (Fontaine) (also: Banque du Nord, Northland Bank Court of Fontaine): The Northland Bank in the Court of Fontaine is a branch of the Snezhnayan Northland Bank, in Quartier Lyonnais. Its sign is written in Fontaine Script as BANQUE DU NORD.

It stands between Caron's Lepaute Horlogerie and Livre's Leschots Clockwork Workshop. Its interior cannot be entered by the player.

Places: A narrow bank front between the two clockwork shops, seen only from the street.

Quests in the Toy War event series place the bank between the two brothers' shops, so it sits at the boundary of their rivalry.

Status as of 7.1: Present at the cutoff (7.1); its interior remains inaccessible.

The bank is part of the Fatui-linked Northland Bank network that has branches in other nations; canon does not detail this branch.

170.content:
Nostoi Region (also: Nostoi): The Nostoi Region is a southern island area of Fontaine that sits outside the raised continental plate the rest of the nation stands on, so the waters around it cannot be dived into. It contains Petrichor, a beautiful town known for very pure water and a view of the great waterfall that rings Fontaine, and the sunken Faded Castle, an old Remurian ruin that leads down to the Sea of Bygone Eras.

The name Nostoi echoes the ancient Greek 'Returns', an epic of kings going home after Troy.

Geography: An island in the south of Fontaine. Petrichor lies on it, in the vicinity of ruins and stone statues of the Golden Troupe of Remuria. Underneath, the Faded Castle is accessible from Petrichor's deep spring. Because the island lies off the continental plate, the surrounding water is not diveable like the rest of Fontaine's.

The region's exploration objects include a Mysterious Bookshelf Full of Grimoires, Mysterious Grimoires and the Symphony puzzle device. A bell tower in Petrichor carries an ancient inscription (Juliano's Legacy), and a tattered navigation log lies south of the town by a crashed boat after Canticles of Harmony.

Places: - **Petrichor**: a town on an island in southern Fontaine, popular with tourists for the encircling waterfall.
- **Faded Castle**: a sunken ruin that was part of the kingdom of Remuria. Harmosts and scholars lived there, maintaining archives and researching music theory and fate. It holds the entrance to the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Faded Castle has lower, middle and higher levels and a portal that links it to the Sea of Bygone Eras, which has its own map and exploration progress.

Books found in the castle include Harmost's Notes and Investigation of the Northern Barbarians; the latter mentions a sword used to choose a Holy King and a 'Mother of Many Springs'. The levels also hold a mural that can be played as a symphony, paintings of Domus Aurea and Praetorian Golems.

People: Petrichor's residents include Tiepolo, a 'Doge'; Foscari, the Doge's assistant; Bossuet, a former Senior Researcher of the Fontaine Research Institute; Babisse and Mécantre, chiefs for the Teyvat Grand Cannon construction and design; and Grundeland, a 'Good Merchant'.

A local cat named Osse leads the Traveler to the castle; the former Harmost Cassiodor and the shadowy Boethius appear in the quests.

History: The Faded Castle was once known as the 'golden castellum' in Remuria's golden age. Former Harmost Cassiodor says he and companions recorded ancient scripts, scores and stories there to harness the power of fate. He opposed Boethius's wish to revive Remuria at the cost of Fontaine and sealed the passage between the castle (and the Sea of Bygone Eras) and the surface.

In The Shadow Over Petrichor (4.6), strange events in Petrichor lead the Traveler and Paimon through ruins in a mountain to the deep spring and the castle, where Cassiodor lifts the seal and they meet Boethius.

Atmosphere: The 4.6 display page says there are 'many beautiful and moving legends' about Petrichor, and its viewpoint is titled 'The Lovely Legends of Petrichor'. The Faded Castle's viewpoints are titled 'Stage of Faded Gold' and 'Secret Locale of the Ancient Order'.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems revive from statues and guard the ruins; treasure hoarders and Fatui agents appear in quests.

Travel: Petrichor has a western Waverider Waypoint. The Faded Castle is entered through the deep spring after the quest chain begins, and the Sea of Bygone Eras is opened after Underwater Nocturne.

Quests: Canticles of Harmony is the main series: Prelude 'Petrichorror Dream' (The Shadow Over Petrichor), First Movement 'In the Hall of the Sea King' (Underwater Nocturne) and Second Movement 'Prisoner in Shackles' (The Last Day of Remuria). Follow-ups include For Yesterday and Tomorrow and Latecoming Homecoming.

The first quest requires the Prologue's Song of the Dragon and Freedom.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Petrichor is peaceful and the castle's secrets have been opened up.

No newer content than 4.6 was found for this region.

171.content: A town on an island of southern Fontaine. Famed for its beauty and unusually pure water, it is a tourist spot for seeing the huge waterfall encircling Fontaine. The name is said to mean 'golem' in an ancient language. Ruins and statues linked to the Golden Troupe of Remuria stand nearby.

172.content: A sunken Remurian castle where Harmosts and scholars once kept archives and studied music theory and fate. Cassiodor sealed the passage to the surface; in 4.6 he lifts the seal and the Traveler meets Boethius. Beyond it lies the Sea of Bygone Eras.

173.content:
Opera Epiclese: The Opera Epiclese is a grand opera house on the island of Erinnyes in the Court of Fontaine Region, and also Fontaine's main courthouse. Trials are held on its stage as public performances before a ticketed audience, with the Iudex Neuvillette presiding from a raised seat. On other nights the same stage hosts plays, musicals, concerts and magic shows. Behind the opera house a lift descends to River Talionis, the wharf from which convicts are shipped to the Fortress of Meropide.

For about five centuries a giant mechanical scale, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, stood on the stage beneath the judge's seat and gave the final verdicts. It has been inert since 4.2, and Neuvillette now passes judgment himself.

Geography: The building stands on Erinnyes, an island the official description calls consecrated, overlooking the city. The island also holds the Fountain of Lucine, Marcotte Station (the Navia aquabus line stop) and Erinnyes Forest. The courtroom is a multi-level auditorium with raised seating sections, an upper floor of sofas, a lobby and backrooms.

Under the building runs an underground passage, used in the Archon Quest when the stage tunnel of Lyney's magic box was investigated. The Fontaine Research Institute's ruins lie on the north side of the island, and an entrance to the Fortress of Meropide is also reached from Erinnyes.

Places: Inside, the judge's seat rises at the back of the stage with the (now inert) Oratrice below it. Until 4.2 Furina attended trials as the opera house's divine icon. A receptionist, Luzerne, greets visitors at the entrance beside a notice board of rules and programmes.

Posted rules require reserved tickets, assigned seating and proper dress, and ban outside food on pain of being expelled and punished by the Maison Gardiennage. Programmes have included the Steambird's La Verite Prize ceremony, which Furina insisted on presenting herself, Lyney's magic shows (a new "water tank escape"), a Melusine Philharmonic Orchestra concert, and the stage play "The Death of Aurelius".

People: Neuvillette presides over trials, and other judges of the Palais Mermonia can be assigned cases. Until 4.2 Furina was the opera house's star and "icon". She had the right to speak at any stage of a trial and starred in revived musical classics, and her performance dates became festivals in their own right. The Maison Gardiennage and the Marechaussee Phantom keep order. Champion Duelists fight accused people who choose a duel before trial.

Staff named in game include the receptionist Luzerne. Neuvillette's connection to the place began with an anonymous letter from Focalors promising him a seat with an excellent view. He did receive a seat in the middle of the front row and found the view as promised, and later understood that the letter meant more than a chair.

Governance: Trials follow Fontaine's theatrical procedure: prosecution and defence argue before the audience, witnesses are called, and the judge rules. Until 4.2 the Oratrice delivered the final verdict, which the Iudex had to honour even when he disagreed. The Oratrice also turned people's belief in justice into Indemnitium, a power source used in the Court of Fontaine and on Erinnyes.

Only a small share of that Indemnitium ever reached the city. Most was stored over 500 years so that the Oratrice could execute a god. Since the Oratrice fell silent, Neuvillette's restored authority over Pneumousia energy has stood in as a temporary substitute, and he has taken over the Oratrice's role in court.

Even after Alain Guillotin's Arkhe system came to power Fontaine's clockwork meka, the Court and Erinnyes still ran on the Oratrice's Indemnitium, and replacing it fully had proved difficult. Before 4.2 Lyney theorised that the Oratrice had something to do with the prophesied crisis.

Culture: Fontainians treat a trial as entertainment as much as justice. Some come for the emotion of real cases, others for the drama of staged productions, and the receptionist says the Hydro Archon recognised both as fit for this stage.

Furina recalled that every reform of the opera house drew noisy opposition from crowds inside it. On one occasion she silenced them with a decree just as Neuvillette tapped his cane. She held productions to exacting standards. When one troupe pretended to accept her demands and ignored them, she simply rehearsed with a different troupe.

History: When the Traveler arrived (4.0), Lyney and Lynette's first show here ended with a stagehand dead in a magic box. Furina prosecuted Lyney, the Traveler defended him, and with Navia's help the real story emerged. In 4.0 the Oratrice then shocked everyone by finding Childe guilty in the disappearances case although the true culprit had been exposed. In 4.2 Furina herself was trapped onto this stage and tried as a fraud. The Oratrice condemned "the Hydro Archon" to death, and Focalors used that sentence to execute herself and destroy the Hydro Archon's throne, which ended the prophecy's threat.

Before Furina's trial, a show at the opera turned into a small riot when spectators accused her of ignoring the prophecy, and she fled while the Marechaussee Phantom restored order. During the trial a rift opened in the opera house and the All-Devouring Narwhal emerged. Neuvillette and Childe, in his Foul Legacy form, forced it back. Some time afterwards Furina abdicated, packed up her belongings and left the opera house.

When Navia fell into Primordial Seawater in the ruins near Poisson (4.2), she found herself in a dream-trial at the Opera Epiclese. The prosecutor Joinville and an audience of the flood's dissolved victims demanded that she "join" them, until the spirits of Melus and Silver defended her and Neuvillette pulled her back to reality.

Atmosphere: Rows of red seats, a hushed full house waiting for a twist, the judge's cane on the floor, gasps and applause at a verdict. Lyney noted that the weather tends to change when trials take place. Outside, newlyweds toss coins into the Fountain of Lucine.

Quests: Chapter IV Act I (Lyney's trial, 4.0), Act II (Childe's verdict, 4.0) and Act V (Furina's trial, 4.2) are set here. Furina's story quest "The Little Oceanid" (4.2) ends with a performance here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Opera Epiclese still hosts both trials and performances, with Neuvillette as presiding judge.

The Oratrice stands inert on the stage. Furina no longer presides over it as the Hydro Archon: she abdicated after 4.2 but has since performed on this stage again as an actress.

174.comment: Opera Epiclese: Lyney's Trial at the Opera Epiclese
174.content:
During Lyney and Lynette's debut, a box-swap trick went wrong: the stagehand Cowell was found dead in a crushed box and the chosen audience member had vanished. Neuvillette locked down the house, and Furina, to please the crowd, made herself prosecutor and the Traveler defence attorney. Furina exposed the twins as members of the Fatui's House of the Hearth. Evidence of Primordial Seawater in Cowell's bag turned the case, and Navia brought the "vanished" woman back on stage. She was Liliane, a pickpocket who had panicked in the box, knocked Cowell out and put him in her place. The Oratrice found the twins not guilty.

Lyney later tried to investigate the Oratrice for "Father". He retreated after hearing a voice from it that seemed to know him and was contaminated with Indemnitium. The stage tunnel used for the trick became evidence, investigated by the Traveler and Navia.

175.content: In the serial disappearances case, the Oratrice declared Childe guilty although the actual culprit had already been exposed and convicted. It was the first time it had disagreed with the Chief Justice. Furina covered the error with bravado, Neuvillette began investigating the machine, and Childe was sent to the Fortress of Meropide. Neuvillette suspected Focalors was using Childe to hold back the All-Devouring Narwhal.

key: The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur
176.comment: Opera Epiclese: The Trial of Furina
176.content:
To force Furina to reveal what she knew of the prophecy, Neuvillette, the Traveler, Navia, the House of the Hearth siblings and Clorinde set a trap. Furina, hiding in a house in Poisson, saw its walls fall away to reveal the opera stage. The Fatui had built a "Giant Magic Box" and tunnelled to the opera house. Offered a duel with Clorinde or a trial, she chose trial. The Traveler charged her with being a fraud. Diluted Primordial Seawater and Sigewinne's examination proved she was human, and Neuvillette ruled her guilty. The Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death. Freminet arrived with the missing first prophecy slate, the Narwhal burst through a rift, and as the blade fell, Focalors, hidden in the Oratrice, executed herself.

Focalors had split herself, leaving Furina to play the god on this stage for 500 years while the Oratrice stored Indemnitium. Her death destroyed the Hydro Archon's throne and returned the power to Neuvillette, who absolved Fontainians of their "original sin". As the Oratrice no longer worked, Neuvillette took the Traveler with him as his executor into the Primordial Sea to subdue the Narwhal.

177.comment: Opera Epiclese: Erinnyes Island and the Fountain of Lucine
177.content: Erinnyes is the island in the Court of Fontaine Region that holds the Opera Epiclese, the Fountain of Lucine, Marcotte Station and Erinnyes Forest. The official description calls it consecrated and says the opera house there symbolises the new era's commitment to law and justice. An old custom survives: newlyweds toss coins into the Fountain of Lucine for a happy life. Lynette believes tears that flow into the fountain carry intense emotion, and the Traveler first heard an Oceanid's voice there. Wines called Sassica and Ornella are said to be produced on Erinnyes, and Neuvillette considers exploring its depths ill-advised.

178.comment: Opera Epiclese: Later Performances at the Opera Epiclese
178.content:
After her abdication, Furina helped a struggling amateur troupe, whose director Aurelie had died, stage Aurelie's musical "The Little Oceanid" at the Opera Epiclese. She directed the rehearsals, and when the ailing actress Dulphy was incapacitated before the finale, Furina played the heroine Clio in the final scene. The performance was a success.

In the 4.2 world quest series "Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine", the villain Jenck was later found maimed and kneeling on the opera stage with a note of apology to the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard; the Traveler suspected a Fatui Harbinger was behind it.

179.comment: Opera Epiclese: The Opera Epiclese during the Fontinalia Film Festival
179.content: During the limited-time event Sunny Summer Fontinalia (6.7), Citlali found it hard to rest near the Opera Epiclese.
