Sandrone explained that all of Fontaine's water gathers at the Fountain of Lucine, and with it the emotions in the water, including those of incomplete souls severed long ago by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's soul-severing research. At the end of the festival the Traveler, Furina, Columbina, Sandrone and others watched the premiere of their film in the Opera Epiclese.

180.content:
Orthant of Memory (also: Hall of Memory, Room of Memory, Memory Orthant): The Orthant of Memory is one of four Seals of Chymical Marriage in the Morte Region of Fontaine, set by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Its riddle slate announces "the Orthant of Memory, the Hall of Memory, the Room of Memory" and the answer to its riddle is a shadow. The Memory piece it once held, one of four substances for forging the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, was already gone when the Traveler arrived; the quest Muse's Mother covers it.

Added in 4.2 with the chain In the Wake of Narcissus. The Orthants were meant to be joined, and Caterpillar explains that the "birth of reason" requires all four.

Geography: Entered through underwater Mysterious Ruins north-west of the Morte Region's Statue of the Seven. A bonfire still burns near the door, and Rifthounds stand near the entrance.

When the Orthant's puzzle is solved the area floods, which opens areas that could not be reached before and solves others that depended on the water.

Places: The entrance and the riddle slate; the door guarded by the riddle; the inner altar chamber where the Memory piece lay; a mechanism whose top is empty when inspected.

People: No residents. The Narzissenkreuz Ordo's remnants, above all Jakob Ingold, are the last to have used it; Caterpillar and Ann search it with the Traveler.

Culture: The slate quotes a verse of "Echoes Hallowed and Humble", Movement 9, Stanza 37: if water loses its incisiveness it cannot become water again, a tree away from soil cannot root, and however hard stone strikes metal, humans cannot live without water or soil.

History: Canon does not say when the seal was built. The Ordo's four substances (Memory, Wish, Soul and Persona) were "reproduced in the material world" from Fontainian esoteric philosophy and the technology of the underground kingdom, and used in the ritual for forging the Holy Blade. In the Search in the Algae Sea version of the quest, Caterpillar says Jakob had been here first and had solved the riddle.

The Ordo's own metaphors explain the purpose: the temple is a microcosm of the universe, its members stand in for gods, and the holy oil is tempered will. The Holy Blade itself stands for reason, which cuts everything open and can be born only of complete human will. Later, in the Tower of Gestalt, Jakob claims to have reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage, calling it an ancient ritual that sealed off the source of life.

Quests: Muse's Mother: find the seal, study the riddle slate, solve the Orthant puzzle and obtain the Memory piece. The riddle ("Born in an instant... often contradicting, your company in eternal rest, never separated... fire cannot burn it") is answered "shadows". There are two versions depending on whether Search in the Algae Sea was started first.

Caterpillar notes the ancient Fontainians and the Ordo both loved riddles; the Traveler can offer silly answers (kidney stones, Oceanid tears) before settling on shadows.

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied; the Memory piece is gone. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

Dangers: Rifthounds near the door and puzzle machinery.

Atmosphere: Dank stone, lingering firelight and the sense of a place already ransacked.

181.comment: Orthant of Memory: The Four Orthants
181.content: Four hidden seals in Fontaine: the Orthants of Memory, Wishes, Souls and Persona, each giving a "piece" (Memory, Wish, Soul, Persona) used to forge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz ("reason"). The Traveler finds that Jakob has beaten them to three of them. In the Tower of Gestalt Jakob says only the five most important nodes in Fontaine survive and that he has reversed the Seal. The Collegium Phonascorum's notes in the Sea of Bygone Eras list the same four names as the Quadrant of Qualities, an echo canon does not explain.

182.content:
Orthant of Persona (also: Persona Orthant): The Orthant of Persona is the last of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage left by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its riddle ends with "the first droplet", and the answer that opens it is an Oceanid. It holds the Persona piece, the most important of the four substances for forging the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, which Jakob wants and which Caterpillar gives the Traveler to keep.

Added in 4.2. It is the "final seal" of the quest chain, and in Search in the Algae Sea it is where Jakob's trap leads the Traveler to the Tower of Gestalt.

Geography: An underground area in the Morte Region whose entrance is sealed. Its position is not described beyond that.

The entrance is shut by the riddle, not by a key; Ann, whom Jakob calls an Oceanid, opens it.

People: Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour accompany the Traveler. Jakob Ingold is the rival who set a trap and sealed the space; the Master, Narzissenkreuz, supposedly excised his persona here.

Ann, whom Jakob calls an Oceanid, is tied to Lyris and Mary-Ann Guillotin; Caterpillar is a hilichurl who knows the Ordo's language and lore; Seymour is a mechanical dog. Their stories are in their own entries.

Culture: The slate quotes the "Third Hymn", Movement 5, Stanza 1, praising Remus as "player of the grand symphony, king of all the world", and begging the Merciful One for eternal life when Sybilla's Golden Bee gives its warning.

History: Jakob tells the Traveler that the Persona section is the most important, because the persona the Master excised lies there. To keep it, he says he set a trap before activating the Orthant and sealed the space. He says he must forge the Holy Blade and place it in his Master's hand before the "second deluge" of the Prophecy of Fontaine.

Jakob says the Blade would let the Master gather the wills of everyone in Fontaine, the continent and the planet unto himself to survive the deluge, which Paimon calls bundling consciousness without consent. After the fight in the Tower of Gestalt he claims to have reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage, calling it an old Fontainian ritual meant to seal off the source of life; the claim and its results are tied to the 4.2 story, not to this site.

Quests: Thalia and Melpomene: head to the final seal, solve the Orthant puzzle with the riddle ("Always united... born in an instant, often contradicting, I accompany you in eternal rest... the first droplet"), and obtain the Persona piece. The answers to earlier Orthants were "shadow", "life" and "love". In the world quest Search in the Algae Sea, interacting with the final seal sends the Traveler to Jakob's trap in the Tower of Gestalt.

Three variant dialogue versions exist depending on whether the Search in the Algae Sea quest was started and in what order the seals were visited. Seymour cannot analyse the Persona, which reads as zero mass.

Status as of 7.1: Open; the Persona piece is in the Traveler's hands. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

Dangers: Jakob's traps and the machinery of the Orthant itself.

Atmosphere: A quiet, tense chamber where the water itself is the key. After the piece is taken, the mood turns from search to confrontation.

183.comment: Orthant of Persona: The Orthant Riddle Answers
183.content: The four slates share a refrain ("Born in an instant, often contradicting, your company in eternal rest") with a changing final line. Answers in the order they appear in the quests: shadow (Memory), life (Wishes), love (Souls), and the first droplet or Oceanid (Persona).

184.content:
Orthant of Souls (also: Shrine of Souls, Room of Souls, Souls Orthant): The Orthant of Souls is one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage set by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, placed in Mysterious Ruins on the east slopes of Mont Automnequi in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its riddle slate names it "the Orthant of Souls, the Shrine of Souls, the Room of Souls", and the answer to its riddle is love. By the time the Traveler arrives the Soul piece has already been removed. The quest is Cupid's Lover.

Added in 4.2. The ruins have a riddle slate with a pocket watch nearby, an elaborate mechanism puzzle with Looking Glass rooms, a lift and an underwater section.

Geography: Reached from the east slopes of Mont Automnequi. The ruins have an upper floor and a lower floor, linked by a lift, with a flooded underwater section reached by lowering the lift.

A Looking Glass room lets the Traveler light torches; a windowsill holds a Special Key that opens a locked door to the last energy-flow device. When energy flow is released in the underwater area, the surrounding ground becomes dry.

Places: The Riddle Slate at the entrance; the mechanism whose top is found empty; three energy-flow devices; the Looking Glass room; the underwater chamber.

A 4-star Nymph's Constancy weapon can be picked up beside the Riddle Slate (gameplay note).

People: Jakob Ingold and his unseen allies; the Traveler with Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour.

Culture: The hymn excerpt comes from the "Song of Serenity", Movement 2, Stanza 84. It says people share one resilient skin and the same divine essence in their veins, as there is one wisdom and one melody, so their wills are one; they should draw close, "even unto outlanders". The wiki links the verse's "one melody" to Phobos, but the stanza itself names no god.

History: The Ordo placed the seal in a Mysterious Ruin. Caterpillar notes that "the birth of reason requires the merging of the four orthants". In the Search in the Algae Sea version he notes that someone else has already solved the riddle.

The riddle ("I accompany you in eternal rest"... "Born in an instant, often contradicting, always united"... "I am life's most cherished treasure") has the answer love. Paimon's guesses are Mora and then "wealth"; Seymour finds a match in an old novel that ends with love lying nestled in the marrow; Ann connects it to her own pocket watch.

Quests: Cupid's Lover: find the seal, study the Riddle Slate, look for a way forward, solve the Orthant puzzle and obtain the Soul piece. The quest's title is thought to refer to Psyche, goddess of the soul and consort of Cupid (the wiki's note). It has two versions depending on whether Search in the Algae Sea was started first.

Enemies met include Recon Log Mek - Ousia and Geological Survey Mek - Ousia in the upper rooms and Recon Log Mek - Pneuma underwater.

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

Dangers: Hostile mek constructs and flooded passages.

Atmosphere: A cold stone shrine where a lone pocket watch lies on the ground, with the sense that someone was here just before.

185.comment: Orthant of Souls: Song of Serenity Excerpt
185.content: Movement 2, Stanza 84: all people are said to share resilient skin and divine essence, one wisdom and one melody, and so one will. It calls them hands and legs, shield and sword, roots, leaves, spring and stream, and urges closeness even to outlanders.

186.content:
Orthant of Wishes (also: Temple of Wishes, Room of Wishes, Wishes Orthant): The Orthant of Wishes is one of the four Seals of Chymical Marriage left by the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, hidden in the Mysterious Ruins of the Fort Charybdis Ruins in the Morte Region of Fontaine. Its slate calls it "the Orthant of Wishes, the Temple of Wishes, the Room of Wishes", and the riddle's answer is life. The Wish piece it held was already taken when the Traveler came; the quest is Meteoric Lance. On the second floor an Ordo member's diary records the Great Ritual.

Added in 4.2. An unconscious man at the door is taken to Lumidouce Harbor for treatment before the Traveler goes on.

Geography: Entered through the Mysterious Ruins at Fort Charybdis, a multi-floor complex with a lift, gates, lifting columns and an underwater area beneath the main machine in the central room. A Looking Glass on one floor leads to a side chamber with a Thundercraven Rifthound and a chest; another Looking Glass is on the third floor.

A Seelie must be led to its court to open access to the underwater section. The riddle slate, the diary and the hymn excerpt lie on or near the second floor.

Places: The entrance with the fallen man; the Riddle Slate; the second-floor excerpt and diary; the central machine room and flooded lower section; the Seelie Court puzzle; two Looking Glass rooms.

People: Named in the diary: the Master (Narzissenkreuz), Mr. Ingold (whom the wiki identifies with Jakob Ingold), Ms. Calafia, Mr. Forsamiro, Madam Laveaux, Ms. Lenormand, Professor Griffin L. Randolph and Ms. Zenaida. In the Search in the Algae Sea version the Traveler comes with Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour.

The diarist calls Ms. Calafia not the sharpest tool but still a disciple of someone (the line is cut off); she questions Mr. Forsamiro about the stone slates and is calmed by Madam Laveaux and Ms. Lenormand, though the diarist expects word to reach the Iudex. Ms. Zenaida led the group who left the Ordo, "disappointed with the future".

Governance: The diary shows an organisation that works through official channels: Mr. Ingold arranges plans for a construction project, the Palais Mermonia confirms the site, and Marechaussee Hunters take charge of security. The Ordo is careful to report its deeds first and to use a cover story, with Professor Randolph's social standing, to buy time.

History: The diary says the Ordo really did find Remuria's ruins at the indicated location. Workers began spreading uneasy stories, and members of the Ordo suffered mentally and were helped. When the work was done, Mr. Ingold, speaking for the Master, thanked the workers; the Master was said to be performing the Great Ritual, tied to celestial bodies and the Primal Fire. Zenaida's group left after her own divination worried her. The diarist's own divinations show the Master alive within the tower.

The final entries turn dark: the writer, curious, divines where those who left went and finds that they are still within the tower, which contradicts their note about leaving. The writer resolves to speak to Mr. Ingold in person.

Quests: Meteoric Lance: find the seal, study the Riddle Slate, look for a way forward, solve the Orthant puzzle and obtain the Wish piece. The riddle ("Often contradicting... born in an instant, your company in eternal rest, never separated... the tainted fruits of sin") is answered "life": Caterpillar says the Ordo regards Fontainians as sinners bearing original sin.

The quest's name probably refers to shooting stars, which people have long associated with wishes (the wiki's note).

Status as of 7.1: Opened and emptied. Nothing newer than 4.2 is recorded.

Dangers: Underwater Patrol Mek, Recon Log Mek - Ousia, puzzle machinery, strong currents.

Atmosphere: Echoing stone floors above flooded depths, with the dread of the man left at the door and the unfinished confession in the diary.

187.comment: Orthant of Wishes: Excerpt from Echoes Hallowed and Humble
187.content: A hymn on the second floor, Movement 5, Stanza 3, that contrasts barbarians and water creatures with those whose strength is will, the thing humans share with the noblest gods, and says those who command with will make the rest bow down and listen.

188.comment: Orthant of Wishes: The Diary of the Great Ritual
188.content: An unsigned diary in the second-floor ruins, some words blacked out. The writer reports the construction, the hired Marechaussee Hunters, the Master's seclusion for the Great Ritual and the disappearance of Zenaida's group, and ends by wanting to confront Mr. Ingold.

189.content:
Palais Mermonia: The Palais Mermonia stands at the highest point of the Court of Fontaine and is where all of Fontaine's administration is handled. To Fontainians it is effectively the highest authority in the land. It houses Iudex Neuvillette's office and the government bodies called Maisons: Ordalie (the judiciary), Gestion (administration and documents), Cardinalice (financial approvals) and Gardiennage (law enforcement), along with the Marechaussee Phantom. It was also Furina's residence while she reigned as Hydro Archon. She moved out after 4.2.

Humans and Melusines staff it side by side. Even in Furina's day they did the real work of government, while she handled social and ceremonial appearances.

Geography: The Palais crowns the northwestern part of the Court of Fontaine, overlooking the city. The area around the Palais has its own Statue of The Seven. An official description pictures citizens below leading orderly lives, as regular as the aquabus, under its gaze.

Places: A front hall with a reception desk, staffed by the Melusine officer Sedene, controls access to the offices beyond. Neuvillette's office holds the court's case-file archives. The square outside is busy with Gardes, Gestionnaires and Palais staff by day, and Steambird reporters loiter behind the building.

People: Neuvillette, Chief Justice (Iudex) and head of the Maison Ordalie and the Marechaussee Phantom, works here. Sedene, a Melusine of the Marechaussee Phantom, keeps the front desk and decides who may enter. Gestionnaires of the Maison Gestion (Cornelia, Eunomia, Imena and others) process the paperwork, and Isadora works as one of the Palais's auditors.

Other judges besides Neuvillette work out of the Palais and can be assigned trials. Gardes such as Bruneau stand near the entrance, the Cardinal Assistant Plessia works there, and Steambird staff (the reporter Houallet and the photographer Antila) watch from behind the building. Isadora says her work is confidential, so she cannot complain about it to anyone.

Governance: The Maison Ordalie runs the judicial system under the Iudex. The Maison Gestion manages documents and administrative tasks, the Maison Cardinalice oversees financial approvals, and the Maison Gardiennage provides law enforcement through the Gardes and Gardemeks. The Marechaussee Phantom, an elite investigative force made up mostly of Melusines, answers directly to the Chief Justice. The Palais also confers Fontaine's honorary titles.

The Palais is famous for red tape. Replacing a single typewriter keycap takes several rounds of forms, and the clockwork-toy maker Livre needed a police officer's help to get paid for meka the Palais had ordered, because the Gestionnaire handling his file kept him waiting on forms. The Maison Gestion has an official seal, a new key-operated stamping machine, and rules requiring a Kamera record of everyone who uses it. The Fortress of Meropide counts the Palais among its best customers. The Court's jurisdiction does not extend inside the Fortress.

History: For about five centuries Furina, playing the Hydro Archon, lived at the Palais, while Neuvillette and the staff governed. Furina once tried to join its daily work out of boredom, but humans and Melusines alike politely insisted there were no duties that needed their god. During the 4.x crisis the Palais was the Traveler's point of contact with Neuvillette. After Furina's trial and Focalors' sacrifice in 4.2, Furina abdicated, left the office's affairs (though not the title) to Neuvillette, packed her bags and left the Palais Mermonia for a rented apartment.

In Act II (4.0), Navia talked her way past Sedene into Neuvillette's office to search the case files for the witness Vacher, found nothing, and told Neuvillette his apology for her father Callas sounded empty. In Act III (4.1), Neuvillette summoned the Traveler here and proposed sending them undercover into the Fortress of Meropide on a false charge. After the Poisson disaster (4.2) the Palais was buzzing with activity, and in Neuvillette's office he and Furina argued over the list of victims and the missing prophecy slate. Furina fled, and Neuvillette concluded that only a trial would make her talk.

Furina says it has been a long time since she visited the Palais, and that no longer working together is good for both her and Neuvillette.

Culture: The Palais grants honorary titles. Recipients normally attend an investiture ceremony, and the ceremony for a title as high as Duke is more elaborate. Callas of the Spina di Rosula once turned down the title of Baron. Wriothesley, offered the title of Duke, asked simply to sign the certificates. After many workdays of correspondence the Palais agreed, and Neuvillette bestowed the title in person.

Atmosphere: Formal, busy and bureaucratic: Melusine and human clerks at their desks, forms waiting for the right stamp, Gardes and reporters outside, and the Iudex in his office reading case files. Wriothesley once found Neuvillette standing drenched in the rain by the road near the Palais and held an umbrella over him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Palais Mermonia remains the seat of Fontaine's government, with Neuvillette handling the nation's affairs from his office there.

Furina no longer lives or works there. Sedene now tells visitors that Furina has left her official post and seemed much more relaxed the last time she saw her.

190.content: The Iudex's office in the Palais Mermonia holds the court's case-file archives, a place outsiders normally never reach. Neuvillette keeps working there through crises. Sigewinne writes to him from the Fortress of Meropide and adds anecdotes in case he is bored at the Palais. In 4.0 Sedene let Navia and the Traveler through after Navia said they had come to archive material for a follow-up case. In 4.1 Neuvillette gave the Traveler a Fruity Trio cake from his desk before sending them into the Fortress of Meropide on a false charge, and in 4.2 Sedene let them in as welcome guests.

191.comment: Palais Mermonia: The Maisons of the Palais
191.content: The Palais houses Fontaine's four Maisons. Ordalie runs the courts under the Iudex. Gestion handles documents and administration, with offices for confidential items and staff matters, and its employees are called Gestionnaires. Cardinalice oversees financial approvals. Gardiennage enforces the law with Gardes, Gardemeks, the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol and the Marechaussee Phantom. In the Fontaine world quest "A Certain Stamp", the Gestionnaire Iaune, after a night of drafting with Roialte and Semaine, must still have a proposal stamped by Thales's new key-operated machine and then by Difor before it can be printed.

192.comment: Palais Mermonia: Furina at the Palais
192.content: While she reigned, Furina lived at the Palais and attended social and diplomatic functions, while others did the real government work and sometimes even gave her speeches. After the prophecy was resolved she felt she had no place in the new order, packed her bags and left the Palais and the Opera Epiclese. In her new rented apartment she left her luggage unpacked and lay staring at the ceiling, until a struggling troupe drew her back to the stage.

193.comment: Palais Mermonia: Palais Mermonia Bulletin Board
193.content: During the limited-time event Whirling Waltz, a bulletin board stood by the Palais entrance. It carried event listings, a note that the Trial Court's annual judicial statistics report could be requested from Officer Sedene of the Marechaussee Phantom, an offer to subscribe to the monthly Palais Mermonia Trial Court Gazette (legal documents and case files compiled by the Maison Gardiennage), and a lost-and-found list. The board was removed after the event.

194.content:
Pale Forgotten Glory: Pale Forgotten Glory is a talent-material domain: the submerged wreckage of a once-proud ship on the seabed north-east of Poisson, in Salacia Plain. What should have been a quiet final resting place is full of mysterious creatures.

Clearing it yields materials for talent advancement, in the Equity, Justice and Order series.

Geography: Underwater wreckage beneath Fontaine's waters, north-east of the town of Poisson in the Salacia Plain.

Hull and decks lie ruined and flooded; what the ship carried or where it was bound is not told.

Dangers: Breacher Primus creatures in Shatterstone and Overgrown varieties, with larger versions in the later stages.

Gameplay note: the domain's Ley Line Disorder increases the active character's Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack damage when any character gains or loses HP.

It has four difficulty tiers (recommended levels 38, 54, 71 and 88). Weekday talent books rotate through Equity, Justice and Order, each series with Teachings, Guide and Philosophies grades.

Atmosphere: Dim, pale and silent, with the faded grandeur of a wreck in deep water.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent talent domain as of 7.1; no story events are tied to it.

195.content:
Pankration Ring (also: Pankration Arena): The Pankration Ring is the arena of the Fortress of Meropide, the underwater prison of Fontaine. Pankration, a bare-fisted combat sport, is the Fortress's most popular entertainment. The host, Roussimoff, announces bouts from the platform above the stage.

The ring sits in the south-western part of the Administrative Area and has its own lift. Official text says that as long as special conditions are met, anyone or anything, from a Sternshield Crab to a clockwork meka, can stand on its stage. Inmates, staff and visitors treat it as both spectacle and exercise.

The arena is the most visible part of the Fortress's social life under Administrator Wriothesley: a place where inmates earn attention and Credit Coupons rather than only serving time. Roussimoff says it is larger than any arena in the Court of Fontaine's Fleuve Cendre, which is why he prefers it.

Its name comes from the ancient Greek combat sport pankration ("all powers"), which allowed almost every technique except weapons. The drink sponsorship by Fonta that Roussimoff mentions ties the ring to the Fortress's wider economy.

Geography: The Pankration Ring lies in the south-western part of the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide, reached by its own separate lift. It has a central stage, with the host's announcer platform overlooking it, and an entrance area outside where fighters wait and talk.

The Administrative Area is the Fortress's central hub, with the Duke's Office in its middle; the ring is entered separately from it.

People: Roussimoff is the host, an open-world NPC titled Pankration Ring Host. He is jovial and energetic, says he would rather fight than announce, and wants to face the best opponents. Goncourt, an inmate with a theatrical bent, uses the ring as a stage and spars there to loosen his joints.

Poiret and Genevieve train for bouts in the Both Brains and Brawn world quest; Champvallon appears at its end. Before the Traveler completes that quest, Roussimoff turns them away as a fighter; afterwards he greets them as "the coach".

Once Both Brains and Brawn is complete, a one-on-one challenge becomes available: Goncourt fights first, then Roussimoff, who calls himself the champ. Each win gives a chest with Credit Coupons. This is a gameplay feature; keep it light in narrative scenes.

Culture: Pankration is described as the Fortress's most popular form of entertainment. Roussimoff calls it a very healthy sport, and a notice board in the arena says it is a great form of exercise. Matches are partly theatre: performers talk about acting a scene on the stage, and Roussimoff worries that plain hand-to-hand fighting lacks theatricality.

Fonta (a sweet drink) sponsors recreational matches; Roussimoff himself prefers Pure Water. He notes that most inmates have hit rock bottom, and that a little sweetness is something they remember after release.

Quests: The world quest Both Brains and Brawn (Administrative Area) is built around the ring: Genevieve and Poiret want to take part, the Traveler helps them train for a series of bouts against Roussimoff, and the quest ends with a clockwork meka fight and Champvallon.

Its steps run across several in-game days, with bouts held in the evening (18:00 to 22:00).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ring remains open and unchanged in the sources read.

196.content: The Pankration Ring is the arena of the Fortress of Meropide, in the south-western Administrative Area (separate lift). Pankration is the Fortress's most popular entertainment; official text says anyone or anything meeting the special conditions can fight on its stage. The host is Roussimoff.

197.content:
Roussimoff is the Pankration Ring Host in the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide. He announces from the platform above the stage but would rather be fighting, and wants to face the best opponents. He prefers Meropide's arena to the Fleuve Cendre because it is bigger. After Both Brains and Brawn he greets the Traveler as "coach".

He finds Fonta too sweet but speaks well of Heinry, and thinks the Fortress's inmates remember kindness after release.

198.content:
Passage of Ianus (also: Ianus Passage): A water current runs through its entire length. Its entrance is Initium Iani, which the Initium Iani page calls the sole path between Machimos and Capitolium, so anyone passing between the outer and inner city of sunken Remuria goes through here. It is part of the Sea of Bygone Eras area and was added in Version 4.6.

Geography: A single long submerged passage, running from the Machimos side to Capitolium, with a continuous water current along it. It has no other known branches in canon.

Its entrance, Initium Iani, lies at the Machimos end. Interactable engravings there speak of a slave named Decimus who now lies at the sea bottom like the exalted Harmosts, a bleak levelling of rank by the sea.

History: Canon gives no separate history for the corridor. It belongs to the Remuria of the Remus era; the Initium Iani page records that the Dragon Prince Scylla was long ago sealed at the entrance by the joint efforts of the Harmosts Boethius and Euergetia, which makes the gate the site of one of Remuria's defining acts.

That seal claim is drawn from the Initium Iani page, which cites the quest "The Last Day of Remuria" for Boethius and an engraving in Caesareum Palace for Euergetia. Treat the passage's own ancient role beyond "the way between outer and inner city" as unstated.

Atmosphere: Dark, flooded and moving: a current tugs along a stone throat between two halves of a dead city, with the silence and weight of the deep above it.

Travel: Entered at Initium Iani from the Machimos side. The water current carries travellers along the corridor, which is the only route to Capitolium.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing in canon changes its state; it remains an accessible underwater route in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

199.content: Initium Iani is the entrance to the Passage of Ianus and the only way between Machimos and Capitolium. According to its page, the Dragon Prince Scylla was sealed here long ago by the Harmosts Boethius and Euergetia. Engravings at the gate describe Decimus, a humble slave, and the exalted Harmost as equally sunken to the sea bottom.

200.content:
Petrichor (also: Petrichor town, the Musicmaking Town): Petrichor is a picturesque town on an island in the south of Fontaine, off the continental plate that carries the rest of the nation. It is known for its beauty and its exceedingly pure waters, and is a popular spot for viewing the great waterfall that encircles Fontaine. A council of elders, the Consilium Sapientium, governs it by tradition, with a "Doge" as its head. Its mountains hold ruins and stone golems from the ancient kingdom of Remuria.

The town is polite to outsiders but wary of change. It is home to the Daydream Club of inventors and to the hometown of the researcher and filmmaker Xavier.

Geography: An island town in the Nostoi Region, off the main Fontaine landmass. Ruins and stone statues from the Golden Troupe of Remuria dot the mountains, and a deep spring leads underwater to the Faded Castle. A bell tower rises over the town, and the southern shore has a crashed boat and a distant island.

The Faded Castle is a sunken Remurian ruin where Harmosts and scholars once kept archives and researched music theory and fate; it contains the entrance to the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Places: The town centre has a Statue of the Seven and a bell tower. Mécantre and Babisse, brothers of the Daydream Club, work on a giant cannon here (the Teyvat Grand Cannon). Inscriptions, ruins in the mountains, and the southern beach are the main sights for adventurers.

The Ancient Inscription on the bell tower records Juliano's story and the riddle to his four hidden caches ("heart of the mountains", "eye of the springs", "corner's apex", "the distant island of pouring pearls").

People: Tiepolo is the current Doge. Others include Foscari (his assistant), Goldoni, Grundeland (a "Good Merchant"), Contarini, Este, Giovanni, Giustino, Jules, Loredan, Martha, Moce, Paula, Venier, Chandraputra, the former Fontaine Research Institute researcher Bossuet, and the Daydream Club's Mécantre and Babisse.

The Daydream Club, a group of inventors from Fontaine, gathers here; its members include Xavier, Garcia, Felix Yogue, Mécantre, Babisse, Este and Grispan under their president Grobel. Xavier, who made films in Inazuma, comes from Petrichor.

Governance: The Consilium Sapientium is a committee of elders that, by tradition, assesses all affairs of the town; the most trustworthy elder is made "Doge". Tiepolo holds that title now. It was founded by Ruggiero, the first Doge.

Foscari, the Doge's assistant, has been arguing that the town should change. Tiepolo describes the town as romantic and idyllic, with people who are polite to guests but suspicious because they seldom leave the island.

Culture: Tradition guides daily life and customs are simple. Residents recall that the town believed its past decline came from getting too close to the outside world, though the young now think otherwise. Realm furnishing sets refer to it as the "Musicmaking Town".

The Doge says Petrichor's history is longer than the Court of Fontaine's. Tiepolo says the town was once governed by the de Petrichor family, whose first duke was appointed by Egeria.

History: The de Petrichor family ruled the town for centuries, from the first duke appointed by Egeria until at least 500 years ago, and were just and benevolent leaders. Their last patrono, Renault, was transferred to be mayor of Poisson and died there in the Siege of Poisson, which ended the line in Petrichor. The town then nearly became an abandoned fishing village until Ruggiero founded the Consilium Sapientium.

Ruggiero came seeking proof of the Grand Symphonies, collecting special conches, and sensed a mysterious energy lingering in what was then a run-down fishing village. He met the Golden Hunter, helped him prevent Boethius from awakening the seals to Remuria, and eventually decided that humanity should not control knowledge beyond its abilities. He stayed on to rebuild Petrichor, attracting refugees and spreading other versions of the legend so that the town's secrets were protected. The adventurer Juliano gave him money.

The wiki notes that the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Carter Scherbius, Mary-Ann Guillotin, Rene, Alain Guillotin and Jakob once went on a picnic here, according to an Ancient Log. Rene de Petrichor, son of the last patrono, is the same Rene who later founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo with Jakob Ingold.

Atmosphere: Calm and old-fashioned: a bell tower, tradition-minded locals who are polite and friendly to guests, and an undercurrent of wariness toward outsiders, with the roar of Fontaine's encircling waterfall nearby.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems and Tainted Hydro Phantasms guard or haunt the ruins, and Fontemer Aberrants roam the shore. Treasure Hoarders arrived at the time of The Shadow Over Petrichor.

Travel: Petrichor is an island off the continental plate, so travel there is over water (the treasure hunters of the opening quest arrive by ship). A deep spring leads to the Faded Castle. The town gets tourists who come to see the waterfall.

Quests: The world quest chain Canticles of Harmony (4.6) begins here with The Shadow Over Petrichor. Other activities include the hidden exploration objectives Juliano's Legacy and Foscari's Dilemma, and the quest Daydreams Beyond Space and Time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Petrichor is a calm island town ruled by the Consilium Sapientium, with its Remurian ruins quiet. No later canon changes its state.

Tiepolo is still Doge, Foscari still urges reform, and the Daydream Club keeps working on its inventions.

201.comment: Petrichor: Consilium Sapientium and the Doge
201.content: The Consilium Sapientium is Petrichor's council of elders, set up by Ruggiero, the town's first Doge, after the de Petrichor line died out. Tiepolo, the current Doge, says there is little to oversee because the townspeople live simple lives by tradition. He welcomes strangers kindly and asks them not to blame wary locals.

202.comment: Petrichor: Ruggiero and the Faded Castle
202.content:
Ruggiero was a scholar who came to Petrichor in search of the Grand Symphonies, and became the town's first Doge. He helped seal the Faded Castle after failing to find the relics he sought there, and later gave up his quest, feeling humans should not control knowledge beyond them. His notes survive in the Faded Castle.

In his notes, Ruggiero came to suspect that the Golden Hunter (Cassiodor) was a surviving Remurian. Bravais, a scholar, believed Ruggiero's accomplishments never got a fair assessment because of Fontaine's weak academic environment.

203.content:
The Traveler arrives to find the town strangely quiet and a gang of Treasure Hoarders hauling statues from the mountain ruins. After a revived golem attacks, a talking cat named Osse leads the Traveler through a deep spring to the Faded Castle, where they find a music box.

During the Canticles of Harmony quests, townsfolk such as Foscari, Goldoni and Grundeland are temporarily possessed by Remurian spirits (according to the wiki's NPC pages), which explains why their dialogue changes afterwards.

204.content:
Poisson (also: Poisson village): Poisson ("fish" in French) is a fishing village in the Belleau Region, at the foot of Mont Automnequi and built from a great ship and a large cavern below sea level. Its people mostly fish or salvage from underwater. It is the headquarters of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's home ground. In 4.2 an earthquake near Poisson sent Primordial Seawater flooding through the lower town, killing twelve people; it has since been rebuilt with Fatui help.

Legend says that before the first diluvian period Poisson was a central hub of Fontaine's maritime traffic, but changing water levels cost it its status as a major port. Visitors still come for its cosy, warm feel.

Geography: The village sits against Mont Automnequi, half in a cavern below sea level, with a huge ship making up part of the town. Lower streets run close to the water, and higher ground is where people fled in the flood. The nearby ruins to the south of town were investigated after the 4.2 flood.

There is no aquabus station near Poisson; Navia says most of the Spina's businesses do not use it as a hub, so she and the Traveler travel by one of the Spina's own boats.

Places: The Spina di Rosula's headquarters is in the village. The large ship is part of the town and appears in quests. The lower streets near the water were where people were dissolved in the 4.2 flood.

After the flood the survivors were housed in shelters while the town was rebuilt. A statue honouring Navia's parents, funded by donations from the residents, is planned.

People: Open-world residents include Alcina, Archenoul (the Spina's diver), Cava, Kosel (a porter), Melissa (a fisher), Munaciello, Rege, Sandino, Yvette (the engineer) and, after the flood begins, Vincenzo. Several are absent after the flood: some are in shelters, others are unlisted.

The Spina's Florent works closely with Navia on rebuilding. Colter, a friend of the late Melus, returned to Poisson after prison. Melus and Silver, Navia's bodyguards (listed on the Spina page as a butler and an attendant), died helping others in the flood.

Governance: Poisson has a mayor in its historical record, Renault de Petrichor, but today the Spina di Rosula administers the town in practice, as Navia herself says. After the flood the Court of Fontaine paid relief to victims, and Navia holds that the Spina should take its own share of responsibility.

Culture: A close-knit, working community of fishers, porters and salvagers, tied to the Spina. People call Navia "Boss". The town's people have donated for a statue to honour Callas and Clementine.

The Spina's founding story is tied here: Poisson is the Spina's place of origin and Navia says its headquarters are here. A long-standing dispute within the Spina, between Callas (who backed the aquabus lines) and Romeuf (who wanted the money spent on improving Poisson), runs through the village's recent history.

History: More than 500 years ago, shortly after the purge of Fleuve Cendre, the outlaw Eduardo Baker was being taken into exile when his followers freed him. With allies from near Mont Automnequi they seized Poisson and took Maison Gardiennage officers hostage, making unreasonable demands. The reporter Karl Ingold photographed Eduardo, his son Jakob, Mayor Renault de Petrichor and his son Rene, the magician "Parsifal", Rosa Reed with her husband and baby, and Tom Alter before the situation worsened. This became the Siege of Poisson.

The Marechaussee Hunter Emanuel Guillotin led the siege. The town was burned and many inhabitants died; Renault and his wife were likely killed. Rene and Jakob survived and were sent to the Narzissenkreuz Institute. "Parsifal" saved Karl Ingold, but was later arrested and died in a duel with Marfisa.

Three years before the game, Callas's partner Marcel secretly sold Sinthe (diluted Primordial Seawater) to the people of Poisson, and its abuse ruined families. Callas was later accused of a murder and chose to duel Clorinde. In 4.2 a quake near Poisson raised the water suddenly, and Primordial Seawater dissolved people near the water on the lower street. The Spina led rescue and evacuation, and Arlecchino's Fatui helped; Melus and Silver died in the rescue. The Fatui built a "Giant Magic Box" for the later staged trial of Furina, and Poisson was part of the lure.

Atmosphere: A warm, cosy fishing village before the flood; afterwards a half-empty one, where Navia says the living are too exhausted to find words for the dead. In the 4.3 story the town is busy with construction, with Navia making many trips between the Court and the village.

Dangers: Before 4.2 there was little danger. After the flood, the lower levels were hazardous because of Primordial Seawater, and the Spina asked residents to leave. In 4.3 Romeuf and his followers plotted to blow up the Clementine Line's supports and bury Poisson in rubble, but the Traveler and Navia stopped the plan and the Maison Gardiennage arrested them.

Travel: Poisson has no aquabus station; in Navia's story quest the Spina's own boat carries visitors from the Court of Fontaine.

Quests: Poisson features in the Archon Quest (Chapter IV, Act II As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, and Act V Masquerade of the Guilty, starting with Deluge of Wrathful Waters) and in Navia's story quest chain Braving the Tides Together (Rosa Multiflora Chapter, 4.3).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Poisson has been rebuilt after the 4.2 flood and remains the Spina di Rosula's headquarters. No later canon changes its state.

Rebuilding was still under way in 4.3, with Fatui help and with Navia and Florent overseeing it. Romeuf's faction was arrested. Clorinde laid low here for a time afterwards.

205.content:
A catastrophe before the cataclysm. After Eduardo Baker of Fleuve Cendre was seized in the purge and freed by his men, he and allies occupied Poisson and took Maison Gardiennage staff hostage. Marechaussee Hunters under Emanuel Guillotin ended the incident with the town burned and many killed. Rene de Petrichor and Jakob survived to join the Narzissenkreuz Institute.

Item texts disagree on who bears blame; Rene's notes blame the Gardiennage's lackeys and Guillotin's role. The Doge of Petrichor recalls that Renault, the last patrono of Petrichor, lost his life as Poisson's mayor.

206.content:
In Deluge of Wrathful Waters the ground shakes near Poisson and the water level rises quickly. The water turns out to contain Primordial Seawater, which dissolves Fontainians, and those on the lower street disappear. A stampede follows on higher ground. The Spina organises rescue; Arlecchino's Fatui help. Twelve people die, including Navia's bodyguards Melus and Silver.

Neuvillette connects the flood to the Primordial Sea, and after it the Traveler, Neuvillette and the Spina lure Furina into a staged trial. Neuvillette later restores power that prevents Fontainians from dissolving in the Primordial Sea.

207.content: Romeuf was a Spina member who thought the aquabus money should improve Poisson. He left the Spina when Callas and Clementine chose to go ahead with the aquabus lines. In Navia's story quest Braving the Tides Together, he and his followers plan to bomb the Clementine Line's supports to bury Poisson in rubble and Colter attempts to assassinate Navia; the plan fails and they are arrested.

208.content: Sinthe was a popular drink in Poisson that was actually diluted Primordial Seawater. Its long-term effects were severe, and it wrecked many families. Callas banned it and began investigating its sellers.

209.content:
Poisson Tunnel (also: The Poisson Tunnel): The Poisson Tunnel is the passage carved through the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi so that the Clementine aquabus line can run beneath the mountain, between the Court of Fontaine and Romaritime Harbor. The Fontaine Research Institute dug it with newly built engineering machines, including the "Golden Vessel".

The success of the tunnel project is credited with sparking a new generation of clockwork technology, including the Construction Specialist Mek.

Geography: Cuts through the West Slopes of Mont Automnequi in the Belleau Region. The aquabus guide Aeval notes that the mountain lies between the port and the Court and is not very steep, but a route round the summit would be too unstable for a small boat, hence the tunnel. It is named for the nearby town of Poisson.

Passengers see it lit by Fontaine-exclusive night lights powered by Indemnitium, a contrast Aeval draws with the fluorescent materials of Sumeru and the torches of other lands. She adds that when the line first opened the tunnel was badly lit, dark and creepy enough to make some young passengers cry.

History: According to the wiki's lore, the Fontaine Research Institute brought in huge engineering devices and developed new machines, among them the "Golden Vessel", to bore the tunnel. The project's success pushed the Institute to develop more advanced clockwork meka for wider use.

The Construction Specialist Mek's archive text says the mek type is named for an engineer employed by Callas during the Clementine Line's construction; with Callas' backing the engineer built the Golden Vessel, and the mek was later designed with a similar structure at smaller scale. Per Aeval, the Poisson House of Caspar supported the project; when it joined the construction, local fears about the line faded.

According to the wiki, Callas' wife Clementine died giving birth to their daughter Navia, after which Callas funded the aquabus system; its lines are the Callas, Clementine and Navia lines. The sources seen do not say outright that the Clementine Line is named for her. Aeval presents the line as a monument to Fontaine's scientific progress, but also remarks that few people use it.

Travel: Aquabuses of the Clementine Line, operated by Aeval, run from the Court of Fontaine Main Station to Romaritime Station and pass through the tunnel. Aeval's tour commentary changes between trips and often mentions the tunnel.

Atmosphere: A long, glowing bore through rock, lit by Indemnitium lamps and watched over by a cheerful Melusine guide telling stories about the project.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tunnel is in use for the Clementine Line.

210.content: The "Golden Vessel" was a gigantic piece of construction machinery built with Callas' financial backing and used to dig the Poisson Tunnel. The Construction Specialist Mek, a large clockwork meka valued for building and archaeological excavation, was later designed with a similar structure at smaller scale.

211.content:
Portus Anticus (also: Where Only the Bell Tolls): In its prime the port had a lofty bell tower whose bells were said to carry through the ocean's barrier and guide sailors home; the viewpoint text imagines lost souls still hearing them. It once held the emperor Remus' prized imperial ship, the Fortuna. It was added in Version 4.6.

Its map has two levels, an upper and a lower one, and ancient engravings in the cavern record military orders from the last days of Remuria.

Geography: A great cavern beneath the waves, the remains of a harbour that once received ships of the Remurian court. The map is divided into an upper and a lower level.

History: Remuria's royal port, with a belltower and the Fortuna, Remus' imperial ship, as described in the Remuria history book that the location page cites.

Engravings in the ruins preserve several documents and one lament. One orders the defence line at the northern harbour withdrawn on the authority of a special envoy named Faunus of Legio V, redirecting troops toward Caesareum Palace, and sets Legio IX to hold the flank against the Dragonborn. A later order, in the name of the Harmost Boethius and in accord with Sebastos Remus' melody, tells Legio V to stop hostilities against the Dragonborn and return to the palace, while Legios VII and IX seal Portus Anticus against northern barbarian attacks so talks are not disturbed. A third engraving is a bitter poem addressed to Faunus about the razing of the city of Lugdunensis and the spoils of war.

Taken together, the engravings show the port as a military position in Remuria's war with the Dragonborn and then as a guarded site during peace talks. The speakers (Remurian officers) refer to their enemies in contemptuous terms such as "savages"; treat those as in-world Remurian views, not narrator fact.

Atmosphere: Vast, flooded and echoing; a drowned harbour whose only remembered sound is its bell, with the cavern's dark water holding the sense of ships that never came home.

Travel: Found in the Sea of Bygone Eras of Fontaine, reached from the Remuria ruins. The viewpoint "Where Only the Bell Tolls" is located here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing further has changed; it remains an underwater cavern ruin of Remuria.

212.content: Fortuna was Remus' prized imperial ship, said to have been kept at the royal port of Portus Anticus.

213.content:
Quartier Lyonnais (also: Court of Fontaine: Quartier Lyonnais): Quartier Lyonnais is a street of shops along the northeastern side of the Court of Fontaine. The Fontaine branch of the Adventurers' Guild is here, alongside clockmakers, a boutique and a shop of curiosities.

It is a commercial district rather than a civic one, with shopkeepers, adventurers and a member of the Gardes among its listed residents. It was part of Fontaine from its first release in 4.0.

Places: Along the street: the Adventurers' Guild branch (receptionist Katheryne); Lepaute Horlogerie, a clock shop managed by Caron; Leschots Clockwork Workshop, whose boss is Livre; the Chioriya Boutique, with Eloffe on staff; and Bertin's House of Curiosities, managed by Mequignon. A rotunda west of the Guild branch has a Fontaine Script sign that appears to say d'avocats.

Behind the rotunda stands a Luxurious Chest. Paimon reads a note in it, from someone who planned to flee to another nation with the money so long as their "Champion Duelist" won, adding that the signature's date shows the schemer did not get away.

People: Residents and workers include Caron (Lepaute Horlogerie), Eloffe (Chioriya Boutique), Livre (Leschots), Mequignon (Bertin's), Katheryne (Adventurers' Guild), Ophelia (an adventurer), Santallier (a member of the Gardes), Savinien (Champion Duelist) and several shopkeepers and passers-by such as Graciette, Ligniere, Trudaine, Veta and Xugney.

Atmosphere: A bright, well-kept shopping street: shop signs, clock and curiosity shops, and adventurers visiting the Guild branch. Treat finer details as scene dressing, not canon.

Travel: The district is on the northeastern side of the Court of Fontaine. The Guild branch is the easiest landmark to find; the rotunda lies to its west.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded; it remains an ordinary shopping street.

214.content: Savinien is listed as the Champion Duelist among the NPCs of Quartier Lyonnais. The note found in the Luxurious Chest behind the rotunda mentions a "Champion Duelist" whose winning the writer relied on; the wiki's chest text does not name him, so the link is only suggestive.

215.content:
Quartier Narbonnais (also: Court of Fontaine: Quartier Narbonnais): Quartier Narbonnais lies on the southwestern side of the Court of Fontaine. It is home to The Steambird, the city's main newspaper, and to Hotel Debord, a famous restaurant, and it is considered a place to find the newest fashion and perfume.

The newspaper's offices, a salon of civic debaters and a theatrical dining house sit side by side, so the district is where Fontaine's press, public talk and entertainment meet.

Places: The Steambird: Fontaine's main newspaper, read across Teyvat; Euphrasie is its Chief Editor and Sir Arthur belongs to the paper; Ethan is a reporter there. Hotel Debord: a famous restaurant whose owner Vaneigem holds that art is the best seasoning for good food and often invites artists to perform; Sanguinetti hosts the food shop. Salon Caritat: the headquarters of an advocacy group that, by its notices, studies law and the administration of justice.

The Steambird columns include All Things Astrological by Mona, who took over from the previous columnist, and it employs reporters, a photographer and a newsy (see its own entry). Hotel Debord has downstairs and upstairs areas: Eloise (a critic), Leone and Argalia (hostesses) and Rodamonte and Renaud are listed among its people. A notice board advertises a show promising that "the most dazzling twin stars" of the Court will reveal a secret. Salon Caritat's notice announces its 36th symposium, on budget overruns in the Maison Gardiennage and their link to public safety.

People: Besides the above: Justeau and Riqueti of Salon Caritat, Hubel (newsstand owner), Angelique, Chesil and Guillem. A discount applies at Hotel Debord for players with Reputation Rank 4 in Fontaine (a game feature).

Culture: The district is where Fontaine goes to read, dine and be seen: news, fashion and perfume are its reputation, and civic debate has its own club. An NPC (Sylvie) mentions its fashion and perfume.

Atmosphere: Newsstands, printing-house bustle, polished restaurant frontage and the chatter of salon members.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded.

The wiki ties the district's name only speculatively to a sword called Narbonnais in a Fontaine book; treat the name as unexplained in-world.

216.content: The main newspaper of the Court of Fontaine, read across Teyvat. Its offices are in Quartier Narbonnais. Staff include Euphrasie (Chief Editor), Charlotte, Chronie, Ethan, Paban and others; Nellie Cochran is listed as a historical Chief Editor who interviewed Alain Guillotin centuries ago. Mona writes the astrology column All Things Astrological. A separate entity covers the paper.

217.content: A famous restaurant in Quartier Narbonnais. Its owner, Vaneigem, believes "art is the best seasoning for good food", and the hotel regularly hosts artists. The interior is designed so guests can watch the performances. Staff listed include Sanguinetti (host), Leone, Argalia, Eloise (a critic), Renaud and Rodamonte.

218.content:
Rag and Bone Shop: The Rag and Bone Shop is a small shop in the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison. Its owner, Alvard, sells all sorts of goods to inmates, who pay in Credit Coupons, a currency used only inside the fortress.

The in-game map description calls it the best-stocked non-official merchandise store in the fortress: anything from Hydro Phantasm taint cleaners to support items for the Pankration Ring can be had there, provided the buyer has coupons. It sits in the southeast part of the Administrative Area and was added in Version 4.1 with the Meropide content.

Places: The shop is a counter run by Alvard in the southeast of the Administrative Area. Alvard is friends with Chamboduc and with Wriothesley, the Duke who runs the fortress; Chamboduc minds the shop when Alvard is out restocking.

The Welfare Meal handed out free by Wolsey is the only thing in the area that costs nothing: Alvard jokes that the only free thing in his shop is the air.

Culture: The shop is part of the fortress's coupon economy. Credit Coupons are earned from small jobs and favours, so a purchase here is either a minor luxury or a practical necessity. Alvard's patter is "you need it, we got it", but he values discretion: he will not say where his goods come from, and whether he takes orders depends on who is asking and for what.

During the world quest Game of the Rich the girl Lanoire is taken to the shop; for that scene the shelves show a thematic stock of sold-out toys, food and curios, which is flavour only and cannot be bought. The real stock is a handful of one-off items such as bottled "Pure Water", blueprints, and Genius Invokation TCG goods (a card back and an event card), some of which stay reserved until the quest The Art of Negotiation is done. Buying everything grants the Consumer Society achievement.

The regular stock is paid for in Credit Coupons and includes a vending machine item, two blueprints (a Linden Wood bunk and one called Majesty of the Forbidden Fortress), the Fortress of Meropide card back and an item titled The Art of Negotiation. The wiki counts 4,560 coupons available in the fortress outside the Archon Quest, enough to buy out both this shop and the Coupon Cafeteria with nothing left over.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of Version 7.1.

Once every item has been bought the shop icon disappears from the map, but Alvard can still be found at his counter and has extra dialogue.

219.content: Alvard owns the Rag and Bone Shop in the Fortress of Meropide. He is a salesman first: breezy, a little sly and unwilling to name his suppliers, though he insists his goods are safe and fairly priced. He is friends with Chamboduc, who covers for him when he is away, and with the Duke Wriothesley.

220.content:
Remuria (also: Kingdom of Remuria, Empire of Remuria, Pax Remuria, Eternal City, Undersea Capital): Remuria was the empire of the god Remus, who called himself the God King and was known to his people as the Sebastos or Imperator. He founded it on the waters of what is now Fontaine, before the Hydro Archon Egeria ruled. It prospered on music and art, its capital was Capitolium, and its emblem was a golden bee. It was prophesied to face utter destruction, and Remus's attempts to avoid that destiny wrecked it. It drowned in a single catastrophe and now lies in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Remuria is the setting of the 4.6 World Quest series Canticles of Harmony, when the buried Grand Symphony Phobos stirred again beneath Petrichor. Its survivors and descendants, the Golden Troupe and the Marechaussee Hunters, shaped some of Fontaine's hidden history, and its golem bodies and ruined palaces are still found across Fontaine.

Geography: The empire spread over the "high waters", the great lake of Fontaine, by conquering islands and building long fairways called the Alta Semita that carried the music of the capital outwards. The capital had two parts: the outer city Machimos, where the warriors lived and which held ports, temples and arenas, and the inner city Capitolium, reached only through the Initium Iani and the Passage of Ianus. A bell tower at the port guided ships between islands.

Today the ruins are two areas: the Faded Castle, once the Harmosts' archive on the shore, and the Sea of Bygone Eras, which holds Machimos (Caesareum Palace, Hortus Euergetis, Portus Anticus) and Capitolium with Domus Aurea. These waters have the same nature as Fontaine's water.

Government: Remus ruled as an authority above all others, but shared governance with four humans of exceptional ability, the Harmosts, who ruled the cities. They were Boethius, Cassiodor, Aurelius and Euergetia. Only the most gifted intellectuals and musicians served the God King directly. Everyday decisions of the "ascended" Remurians came to depend on Phobos, which handed down the course they should take.

Legions with numbers such as Legio VI Rithimi Versi and Legio IX served under the Harmosts. Boethius commanded the force that fought Scylla; Euergetia pacified the northern barbarian border; Aurelius completed an earlier northern campaign among island tribes without violence.

Culture: Music defined Remuria. Remus believed it separated people from other living things, and taught the early Fontainians farming, house building and the arts. Conch shells were used as instruments, and in mourning, Remurians cast harps of black iron that could not be played, their silence being symbolic. Capitolium was a paradise of theatres and palaces with carved beams, with a palace of copper pillars at its heart.

Harmost writing on music in the Faded Castle distinguishes three kinds: the music of the world (Musica Mundana), the music of mortals and gods (Musica Humana) and the music of instruments (Musica Instrumentalis). The Harmosts studied scripts, scores and all possible stories in the castle in order to understand fate, which Remurians called Fortuna.

Religion: Remus was god and king. The seers, among them Sybilla and her fellow golden bees, prophesied that the greatest empire would meet the most utter destruction. Remurians thought of fate as Fortuna, a rule that governs all things, and the Grand Symphony was Remus's attempt to take that power away from it. Outside their borders, northern tribes revered Egeria, the Mistress of Waters, in many forms.

History: After the first civilisation fell to flood, Fontaine had no real civilisation for a very long age. Remus arrived in his ship and brought agriculture, cities and music. Seers prophesied that his empire would be utterly destroyed, so he built the Grand Symphony, Phobos, and put the souls of his people into immortal bodies to escape fate. Phobos magnified the cruellest wishes of the ascended Remurians, they went to war with the other peoples of Fontaine, and in the end a tsunami drowned the empire.

Remus took the advice of the seer Sybilla and visited Egeria, then imprisoned in the Primordial Sea. Scylla, a vishap prince guarding her cell, fought him for thirty days before letting him pass. Egeria gave him a goblet of primordial water, which he mixed with an immortal stone to make golden Ichor. Remurians turned into "ascended" souls in golem bodies that the sea could not dissolve. Sybilla gave her life to make Phobos.

Remuria declared war on the "barbarian" tribes, Lochfolk and vishaps. The resistance, the Lochknights, formed around Erinnyes. Remus, waking in sorrow, separated Cassiodor from the Symphony so he could act freely, and secretly arranged with Scylla for a fake betrayal. Phobos learned of it and guided Boethius to sabotage it. Scylla was lured into a trap and sealed at the Initium Iani. Boethius refused Remus's order to end the war. Remus presumably triggered the Requiem; with no one to control the power, great waves swallowed the capital and its invaders alike.

Afterwards the survivors lived as barbarians until Egeria returned to settle conflicts. Fontaine as it exists was founded by Egeria at its spring waters. Boethius survived and founded the Golden Troupe to revive Remuria; Cassiodor, as the Golden Hunter and head of the Marechaussee Hunters, opposed him and eventually broke Boethius's soul, sealing the pieces in the palace.

People: Remus; the seer Sybilla; the four Harmosts; the vishap prince Scylla; and the many golem soldiers and musicians. Este the Quick-Witted, a Remurian legionnaire seen only in memory, has a living Fontainian descendant in Petrichor. Cassiodor adopted a cat's form and the name Osse.

Aetius and his sister Placidia (Legio VI) left an epitaph in Caesareum Palace. Hirtius, vicarius of Legio VI, wrote a survey of the northern tribes. The Aremorica leader Erinnyes opposed the empire, and an earlier chief, Cunoricus, bowed to it about twenty years before that survey.

Status as of 7.1: Only ruins, golems and memory remain. In Version 4.6, Phobos was finally ended and its souls went to the sea; Remuria is no longer a threat.

Remurian descendants live as ordinary Fontainians. Remus's story is still told in books, many half-forgotten, and the Golden Troupe's own distortions of it confused historians.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems still guard the ruins, and vishaps such as the Primordial Bathysmal Vishap live in the deep. Before the Requiem, the symphony could pull souls from the living; this is no longer a risk.

Atmosphere: Gold leaf and rust, sunk music, weighty stone voices that speak as if the war were still on, and a sorrowful calm. The prevailing mood is of an ancient dream slowly released.

221.content: The four human rulers who shared Remus's power: Boethius, Cassiodor, Aurelius and Euergetia. Euergetia is remembered by Cassiodor as kind, almost a sister; Boethius grew arrogant and contemptuous of non-Remurians, while Cassiodor, who came from a tribe Remuria conquered, joined the empire and later opposed what it became. Remus cut Cassiodor off from the Symphony to keep his free will. Each Harmost could also bend the Symphony's power; Euergetia could make conquered people vividly taste their native dishes.

222.comment: Remuria: Golden Ichor and the Ascended Remurians
222.content:
Remus mixed primordial water with an immortal stone to make golden Ichor, which held the minds and souls of his people. They were moved into stone golems with Ichor for blood so they could survive the coming flood. The result was immortality, but also pride; many came to see non-Remurians as lesser. In the present day, some descendants remain ordinary Fontainians.

Boethius says that he and Cassiodor were new humans crafted by Remus's own hand and are the last survivors, and that Cassiodor's soul is like insoluble Ichor. Ruined golems are still found in the wild; later folklore painted even the greatest scholars as soul-stealing magisters who bound mortal spirits into golems, which the book's author blames on the moral decay of Remuria's final days.

223.comment: Remuria: Phobos and the Grand Symphony
223.content: Remus and Sybilla made the Grand Symphony to avert the prophecy and free humans from Fortuna. Sybilla had no will of her own and wanted to make humans happy, so Phobos satisfied whatever the Remurians wished, including slaughter and conquest. In Fortune Plango Vulnera Phobos itself speaks, calling itself the sum of all souls. Remus tried to end it with the Requiem, and the Traveler eventually played that Requiem.

224.comment: Remuria: The War on the Tribes
224.content: The Faded Castle notes by the Vicarius Hirtius paint northern tribes as crude savages, but admit some, like Lugdunensis, ruled by a holy king, were more developed. Legio V razed that city; the Harmost Boethius destroyed another city and erased its name. The resistance formed by tribes who worshipped Egeria, led by Erinnyes, joined the rebellion that Scylla led, at Remus's secret request, against Remuria. Their agony is said to have woken Remus.

225.content: Boethius gathered survivors in the Faded Castle to revive Remuria; their research and goals later shaped Fontaine's hidden history. The Phobos page links Remurian arts that survived the fall to the later Narzissenkreuz Ordo, which drew on what it learned of the Golden Troupe; the sources leave most of the details unsaid. Cassiodor's Marechaussee Hunters stood against them.

226.content:
Rift of Erosion: The Rift of Erosion is a point of interest in the Fortress of Meropide, west of the Dormitory Block in the Administrative Area. It is called a "potential danger" and is guarded by Galvana.

Little else is stated. Galvana muses about sealing it off, and a locking mechanism like the one used here is later requested at the Geode Mine Shaft.

Geography: Located to the west of the Dormitory Block, Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide.

Galvana notes that the space is not small and would be good to put to use, while also agreeing it would be safer to seal it off.

When the Traveler jokes about sealing every entrance and exit, Galvana finds that extreme, and she blames the frequent breakage of searchlights on their installed energy storage devices or on people ignoring the instructions.

People: Galvana stands guard at the rift until the quest Scenes from Life in Meropide: Dead End is completed, after which she moves to outside the elevator to the lower Production Zone. She has a younger twin sister, Galvaryet, and prefers to be serious during work hours.

History: Guards had Clynes install a locking mechanism at the Geode Mine Shaft "like the one at the Rift of Erosion", as noted in An Eye for an Eye.

Dangers: Treated by its guard as a potential danger; the rift's actual hazard is not described.

Status as of 7.1: Guarded and unchanged as of 7.1 apart from Galvana's relocation after the Dead End quest.

227.content:
River Talionis: River Talionis is a small wharf beneath the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine, the external reception area of the Fortress of Meropide. A single boat carries prisoners through an underground tunnel straight to the Fortress.

New inmates are registered here before the crossing. The receptionist, Marette, handles the paperwork, including recording that a sentence has been served.

The place sits where Fontaine's court system meets the autonomous prison: sentencing happens above, and the sentence begins at this wharf.

The name is Latin-styled; the wiki reads it as "River of Retribution" after the phrase lex talionis, a translation note rather than in-game text.

Geography: The wharf lies under the Opera Epiclese, where Fontaine's trials are held, and is reached by an elevator behind the opera house. It has a small dock with one boat, which runs through an underground tunnel to the Fortress of Meropide.

This is the Fortress's formal front door; other ways in (the spotlights around the prison, a broken pipe leading to the dormitories) are unofficial.

People: Marette is the Fortress of Meropide Receptionist. She is a little sleepy and procedural (her idle line asks you to register), remembers the Traveler and Paimon as the pair the Iudex had personally escorted over, and tells them not to make waves until their sentence is complete.

After Step 4 of Deluge of Wrathful Waters she updates the Traveler's file, declares the sentence officially served and says they are free to go.

Governance: The Fortress of Meropide is Fontaine's de facto prison but is technically self-governing and outside the jurisdiction of Fontaine's legal system; those sent there are in effect exiles. The Court of Fontaine only sends some Garde to help with security (per A Tea Party Most Thorny). The reception wharf is the formal point where a convicted person passes from one authority to the other.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wharf is unchanged in the sources read.

228.content: River Talionis is the external reception area of the Fortress of Meropide, a wharf beneath the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine with one boat that ferries prisoners to the Fortress through an underground tunnel. It is reached by an elevator behind the opera house. The receptionist is Marette.

229.content: Marette is the Fortress of Meropide Receptionist at River Talionis. She registers arriving prisoners and records the end of sentences. She remembers the Traveler as someone the Iudex had escorted in personally, which she notes is unusual.

230.content:
Romaritime Harbor (also: Romaritime Station): Romaritime Harbor is a large coastal elevator and observation deck built into a waterfall on Fontaine's edge. A lift carries people between the harbor below and the top of the falls, where the Clementine Line aquabus runs on rails to the Court of Fontaine. It is also the way to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru, and Aeval calls Romaritime Station "one of the great gateways of Fontaine".

Its name joins the French words for rosemary (romarin) and maritime.

Geography: The harbor has a lower level at the waterline and an upper level reached by the great lift, which takes a long time even by elevator. The thundering waterfall drowns out the noise of arrivals below. A Statue of the Seven and a Waverider waypoint are here, and the aquabus line begins at the top.

The harbor lies in the Belleau Region. The Maison Gardiennage's notice warns visitors to follow the prescribed route and use the lift, and disclaims responsibility for injuries from gliders or other dangerous shortcuts.

Places: The lower level has the docks and a security post; the upper level has the aquabus station and the harbor's Navbed, Rena, who handles queries about the aquabus. A bulletin board outside the lift carries the Harbormaster's notices.

According to the Clementine Line tour, the great lift was designed to work on several energy sources.

An engineer riding the aquabus, Edwin Eastinghouse, spoke of a mysterious Arkhium that could lift even heavier things, and wanted to use it to raise cargo ships from below the station; Aeval says this was probably not a joke.

People: Lower level: Augereau (a member of the Gardes), Baguette (the harborworker hound), Etienne (harbor security), Everallin (Marechaussee Phantom) and Lectoure (a sailor). Upper level: Baiji, Cheriez, Galathee (boat captain), Hermosa (a self-proclaimed adventurer), Rena, Siora (Marechaussee Phantom) and Zadra. Melusine guides such as Aeval run the aquabus tours.

Melusines work as aquabus guides in uniform; the Marechaussee Phantom is largely made up of Melusines.

Governance: A Harbormaster issues notices; the Maison Gardiennage polices the harbor, with Gardes and Marechaussee Phantom on site. All duelling in Fontaine requires registration, and unapproved duels are banned.

Culture: The bulletin board tells visitors to check local rules, avoid homemade potions, use licensed divers and beware of scams. One ad offers dive services at 30,000 Mora per minute, and a reply points out that even Freminet, the best diver around, does not charge that much.

Aeval, the Melusine guide of the Clementine Line, cheerfully narrates the journey; one of her tour talks covers the Steambird's serialised novels and Merusea Village.

History: The harbor provides passage to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru. The Callas Line, a sister aquabus route, was suspended after the Fontaine Research Institute's explosion; the Clementine Line is the line that ends here.

In the finale of Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2), the Traveler and Charlotte meet Lyney, Lynette and Freminet at the harbor; Lyney says their "Father" has been given the Hydro Gnosis, and Arlecchino appears, saying that as a Harbinger it is her duty to hand it to the Tsaritsa. In Chapter V (5.0), the Traveler says goodbye to Fontaine friends, including Furina, Navia, Clorinde and Charlotte, at the docks before leaving for Natlan.

Atmosphere: The official description stresses the thunder of the waterfall drowning out the harbor's comings and goings, and a wait for the lift that is forgotten once the Clementine Line carries you toward the heart of the nation of Hydro.

Dangers: Mostly everyday hazards: the lift's long ascent, unsafe gliding, and Eremites active in the nearby desert, which the Maison Gardiennage warns merchants about. The notice board also warns that Fontaine's currents can be treacherous for unlicensed divers.

Travel: Clementine Line aquabus: Court of Fontaine main station to Romaritime Station (the terminus). Passage onward to the Girdle of the Sands in Sumeru. Visitors can call an aquabus from the bench if none is at the station.

The planned Lumidouce Harbor line, serving the other major harbor in Erinnyes Forest, has not been built.

Quests: Features in the Archon Quest finale of Chapter IV (4.2), the start of Chapter V Act I, Natlan! A New Adventure (5.0), and many Fontaine journeys. The Clementine Line is named for Navia's late mother.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Romaritime Harbor is a working port and aquabus terminus. No later canon changes its state.

The bulletin board still lists the Callas Line as suspended indefinitely; according to the Aquabus entry Navia decided afterwards to rebuild it and add stops. The Traveler left for Natlan from here in 5.0.

231.content:
The Clementine Line is the aquabus line between the Court of Fontaine and Romaritime Station, operated by the Melusine guide Aeval. It was named for Clementine, Navia's late mother, and the system was designed with Callas's cooperation. The engineer considered a second waterway for cargo but dropped it because there was no demand.

Callas's insistence on building the aquabus lines led Romeuf to break away from the Spina; after the Prophecy of Fontaine was dealt with, Romeuf's faction tried to topple the line's supports to bury Poisson.

232.comment: Romaritime Harbor: Romaritime Harbor Bulletin Board
232.content: A notice board outside the lift. Messages cycle through: station notices, duelling rules, a Maison Gardiennage warning about Eremites near the desert, safety rules for the lift and aquabus, a diver's ad and replies, lost property, and notes about travel to the Fontaine Research Institute.

233.content:
Roots of Erinnyes (also: Depths of Erinnyes, Hauteclaire): The Roots of Erinnyes are a network of subterranean caverns and water veins beneath the island of Erinnyes in Fontaine, in the region of Erinnyes Forest. Its waters work as an information system, and the central part is called Hauteclaire. Many of its channels lead up to the Weeping Willow of the Lake. In the 4.2 world quest series The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes, the Traveler cleanses it of corruption alongside a strange Melusine named Pahsiv.

Pahsiv explains, in broken words, that all of Erinnyes is an information system whose centre is the roots: willows collect, fog handles and springs send. A powerful "visitor" who protects Fontaine uses it to sense evil, so its destruction would blind that guardian.

Geography: Below Erinnyes Forest, a labyrinth of caverns and water veins connects springs, the lake and the great willow. The way in is a hidden passage under the square at Marcotte Station, opened by inserting three Teardrop (Waterdrop) Keys into the statues at the fountain there. By Pahsiv's directions, the keys lie along the foggy path to the south, at the spring to the north and by the willows to the east.

Deeper down, the passage leads through underwater stretches to the roots themselves, which are the roots of the great willow in the lake; when they are corrupted the tree looks sickly and the lake turns yellow. The roots lie "very far, very deep", as Pahsiv puts it.
