On the surface, Erinnyes Forest has puzzles that use the Xenochromatic Ball Octopus (Contaminated Bacterial Mats, Dew Bubbles, Harmonious Reed Pipes, and so on). After the cleansing, six non-hostile Primordial Bathysmal Vishap Hatchlings appear along the river between the forest's Statue of the Seven and Loch Urania.

Places: The Weeping Willow of the Lake stands at the centre of a lake and its roots seem to extend underwater. Its condition is tied to the health of the water veins: before the cleansing the whole lake area appears sickly yellow, afterwards vibrant blue. Marcotte Station, with its fountain and square, hides the entrance.

Elsewhere on the island of Erinnyes stand the Opera Epiclese, the Fountain of Lucine and the ruins of the Fontaine Research Institute on the north side. The wiki's Erinnyes island page cites the NPC Elphane as saying that Neuvillette considers exploring the depths of Erinnyes ill-advised.

People: Pahsiv, listed as a Melusine, speaks only in single words and was named by Paimon; Paimon notes that she acts more like a wild fairy than an ordinary Melusine. She protects the roots from a "purple thing", scratched the writing from the stone tablet, and vanishes after the cleansing without asking for a reward, though she comes back with a chest for Paimon. The brothers Remaudiere and Keratry are among the people in the Marcotte Station square above.

Dangers: Corruption: dark filth and a Root-Consuming Tumour at the heart of the roots. The tumour's destruction triggers an arcane formation from which Rifthounds (Thundercraven and Rockfond Rifthound Whelps) pour. Late in the fight a Primordial Bathysmal Vishap joins the player's side. Afterwards the Local Legend Mageblade Corrouge appears where the tumour was.

Before the cleansing an enraged Primordial Bathysmal Vishap has to be subdued at the spring (the quest Furious Mouth of the Spring); Pahsiv says the unnamed purple thing fought a "blue thing", which suggests a vishap, and the blue thing "lost lots".

Atmosphere: Fog, willows and reed pipes above; below, flooded passages and a root chamber that Paimon calls "a whole load of funky stuff", with the party always aware that something evil lurks nearby. After the final fight a sudden rise of water carries the Traveler and Paimon up to the surface.

Quests: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes (4.2): Foggy Forest Path, Wilting Weeping Willow and Furious Mouth of the Spring (three concurrent quests, each yielding a key) lead to Within the Depths of Erinnyes. The Traveler also needs to have done The Outlander Who Caught the Wind for Furious Mouth of the Spring.

In Within the Depths of Erinnyes the Traveler and Paimon insert the three keys, descend, cleanse the filth around the root, defeat the tumour and Rifthounds, and are washed up on the surface, where the willow has recovered.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the roots are cleansed and healthy. The willow is vibrant blue, and no later content has changed the area.

Pahsiv vanished at the end of the quest and reappeared briefly with a chest; where she is now is not stated. Paimon wants to visit her often and teach her more words.

234.content:
In the official text, Hauteclaire names the central part of the Roots of Erinnyes. The wiki also records Hauteclaire as the name of the sword of the historical Erinnyes, High King of Aremorica, better known as the weapon Splendor of Tranquil Waters; in the book La Chanson d'Erinnyes, a retelling that takes liberties, she throws it into a lake. The link between the two is not explained, and the name echoes the sword of Oliver in the French Song of Roland.

The weapon's story says the sword sank into the lake beside Egeria's blessings after her judgment, and the knight walked away never to be seen again.

235.content:
A Melusine who stays in Erinnyes Forest and speaks in single words, using "Pahsiv" for "yes" and "Melusine" for "no", as Paimon works out. She wants the Traveler's help to stop the Erinnyes water veins from failing and gives them a quiet reward at the end. She fears the purple thing but guards the roots.

She says the water vein carries the "visitor" lots of information, tastes evil and senses it. She scratched the writing off the stone tablet to hinder the purple thing, and when the Traveler is exhausted she touches their stomach to give them warmth and strength.

236.comment: Roots of Erinnyes: Erinnyes the High King
236.content: Erinnyes, a historical Lochknight and High King of Aremorica in the last years of Remuria, united the tribes of Fontaine against the Remurian Empire. She wielded the Splendor of Tranquil Waters, which the wiki identifies as the sword Hauteclaire, and swore with her knights to protect the Oceanids. After Egeria told her that Egeria herself had created humans from Oceanids, her faith broke and she left, never seen again. The island and forest are likely named after her; the Roots may share the name.

237.content:
Sacellum Requietis (also: The Sacellum Requietis, throne room of Domus Aurea): The Sacellum Requietis is the throne room of Domus Aurea, the royal palace of Remuria. The God King Remus once ruled from it. In Version 4.6 it is where the Traveler silences the Grand Symphony Phobos at the end of the Canticles of Harmony quest chain.

Canon says very little about the room itself, so its meaning comes from what happened around it: the palace was the instrument of Phobos, and this chamber is where its sound was ended.

Geography: It lies on the upper level of Domus Aurea, in the Clivus Capitolinus area of the Sea of Bygone Eras. Players reach the upper level by lift after the final fight, and the quest then points to a podium where the Requiem is played on a harp.

History: The room is where Remus held court. According to the old book on Remuria, the king rested at the heart of the palace, listening to every melody and note from across the empire and correcting any discord with a pluck of his strings. He used that position to guide his people's symphony.

In the present, Boethius planned a ritual in the palace to take on flesh. After Boethius and Phobos were defeated and Cassiodor faded, the Traveler went to the upper level and played the final Requiem, Remus's final symphony, an order for the Grand Symphony to end, and the souls bound to it went on towards the sea.

A viewpoint called "Domus Requiem" opens in the palace after the quest, and its text is a prayer that the dead be granted eternal rest and that light shine on them always. A music box tune named Tears of Days Past, which shares the Requiem motif, is also tied to this place.

The Requiem leitmotif is shared by three pieces of music in the game: Whisper of Domus Aurea, which plays while the harp is played in the quest, Tears of Days Past, and Lacrimosa, the sixth score of the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box, which the player unlocks at the end of the quest.

Status as of 7.1: Peaceful since the Requiem. Phobos is gone and the palace is silent.

Two viewpoints open in the palace after the story, one of them "Domus Requiem".

Atmosphere: Hush and gold, a stage emptied of its conductor. A scene here should feel like attending a funeral after a long war, with a distant echo of choral music.

238.comment: Sacellum Requietis: The Silencing of Phobos
238.content: After the fight with Boethius, Cassiodor asks the Traveler to complete the final Requiem for his Imperator's wishes. Scylla explains that completing Remus's last symphony will send the souls back to the present and into the great sea, where they will join the current and one day be reborn as mortals. The Traveler plays the harp at the podium; the souls follow a golden bee upward, and the people of Petrichor recover.

239.content:
Salacia Plain: Salacia Plain is an open, serene stretch of crystal-clear sea in the Court of Fontaine Region. It is explored with the blessing of the Transoceanic Sourcewater, which lets travellers pass here unhindered, and it is home to sea creatures such as the Angelic Sea Hares and the singing Blubberbeasts.

Official text calls it a place where many precious memories and secrets still slumber beneath the glittering surface. It belongs to the underwater world around the capital, in the same map level as "Source of All Waters: The Great Fontaine Lake".

Geography: Open sea water with currents, seagrass and sea-floor features, near the Court of Fontaine and the Opera Epiclese. The surrounding sea is full of explorable underwater mechanisms.

Exploration features listed there: Accelerated Aquaring, Bullet Barnacles, currents, Fontemer Seagrass, High-Pressure Water Vents, Pneumousia Blocks and Relays, Recovery Orbs, Seelies, time trial challenges and Xenochromatic Creatures. Fishing is possible at the Western Shoal.

Atmosphere: Calm, bright, and clear: current-borne music, sunlit water and slow-moving sea life. The official site invites visitors to swim alongside the Sea Hares, listen to the Blubberbeasts' song and let the "music of the currents" guide them.

Dangers: Little is stated. As a Hydro sea area it includes underwater hazards such as strong currents and vents, and the Dagger in the Water daily commission uses Pufferfruit targets there (a gameplay challenge).

Quests: Dagger in the Water, Freminet: A Story and Sightseeing With Friends: A Trip to Fontaine are the quests that list Salacia Plain. Dagger in the Water has spots near the Opera Epiclese and near the Court of Fontaine, as well as in Liffey and Morte.

Travel: Reached by diving from the Court of Fontaine Region; the Transoceanic Sourcewater's blessing allows passage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the area is recorded.

Because the sources give almost nothing in the way of history, treat the place as scenery. Its name comes from Salacia, the Roman goddess of salt water.

240.content:
Salon Caritat: Salon Caritat is a society in the Quartier Narbonnais of the Court of Fontaine devoted to the study of law and the improvement of justice. In practice its members act like a civic advocacy group, currently pressing on government spending and water pollution.

Its headquarters notice states its purpose as furthering the study of law in Fontaine and improving the administration of justice. It organises numbered symposia to which all members are invited. The name is Occitan for "charity", per the wiki's etymology note.

People: Two open-world members are known. Riqueti worries about the Palais Mermonia's sense of crisis; he once served in the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol of the Gardes before transferring to the Maison Gestion. Justeau is preoccupied with ocean pollution and complains that hardly anyone else cares.

Riqueti describes the Patrol as the least mechanised branch of the Gardes, recruiting on ability regardless of family background, and says its captain Chevreuse would have no use for gardemeks. He holds that Fontaine should not assume life will be easy after a crisis, and that it must keep attending to its other problems.

Atmosphere: Expect earnest, slightly pompous talk: members using formal legal and administrative language about budgets and the environment, convinced that the public is ignoring an obvious danger. It is a place of speeches and petitions rather than action.

History: The notice announces the salon's 36th symposium, on the Maison Gardiennage's budget overruns and their link to public safety in the Court of Fontaine. That implies regular meetings over some time, but canon gives no dates.

The notice also frames the salon's aim as improving justice generally, so its interest in pollution and spending sits alongside, not in place of, its legal-study purpose. Riqueti's dialogue changes after the Archon Quest events around the prophecy, when he treats the prophecy as the largest crisis Fontaine has faced and urges attention to other problems (revelation tied to Version 4.2 content). Note that the wiki gives no building description beyond the headquarters marker in the Quartier Narbonnais.

Status as of 7.1: Active as of Version 7.1, with members still voicing concerns around the Court of Fontaine.

241.content: Riqueti and Justeau are the Salon Caritat members met in the open world. Riqueti is a former Patrol member turned administrator who doubts how Fontaine's institutions handle risk; Justeau is fixated on the water pollution crisis and says the ocean cannot be relied on to clean itself.

242.content:
Sea of Bygone Eras (also: Undersea Capital): The Sea of Bygone Eras is a stretch of Fontaine's waters, too deep for sunlight to reach, where the capital of ancient Remuria lies in ruins on the sea floor. It is reached through the sunken Faded Castle in the Nostoi Region and has its own map. Its ruins include the warrior city Machimos, the gated inner city Capitolium and, on the hill at its heart, the golden palace Domus Aurea, where the God King Remus once tended the "symphony" that ruled his empire.

Before it sank, this water was part of the Great Fontaine Lake. In the 4.6 world quests (Canticles of Harmony) the Traveler, the spirit of the former Harmost Cassiodor and the freed vishap prince Scylla went down into the ruins and destroyed Phobos, the Grand Symphony, which had trapped Remurian souls for millennia.

Geography: A dark sea floor of coral reefs, rock towers, caverns and broken stonework, crossed by currents. Machimos, the outer city, makes up the larger, outer part of the ruins: the tall rock formations there are probably what is left of it. The only way from Machimos into Capitolium is the Initium Iani gate, which opens onto the Passage of Ianus, an underwater corridor with a current running its whole length. Capitolium contains Clivus Capitolinus (the hill of Domus Aurea), the harp-shaped aqueduct Alta Semita and the Collegium Phonascorum.

Event-menu text describes the waters as lying south of a "Great Terrestrial Lake" and as once part of the same high sea. Monsieur Os (Cassiodor) adds that because these waters were once part of the Great Fontaine Lake, they have the same properties as Fontaine's waters. The outer ruins hold the sub-areas Initium Iani, Hortus Euergetis, Caesareum Palace and Portus Anticus, the last sunk into an underwater cavern. Domus Aurea has upper and lower levels; its throne room is the Sacellum Requietis.

Places: - **Machimos**: the outer city, once full of temples, arenas, walls decorated with glaze and gold, statues and markets; home of Remuria's warriors.
- **Capitolium**: the inner city, a "paradise for artists" of theatres and carved palaces.
- **Domus Aurea**: the royal palace on Clivus Capitolinus, built as a giant instrument for playing Phobos and considered the "heart" of the Symphony.
- **Initium Iani / Passage of Ianus**: the gate and corridor between the two cities.

- **Caesareum Palace**: a training ground of the Remurian legions, where the chains that bound Scylla were kept.
- **Portus Anticus**: the old royal port, whose bell tower once guided sailors home.
- **Alta Semita**: the aqueduct that once carried Ichor from Domus Aurea to "the great lake in the far north".
- **Collegium Phonascorum**: Remuria's school, where Harmosts and music lecturers taught the Symphony.
- **Hortus Euergetis**: an undersea garden named after the dead Harmost Euergetia.
- **Sacellum Requietis**: Remus' throne room inside Domus Aurea.

History: Remus, a god who came to Meropis, founded Remuria above the waters of present-day Fontaine and made Capitolium its centre. A prophecy said the empire would face utter destruction and its people would return to the primordial sea. To escape that fate, Remus gave his people golem bodies of stone with golden Ichor for blood and bound their souls into the Symphony, Phobos. Phobos turned the empire to war against the "barbarian" tribes and vishaps. Remus' secret final plan to destroy it failed when the Harmost Boethius sealed Scylla at the Initium Iani, and a great wave from the Symphony sank the capital and its people.

According to Scylla, his vishap army's assault on the capital was part of Remus' secret plan. Scylla was to reach Domus Aurea with the Requiem, Remus' final order for Phobos to destroy itself, and to guide the power it released. Remus would sacrifice himself to start the Requiem. Boethius falsely claimed Remus had ordered the legions to stop resisting, let the Dragonborn come in, then shut the Initium Iani and turned Scylla to stone. Without Scylla, the Requiem's power became a tsunami that drowned Remurians and invaders alike. Afterwards Boethius gathered survivors as the Golden Troupe in the Faded Castle to revive the empire. Cassiodor opposed him, broke his soul into fragments, sealed them in these waters and sealed the passage to the surface.

Over the centuries Boethius' shattered soul bound itself to the remains of Phobos. Shortly before the 4.6 quests, the Symphony grew strong enough to reach the surface, replacing the souls of Petrichor's townsfolk and visiting adventurers with Remurian souls who relived the empire's last days. In Pale Crown Palace (7.0), the Belyi Tsar wrote that Sybilla, the prophet behind Phobos, had tried to build a system independent of the ley lines and Heimarmene. He believed the Remurians had somehow escaped the heavens' gaze and passed on their arts, though in distorted form. The Temple of Space (6.5) also preserves records of Remuria among its fallen civilisations.

People: No living residents. Golem soldiers of the old legions (Praetorian Golems) still guard the ruins. Scylla, the "Fell Dragon Prince", now lives free in these waters and welcomes visits from the Traveler. The souls once held in the Symphony have passed on.

Scylla calls himself a prince among the Dragonborn. Cassiodor says he was really an unusually strong vishap, because no new Hydro Dragon could be born while Egeria slept. Scylla once fought Remus for thirty days before guiding him to Egeria's prison, and became his friend. Since he lost his body to the seal, he now lives in a body made of Ichor. After hearing that a true dragon (Neuvillette) has been born, he has thought of seeking an audience with him, but doubts he still counts as Dragonborn. Lesser creatures that feed on the Symphony's music live here: allochromatic anemones, wonderchime flowers, eels, "washer" octopuses and the golden Auric Anglerfish, which the Collegium's zealots built to bring non-human creatures under the Symphony.

Atmosphere: Silent blue darkness lit by golden ruins, glowing sea life and the faint pulse of old music. White stone and bronze lie broken among reefs; engraved orders and memorials from the empire's last war still cover the walls. Since Phobos fell, Scylla finds the deep far more peaceful, and quiet enough that he is tempted to sleep.

In-game text describes the citizens' belief that the empire would last for ever while the God King's melody played from the golden throne, and how that pride and hatred sank beneath the waves. Paimon thought the inside of Domus Aurea looked "more like the guts of some giant machine" than a palace.

Dangers: Praetorian Golems and Hunter's Rays, ancient sealed doors and defences, crushing depth and darkness, and the Local Legend Cineas, "Unreturned Envoy", a Primordial Bathysmal Vishap. The Symphony's power can still move or freeze objects. While Phobos still existed, its music could seize souls. The Traveler was immune because Phobos' melody did not sing of their destiny.

Travel: Gameplay: the area unlocks after the world quest Underwater Nocturne, through the portal in the Faded Castle. Travellers explore it by diving, using the Symphony (the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box sends a Pause Soundwave to stop objects and a Play Soundwave to start them) and, after Scylla is freed, his "Summon the current" ability to ride water currents.

Gameplay: other puzzles include Autoharmonic Reed Pipes, potential energy orbs, resonant anemones, wonderchime flowers and allochromatic anemones, swaying eels in the coral reefs, washer octopuses and the Auric Anglerfish. Restoring the Alta Semita aqueduct (Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction I-II) is needed to open Domus Aurea's gates.

Quests: Canticles of Harmony (4.6): Prelude "The Shadow Over Petrichor" (Faded Castle), First Movement "Underwater Nocturne", Second Movement "The Last Day of Remuria" (freeing Scylla and breaking through the Initium Iani), Third Movement "Gradus ad Capitolium" (restoring the golden aqueducts) and Finale "Fortune Plango Vulnera" (the battle in Domus Aurea and the Requiem).

In the finale, Boethius tried to "take on flesh" as a new Sebastos in Domus Aurea. Cassiodor let himself be absorbed so that he could seize control of Boethius' body from within, and Phobos showed itself as "that-which-was-once-Sybilla". Cassiodor asked the Traveler to destroy both of them. Golems executed the defeated Boethius, Cassiodor faded, and the Traveler played the Requiem at the harp in the throne room. The freed souls rose like a current to the High Sea, led by a spirit-guiding golden bee. Osse, the cat Cassiodor had possessed, was left an ordinary cat. Scylla brought the group back to Petrichor, then swam off to enjoy his freedom.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sunken capital is quiet: Phobos was destroyed in 4.6, the trapped Remurian souls have passed on and Scylla is free in the deep.

The Symphony mechanism still works for exploration, and golem guards remain. Cassiodor and Boethius are gone. Later versions refer back to Remuria in lore texts, such as the Temple of Space (6.5) and the Belyi Tsar's notes in Pale Crown Palace (7.0).

243.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Capitolium and Domus Aurea
243.content:
Capitolium was the inner city of Remuria's capital, open only to the finest scholars and musicians, and only a few of them served the God King directly. At its centre, on the hill Clivus Capitolinus, stands Domus Aurea, a golden palace of tall copper pillars built as a giant harp-like instrument for playing Phobos. Remus sat at its heart, listening for any wrong note anywhere in the empire and correcting it with a pluck of his strings. Scylla calls the city the "Eternal City" and says Remus' will still protects it. In 4.6 Boethius made his last stand inside the palace, and the Traveler played the Requiem in its throne room, the Sacellum Requietis.

In a cavern beneath the hill, an engraving records an order from Boethius to receive Dragonborn envoys for talks. The rest has been hacked out and replaced by the word "Traitor" scratched over and over, with a final curse inviting the enemy to sink into the "immortal prison" with the city. The wiki says the palace was fashioned from Remus' ship, the Fortuna.

244.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Machimos and the Initium Iani
244.content:
Machimos was the outer city of Remuria's capital, home of its warriors, with arenas, temples, gold-and-glaze walls and busy markets. The Initium Iani was the only gate into Capitolium, opening onto the Passage of Ianus. Boethius and the Harmost Euergetia sealed Scylla there by shutting the gate on him as he tried to break through. In 4.6 the freed Scylla broke the gate's stone seals and carried the Traveler through the trench beyond.

An engraving at the gate notes that a humble slave named Decimus now lies at the bottom of the sea just as the exalted Harmosts do.

245.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Caesareum Palace
245.content:
A training ground of the Remurian legions where the chains that held Scylla were kept. Boethius ordered Legio VI Rithimi Versi of the Legion Athanatoi to hold back the Dragonborn here; its records say no soldier deserted and no enemy got through. A nameless stone statue still offers a challenge to visitors.

The engravings contradict each other. One order tells the legion to receive the Dragonborn peacefully, and the lines after it are deliberately struck out. Another order from Boethius seals Portus Anticus and the Initium Iani behind seven layers of defence, and records that three chains forged from Euergetia's blood and bone were moved here to imprison the drake chieftain for ever. A memorial by two siblings, Aetius and Placidia, says they died fighting the "traitorous" Dragonborn at the gates, choosing "civilization and death" in the name of their benefactress.

246.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Portus Anticus
246.content:
Remuria's royal port, now sunk into an underwater cavern. Ships came in past the Ocean Pillars along the royal fairway. Its tall bell tower was said to stand at the border of reality and dreams: its bell could "pierce the barrier of ocean" and lead sailors lured to sleep by sirens back home through the mist. The imperial ship Fortuna was berthed here.

Engravings record orders from Legio V's envoy Faunus withdrawing the northern harbour defences. A later order from Boethius tells Legio V to stop fighting the Dragonborn and return to Caesareum Palace, then has Legio VII and Legio IX seal the port behind them. One bitter verse condemns Faunus for razing the city of Lugdunensis.

247.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Alta Semita
247.content:
A huge aqueduct shaped like a harp that once carried Ichor from Domus Aurea to "the great lake in the far north". Scylla remembers swimming in those waters. It broke apart after the fall. In 4.6 the Traveler restored it with fragments of the Symphony so that Domus Aurea's gates could be opened.

An engraving there mourns the Harmost Aurelius, who had pacified many tribes for the empire and once promoted Boethius. He sank with his great flagship of forty rows of oars, which "traitors" working with the barbarians scuttled as it carried him north. No one knows where he is buried.

248.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Collegium Phonascorum
248.content:
Remuria's centre of learning, where Harmosts and music teachers taught citizens the theory of the Symphony. Scylla calls its scholars "mad believers" who tried to bring non-human creatures under the Golden Symphony, creating the Auric Anglerfish.

A Harmost's notes found here set out Aurelius' four categories of all things (Substance, Property, Quality, Relation) and describe Phobos as a symphony that blends mortal melodies so that it can "vie with Fortuna". The notes go on to argue that people outside the Symphony merely play out a fate written for them, so they are not equal humans and must be wiped out. This is the ideology behind Remuria's wars of conquest.

249.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Hortus Euergetis
249.content: An undersea garden named after the dead Harmost Euergetia, called "the benefactress". An engraving signed "Ouranides of Ouranopolis" (Cassiodor's alias) mourns her as colleague, friend and sister, and promises that flowers will always bloom there for her even if her name is forgotten.

250.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Scylla in the Sea of Bygone Eras
250.content: Scylla is a giant vishap prince who led Dragonborn vishaps and "barbarians" against Remuria. Boethius trapped him in stone at the Initium Iani, and he stayed chained for millennia. Thoughts escaping from his stony prison took the form of a large glowing fish that swam past the Faded Castle's windows. The Traveler, Paimon and Cassiodor broke his three chains in 4.6, and he helped them reach Domus Aurea and complete Remus' Requiem. Proud, booming and friendly, he calls the Traveler and Paimon "little ones" and despises Boethius. He now roams these waters freely and asks the Traveler to visit him.

251.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: The Symphony and Phobos
251.content: The "Symphony" is human memory and persona woven into music, a melody in which souls can live and have their wishes granted. Sybilla, the Great Golden Bee and a prophet who survived an earlier cycle, taught the secret to Remus. He poured these melodies into Ichor, which the primordial sea could not dissolve, so that people could rule their own fates. Overwhelmed, the people asked to be guided, so Remus wrote every melody into one great Symphony: Phobos. Phobos turned out to have Sybilla's selfless urge to make "everyone" happy, so it tried to grant even its Remurians' wishes to conquer. The Symphony's remaining power still moves the ruins (the Symphony mechanic) and feeds the area's strange creatures.

252.comment: Sea of Bygone Eras: Golden Castellum and the Golden Troupe
252.content: The Faded Castle, once the "golden castellum", is the gateway to the Sea of Bygone Eras. Harmosts and scholars kept an archive there of scripts, scores and stories of things that had and had not happened, hoping to master fate. After the fall, Boethius' surviving followers, the Golden Troupe, gathered there to bring back the empire. Cassiodor sealed the way to the surface to protect Fontaine, and the seal held until he opened it for the Traveler in 4.6.

253.content:
Secret Vault (also: Marechaussee Hunter vault): In the story quest Buried Honor, the group of Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney and the Traveler plays a tabletop adventure whose "treasure" turns out to be real Hunter heritage. The vault's door needs four keys, passed down through generations of Hunters, to form the complete key. What lies inside is no gold: a tablet and worn weapons, which the characters understand to be the Hunters' true legacy. It first appeared in Version 4.7.

The same cave is tied to a seal on a Devorator kept by a Hunter family, a duty its latest heir neglected.

Geography: Entrance east of the Central Laboratory Ruins, hidden by a rock that can be blown open; beyond lies a water-filled cave and then a quiet narrow passage ending at a stone door with a pattern mechanism.

Puzzles in the approach use water-volume detection crystals, and each puzzle yields a key part. A treasure map found in the story marks the way.

History: In the quest, the door is described as sealed for more than a hundred years. Clorinde recognises the keys as Marechaussee Hunter keys passed from generation to generation; four are needed to form the complete key, and she holds her own, inherited from her Master. Florian, a descendant of Hunters, had acquired three keys by theft and force and wanted the fourth.

Florian explains that his family served as Marechaussee Hunters for generations and also passed down a seal, ancient in origin, which they were told to tend. After his father died he neglected it, and when he checked it his memory went hazy. Clorinde suspects the influence of a Devorator, a monster active several centuries ago that amplifies obsessions and desires; some Hunters sealed such creatures hoping for a permanent solution later. Florian recovers after the monster leaves him.

People: Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney and the Traveler open it; Florian, a Hunter descendant, intended to seize it.

Dangers: In the quest, explosives had been planted in the cave; Clorinde dismantled them. The path also includes a fight with a possessed Florian.

Atmosphere: Hushed and ancient; the writing describes it as so quiet that the secret there seems to breathe.

Quests: Buried Honor, part 3 of the Silent Night act in Clorinde's story chapter (Rapperia Chapter).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it stays accessible as an exploration point holding the Hunters' tablet and weapons.

254.content: Four keys, each entrusted to a respected Marechaussee Hunter and passed down, combine into the complete key that opens the Secret Vault door. Florian stole three; Clorinde held the fourth.

key: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars
255.content:
Shadow of Another World (also: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars): Shadow of Another World is a Trounce Domain in Salacia Plain, Fontaine, unlocked after completing the Archon Quest "Finale". It lets the Traveler relive the battle against the All-Devouring Narwhal, the beast from another world. Its flavor text says that battle was the intersection of this world's fate, that Fontaine now treads a brighter path, and that the giant's whale-song will not fade from memory.

The fight is titled "Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars". It rewards weekly-boss materials: Lightless Silk String, Lightless Eye of the Maelstrom and Lightless Mass.

Places: The domain is a recreated arena rather than a place with its own geography. The recollection is reached from Salacia Plain.

Players may enter the narwhal's belly mid-fight, where a dark shadow must be defeated.

Dangers: The All-Devouring Narwhal and the dark shadow within its belly. Hostility builds as the player strikes the beast or destroys the Eye of the Maelstrom, until the narwhal devours a character; defeating the shadow inside weakens it.

Pneuma or Ousia attacks can quickly destroy the whirlpool and interrupt the shadow. When the narwhal's health is low it stops devouring characters. These are game mechanics.

The domain requires Adventure Rank 35 or higher at its first tier (35, 40, 45, 50 across tiers) with recommended levels 60 to 90. Besides weekly-boss drops the reward table gives a Midlander billet and Varunada Lazurite.

Atmosphere: Remembered rather than real: echoing whale-song, a looming starlit giant, and the relief that Fontaine's fate turned out brighter.

Quests: Unlocks after the Archon Quest "Finale" in Chapter IV, whose final battle it recalls.

Status as of 7.1: A permanent boss domain as of 7.1, added in 4.2; no new story events occur in it.

256.content:
Thalatta Submarine Canyon (also: Thalatta Canyon): The Thalatta Submarine Canyon is an underwater subarea of the Court of Fontaine Region, within the map level of the Source of All Waters, the Great Fontaine Lake. Its name uses "Thalatta", the Attic Greek form of the word for sea. It debuted in Version 4.0.

Canon records only exploration content here: a group of Hunter's Rays with an impostor among them, and one of the seven Mysterious Cores.

Geography: The canyon lies below the surface of the lake, so a scene there is a submerged one, with Hunter's Rays swimming between Teleport Waypoints. The wiki gives no description of its walls, depth, size or named landmarks.

The English name comes from an ancient Greek word, and localisations render it as a submarine canyon or sea valley. No in-world explanation of the name is given.

Dangers: An Underwater Survey Mek hides among a group of Hunter's Rays. Defeating it unlocks the hidden achievement "Like Tears in the Rain", whose name references the film Blade Runner.

Quests: No quest is recorded in the canyon. One Mysterious Core, a quest item from chests after completing seven Pneumousia puzzles, is placed here as the seventh. The cores are handed to Henri to begin "Still Mouthwatering!", a quest set elsewhere.

The Mysterious Core quest item is described in game as a gear-shaped core taken from a mysterious machine. The other six cores lie in the Beryl, Belleau and Salacia areas, so this canyon is the seventh stop of a trail across the Court of Fontaine Region and surroundings, not a place with its own story. The Hunter's Ray achievement was added in 4.0 and is hidden until completed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is accessible and has no known story events.

257.content:
The Duke's Office (also: Duke's Office, Wriothesley's office): The Duke's Office is Wriothesley's office, in the centre of the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide. Its door is often shut tight, yet its owner knows everything that happens in the Fortress. It has three floors.

The top floor holds Wriothesley's desk and a sofa with a tea table; in Chapter IV of the Archon Quest it is where the Traveler comes to ask him for answers about the Fortress. A basement opens later and holds a lift to the Forbidden Zone.

It stands directly across from the Administrative Area's teleport waypoint, so it is the first landmark most visitors see. In the Archon Quest Sigewinne stops by there to check on Clorinde.

The Fortress was originally a self-governing community of exiles; Wriothesley took over as Administrator after challenging his predecessor, and this office is the seat of that authority.

Geography: The office has three floors. The top floor is the working office, with a desk and a sofa with a tea table. The basement floor becomes available during Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones and contains a lift down to the Forbidden Zone and a door to a room overlooking a ship, the Wingalet. After Masquerade of the Guilty the door stays open but the ship is gone.

The Fortress's map description calls it central: from there the Duke can know what goes on in the prison even when the door is closed.

People: Wriothesley, the Duke, works here. Sigewinne, the Fortress's medical officer, comes by in the quest to check on Clorinde, and Freminet's recovery is mentioned. The quest also features Jurieu and Lourvine.

Wriothesley meets the Traveler's questions with a playful correction of the word "explain" to "enlighten", then leads them down into the Forbidden Zone.

Governance: The Administrator of the Fortress of Meropide is known as the Duke. The Fortress is autonomous, and Wriothesley's reforms since taking over its administration are described on his own entry; this office is where he receives visitors and makes decisions.

Quests: In Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones (Chapter IV, Act IV, Part 3 of the Archon Quest) the Traveler comes to the office to question Wriothesley directly, then follows him through the newly opened basement lift into the Forbidden Zone. Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2) later changes the basement room.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the office is unchanged in the sources read.

258.comment: The Duke's Office: The Duke's Office
258.content: The Duke's Office is Wriothesley's three-floor office in the centre of the Fortress of Meropide's Administrative Area. Its door is often shut, but he knows all that happens in the Fortress. The top floor has his desk and a tea table; the basement, opened in Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones, has a lift to the Forbidden Zone and a door to a room overlooking a ship.

259.content:
The Narzissenkreuz Ordo (also: Narzissenkreuz Ordo chamber): The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, as a place, is the hidden meeting chamber of the secret society of the same name. It sits at the top of the Tower of Ipsissimus in Fontaine. In its ceiling is a Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz to count down to the apocalypse of the Prophecy of Fontaine.

The chamber is now empty of ceremonial items and has not seen a Dispelling Ritual for a long time, but Caterpillar recognises it as the place where the sinners of Fontaine once gathered. Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour use it as a base while looking into the Ordo's past. The map text calls it a place where great dreams were once born and countless souls melted.

The society behind the room was founded over 400 years ago by Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, former members of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, who sought to merge the wills of many people into a Descender to survive the prophesied destruction. It was later declared an illegal extremist group and the tower sealed.

The wiki notes that the clock and the large round window resemble the Nod-Krai emblem, which also represents the Three Moons; this is an observation, not a stated link.

Geography: The chamber is an instance entered by choosing "Read" on a book at the end of the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Central Quartier; the first entry unlocks it as a waypoint on the map. A second book on a music stand inside lets the player leave. Its ceiling holds the Doomsday Clock, and a large circular window lights the room.

During the world quest Search in the Algae Sea, a vent on the south-west of the Tower of Ipsissimus roof opens as another route in, and a large crack in the floor becomes a second exit.

People: The Ordo's former members and leaders are described in their own entries. In the room today are Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour, who investigate the Ordo here. Caterpillar says he belonged to the Ordo but not to its inner circle, and that he was personally mentored by Narzissenkreuz.

Members had clearance levels from one to four; honorary levels were given for significant contributions. Rene founded the Ordo with Jakob, who performed tricks to attract recruits from the Institute.

Culture: Two notes found in the chamber after Search in the Algae Sea show the Ordo's outlook: one explains a ritual line about sinking into the great sea to be reborn, tied to a play about Ajax and an ancient Sumeru text phrase read as "primordial human"; the other argues that to excise the self is to die before death, so one can avoid receiving a Vision, which it treats as selling oneself to the fate of the world.

The notes reflect a goal of becoming a will able to protect, sustain, destroy and create a world, distinct from a Descender.

History: The society formed after its founders learned of the coming destruction of the world, and held that merging many wills into one being was the way to survive it. Their later work, including research on the Primordial Sea, leads on to the events investigated in Search in the Algae Sea. See the faction entry for details.

Quests: Riddles Awaiting Answers begins automatically when the Traveler first enters the chamber after Unfinished Comedy. Search in the Algae Sea, the only world quest of In the Wake of Narcissus Act I, is started here by talking to Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour two in-game days after Initial Facts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chamber is unchanged in the sources read, serving as the investigators' base.

260.comment: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo (chamber)
260.content: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, as a location, is the hidden meeting chamber of the secret society at the top of the Tower of Ipsissimus. Its ceiling holds a Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz to count down the apocalypse. It is entered via a book at the end of the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Central Quartier.

261.content:
"The Real Annapausis" (also: The Real Annapausis): "The Real Annapausis" is the hidden heart of Annapausis, reached after Ann's storybook quest to rescue Princess Lyris. It is where the consciousness of Mary-Ann, a hybrid Oceanid, resides. First entered in the world quest "Mary-Ann's Story" (4.0), it then closed until "Rowboat's Wake" (4.2) made it permanently accessible.

The place looks like a gentle garden and school hall where Mary-Ann keeps tea, flowers and a "dog" waiting for visitors. It is, in her own words, a tomb rather than a home.

Geography: Part of the Annapausis subarea in the Court of Fontaine Region. It is reached by escaping the "Convoluted Corridor" of the adventure and has its own map entry. Inside are a flower garden, a tea hall that rings a bell for teatime, and a doghouse; at the end of the first visit the room floods.

The wiki notes the name Annapausis plays on the Ancient Greek word anapausis, "rest". In Chinese and Japanese the name suggests a resting or sleeping place, also a pun on Ann's name. This is the wiki's reading, not in-game commentary.

People: Mary-Ann lives here. She appears as a young woman with fair skin, bright blue eyes, mid-length blue hair and a blue-and-white frilled dress. She is a hybrid Oceanid formed when Lyris absorbed the dying Mary-Ann Guillotin's consciousness, and the wiki says she unintentionally created the Oceanid Ann out of parts of her memories and dreams. Ann, Paimon and the Traveler meet her here.

In the first meeting she speaks of being long in Fontaine, of "a friend" (Rene) who had been to Sumeru and of Basil, a capable caretaker of children and flowers. Her "dog" speaks with polite court manners and is not Mori; Ann notices this.

History: Per the wiki, during a conflict in the remains of Elynas 400-500 years ago between the Marechaussee Hunters and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, Mary-Ann Guillotin was gravely wounded by an explosion. Lyris dissolved her and absorbed her consciousness, creating Mary-Ann. Mary-Ann presumed her old companions dead and built a dream in Annapausis, hiding inside a fairy tale the human had once told Lyris and waiting for the Institute's people to return.

In "Mary-Ann's Story" the Traveler deduces that the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom is only a story, and Mary-Ann sends the party away, saying the story is ended and Annapausis is "our tomb". In "Rowboat's Wake" the Narzissenkreuz now defeated, the Traveler and Ann return; the Traveler smashes the "Will to Resist" with the Holy Blade, breaking the illusion. Mary-Ann forgives Rene (now Narzissenkreuz), accepts the past and decides to live as herself.

Quests: "Mary-Ann's Story" (Ann of the Narzissenkreuz Act III, 4.0) and "Rowboat's Wake" (In the Wake of Narcissus, 4.2). After the latter, returning to the Real Annapausis and approaching the house grants an achievement.

In "Mary-Ann's Story" the first visit includes a bell for teatime, tasteless snacks, sunflowers that bloom when watered, and dandelion seeds from Paimon. Mary-Ann tells a parable of water droplets that unite, to ask whether uniting costs identity.

Atmosphere: Warm, pretty and tinged with unreality: tea set out for guests who are not coming, flowers waiting to bloom, food that tastes like water, and a temperature that drops sharply when the dream breaks.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the place is open and empty of its resident. Mary-Ann set out after "Rowboat's Wake" with Ann, Seymour and Mamere to see the world beyond the glass wall, saying the garden is somewhere they can come back to if afraid.

262.comment: "The Real Annapausis": Mary-Ann Guillotin and Annapausis
262.content: The human Mary-Ann Guillotin was the sister of Alain Guillotin; the Oceanid Mary-Ann is a different, hybrid being that has her memories fused with Lyris'. The Real Annapausis is her constructed refuge. Ann, a young Oceanid born from the dream, believes her purpose is to rescue Princess Lyris, a quest Mary-Ann gently frees her from.

263.content:
The Wingalet (also: Wingalet, Wingalet Gloop-Gloop Funderwater Fisharium): The Wingalet is a very large ship that Wriothesley, administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, built in secret in the Forbidden Zone beneath the prison. He began it once he suspected the Primordial Sea lay just beyond the Fortress's sluice gate, meaning it as an escape vessel and something for Fontainians to hold on to. It surfaced during the Prophecy of Fontaine to rescue people from the flood, then went back into storage. In Version 6.7 it was leased out during the Fontinalia Film Festival and fitted with an aquarium.

Wriothesley modelled the project on the legendary Fortuna, the ship of Remuria's first king, though he did not expect it to match that legend.

Geography: Built in a factory-scale production zone of the Fortress of Meropide, below the Duke's Office and near the isolation gates of the Forbidden Zone. Wriothesley shows it to the Traveler and Paimon as a gargantuan silhouette seen through glass in the distance. When it rises, its sides open and cranes extend with hooks to haul people from the water.

The 6.7 version has spacious cabins, a long deck with a high balcony at the stern, and captain's quarters. A deck area is a marked point of interest on the map near the Court of Fontaine, and a waypoint on the ship unlocks with the story quest, even before the player can dive.

History: Some years before the Traveler reached the Fortress, Wriothesley began to suspect that the Primordial Sea lay under the sluice gate he had found. He launched the project in secret so that Fontainians would have a way to reach safety and something to cling to, drawing on a whole factory's labour, materials and technology, with technical advice from Jurieu and Lourvine of the Fontaine Research Institute. The Traveler learns of it in "Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones" (Cataclysm's Quickening). Wriothesley warns that if the Fortress's workers learned the truth behind the ship, riots could destroy the Fortress faster than the catastrophe. When the Prophecy of Fontaine came to pass and the nation flooded, he commanded the Wingalet, which rose from the water to rescue the stranded. After the Prophecy was averted, it returned to the Fortress's factory and sat idle.

Wriothesley's character story "The Wingalet" frames the project as a response to unsettling signs, a historian-inmate theory that the sea that swallowed Remuria could return, and his wish to prepare even if the effort proved futile; it calls the Wingalet a ship built to flee disaster and says an unbridgeable gulf lay between it and the golden Fortuna. The story ends by repeating the quoted line that oceans rise, empires fall and change alone endures.

The 6.7 story quest "Sunny Summer Fontinalia" is a limited-time event story. Wriothesley, unable to afford the ship's heavy maintenance, rented it out during the festival to raise Mora and to give the inmates who keep it running a visible reward. See the entries below.

People: Wriothesley commands and controls it. Jurieu and Lourvine, former Fontaine Research Institute researchers working for him as technical consultants, advised on the design. Inmates of the Fortress clean and maintain it. In 6.7 Sandrone leases it under the surname Guillotin and is called its current captain.

Citlali is shown at the aquarium's front desk in the 6.7 story, the person Sandrone hired. Furina, Columbina and the Traveler's other companions pass through during the film shoots.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Wingalet belongs to the Fortress of Meropide and, since 6.7, doubles as an aquarium that Wriothesley agreed to keep running in part.

At the end of "Those We Have Kept" Wriothesley asks Sandrone, the current captain, whether some installations may stay so Fortress inmates can enjoy the aquarium, and she agrees. No later use of the ship is shown in canon through 7.1.

264.content:
The Wingalet was built beneath the Fortress of Meropide as insurance against the Primordial Sea breaking through the sluice gate of the Forbidden Zone. Wriothesley hid it from the Fortress's own population so that panic would not spread. He admits it is no match for the legendary Fortuna, the ship on which King Remus founded Remuria with the seer Sybilla, but it gave Fontaine something to hold on to. During the Prophecy of Fontaine it was used for rescue work under his command.

Jurieu, once assistant to Edwin Eastinghouse and versed in Arkhium and gravimeters, and Lourvine, his former assistant, helped design it. The same quest where the Traveler is shown the ship also reveals the Fortress's history and the rising Primordial Seawater around it.

265.comment: The Wingalet: Sunny Summer Fontinalia and the Wingalet Fisharium
265.content:
During the limited Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (Version 6.7), Wriothesley rents the Wingalet out for the Fontinalia Film Festival to cover its upkeep and boost morale among the inmates who maintain it. The renter is a deep-pocketed woman with a fishing permit and business licence who sets up an aquarium; she turns out to be Sandrone, who uses the cover in the hope of finding the underwater home she shared with Alain Guillotin. Xavier and Lepine-Pauline's two film crews share the ship as a location. In the event the player runs the aquarium by collecting creatures and curios, and event rewards include a banner and a rules sign from the Fisharium.

Sandrone applied for the fishing permit under the name Guillotin, then keeps the aquarium open only to look legitimate if the Gestionnaires check. At the end of the story Wriothesley, thankful for the ship's good condition, asks that some installations stay so the Fortress's inmates can enjoy the aquarium.

266.content:
Tower of Ipsissimus (also: Tower of Gestalt, Sealed Ruined Tower): The Tower of Ipsissimus, also called the Tower of Gestalt or the Sealed Ruined Tower, stands in Fontaine's Morte Region. The secret society known as the Narzissenkreuz Ordo built it as its base. The Court later declared the Ordo an illegal extremist group and sealed the site. The tower is the way down to a seal over the Primordial Sea, and it sinks beneath the water for good after the 4.2 world quest Savior's Wake.

Its name comes from an old Remurian idea of a will powerful enough to rule, sustain and destroy the world. Its other names, such as Gestalt, point to the Ordo's goal of merging many wills into one.

Geography: A tall tower with a clock face high on it, rising from the Morte Region. Inside it has a top, a middle and a bottom level, each with its own puzzle, and below the bottom level lies the sealed way to the Primordial Sea. A hidden meeting chamber, also called the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, sits at the top and has a Doomsday Clock set into its ceiling.

The chamber can also be entered through a book at the end of the Central Quartier in the Institute of Natural Philosophy. A vent on the tower roof, a crack in the floor and a book on a music stand serve as other ways in and out. Teleport waypoints called 'Exploring the Tower of Gestalt' follow the Traveler down through the levels during the quests.

Places: Each level carries exhibit-style panels and certificates for Ordo members, plus optical couplers (an Ordo design) used for puzzles. Notes describe the tower as a model of the evolution of the human soul. The bottom level holds a storybook with comments in purple ink, and a long investigation log about studying ruined temples and ancient Remurian script.

Certificates honour members by level. Madam M. Laveaux, Level 4, is said to have returned from Natlan. Ms. E. Lenormand, a book merchant, was promoted to Level 3. Erich, a historian formerly of the Institute of Natural Philosophy, is at Level 2. Griffin L. Randolph and Susannah hold honorary Level 1 rank. Ms. Giuffria, a dancer, reached Level 3. The panels credit a sponsor, Mr. Eliphas, for the optical-coupling design.

The investigation log says the Ordo's scholars had trouble reading antediluvian bronze slates and stone tablets in Remurian script until they were reminded by Erich about a copy at the Institute of Natural Philosophy. They sorted a spirit into memory, wishes, soul and persona, with 'True Will' as the state nearest to divine freedom.

People: The Ordo was founded over 400 years ago by Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, former members of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, and led by Narzissenkreuz. Jakob personally confronts the Traveler at the top of the tower. Ann, Caterpillar and Seymour come to the tower with the Traveler.

Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin, also from the Institute, refused Rene's methods and never joined the Ordo.

Governance: Members were grouped in clearance levels from one to four, with honorary levels for supporters who could not pass the tests. A notice on a wall panel high in the tower, carrying the seal of the courts and the signatures of Alain Guillotin and Neuvillette, declares the Ordo an illegal extremist group and criminal organisation under Fontainian law and the Mermonia Act, and orders the site sealed permanently. Destroying the notice board would count as a challenge to national authority.

Culture: The Ordo believed people refine themselves through cycles of samsara: Hyperborea, Natlantea, Remuria and the first half of the fourth cycle, Khraun-Arya. The tower's introduction text insists this is a spiritual idea and no challenge to the Akademiya's research. The Ordo's goal was the loss of paradise, the defeat of evil dragons, original sin and baptism, and finally freedom from the gods.

History: The Ordo, formed after the All-Devouring Narwhal devoured the Primordial Sea, held that the world's destruction was coming and that the only escape was to merge people's wills into one transcendent being. It used the Tower of Ipsissimus as its base while it studied the Primordial Sea beneath. In Search in the Algae Sea (4.2) the Traveler is taken to the top of the tower, where Jakob demands a component of the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. After a fight the blade is forged, and the Doomsday Clock strikes twelve and crushes Jakob.

Rene de Petrichor later removed his own personality and was 'reborn' as the Master, merged with the Director of the old Narzissenkreuz Institute, as part of a plan for an Oceanid that would gather the minds of all Fontainians. In Savior's Wake the Traveler goes down the three levels, breaks the seal above the Primordial Sea and fights reactivated clockwork meka. In Waking from the Great Dream the Traveler defeats Narzissenkreuz.

Dangers: Clockwork meka of 'Special Order 172' wake at the lowest level when the seal is broken. The Primordial Sea beneath is dangerous.

Atmosphere: Eerie, ceremonial and unfinished. Panels read like a trade-fair exhibit, with polite thanks to sponsors whose names have been struck out, and a countdown clock hangs over everything.

Travel: The tower is on the ground close to a teleport waypoint. After Savior's Wake it is permanently underwater, so the structure cannot be walked through again.

Quests: The world quest series In the Wake of Narcissus (4.2) covers Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream and Rowboat's Wake. Savior's Wake is the quest that takes place in the tower itself.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed by the courts and, since 4.2, permanently submerged.

267.comment: Tower of Ipsissimus: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo Chamber
267.content: A hidden meeting chamber at the top of the tower. A Doomsday Clock made by the mage Narzissenkreuz is built into its ceiling to count down to the apocalypse. Its map description reads that great dreams were once born here and countless souls melted. Notes left inside speak of forsaking the self and being reborn as a holy infant, and warn that receiving a Vision means selling oneself to the fate of the world.

268.content:
Vasari Passage (also: Court of Fontaine: Vasari Passage): Vasari Passage sits at the bottom (south) of the Court of Fontaine. Streets lined with shops lead toward a large fountain plaza, and a cafe and several vendors serve passers-by.

It is one of the capital's shopping districts and a common meeting spot because of the statue plaza.

Places: Statue Plaza, the large fountain square where the shop streets converge; the Eastern Street and the Western Street; and Cafe Lucerne, managed by Arouet. Vendors include Boucicaut (Damoville Purveyor), Estelle (Beaumont Workshop), Eugenie (fresh produce) and Louis (snack shop).

The plaza is a gathering point for people such as Nour (a member of the Gardes), Paban (a newsy), Talvat (a freelance photographer), Lovi and Potier by day and Ismenor at night. The Eastern Street holds staff of the Confrerie of Cabriere (Calcagni), and Charlene of the Gardes is on the Western Street.

People: Listed residents include Sanin, Nolette, Wei Xiaobao, Estella, Manet and Olivier, and Chatelet, Gontharet and Menthe at Cafe Lucerne.

After the world quest A Certain Stamp, the Maison Gestion gestionnaires Roialte (plaza) and Iaune (Western Street) can be found in the district at night.

Atmosphere: Shop windows, a plaza fountain and the steady foot traffic of a capital's commercial heart.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the district is recorded.

The name is unexplained in-world; the wiki only suggests a reference to the Vasari Corridor in Florence.

269.content:
Weeping Willow of the Lake (also: Erinnyes's Watery Weeping Willow, Saule pleureur du lac): The Weeping Willow of the Lake is a large willow growing at the centre of a lake in Erinnyes Forest, its roots apparently reaching under the water. Fontaine's lore treats it as a barometer: it flourishes or withers as the water veins run sweet or bitter.

In ancient times it was an object of reverence. The viewpoint text laments that omens arrive only in the same month as calamity.

Geography: A lakeside subarea in Erinnyes Forest. Before the Roots of Erinnyes are cleansed in "The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes", the whole lake area looks a sickly yellow and the willow is tainted; afterwards it is a vibrant blue. The map reflects the change.

All water veins converge on Erinnyes, and the tree's condition is tied to the veins' health. Its viewpoint is unlocked after completing "Within the Depths of Erinnyes", and its Archive entry stays hidden until collected.

Culture: The viewpoint calls it revered in ancient times, tying the willow's flourishing or withering to the water being sweet or bitter and treating it as an omen, though one that comes too late.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the lake and willow are healthy after the cleansing of the Roots of Erinnyes in 4.2.

Naming: The Chinese name means roughly "weeping willow in the lake", the French is "Saule pleureur du lac", and the viewpoint title is "Erinnyes's Watery Weeping Willow". The lake's colour on the map changes with the cleansing quest, from yellow to blue.

270.content:
West Slopes of Mont Automnequi (also: Mont Automnequi West): The West Slopes of Mont Automnequi are the western side of one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, in the Belleau Region; the east side lies in the Morte Region. The slopes are known for the Poisson Tunnel, which carries the Clementine Line through the mountain, and for the clockwork inventor Antoine. Added in Version 4.0.

Official exploration text calls Mont Automnequi one of Fontaine's most iconic peaks, noting that although much of the nation is covered by water, mountains and forests exist too.

Geography: Mountain slopes in the Belleau Region. The Poisson Tunnel passes through them. Local specialties include Lumidouce Bells and Rainbow Roses, and the wiki lists a viewpoint and a fishing point here.

The name probably derives from French for autumn and equinox (a wiki inference). The official site's exploration description says huge engineering devices from the Fontaine Research Institute dug the tunnel, solving one of the biggest problems in building the aquabus lines.

Places: Poisson Tunnel: carved through the slopes for the Clementine Line. The Fontaine Research Institute built it with enormous machines, including a bore called the "Golden Vessel". The project's success spurred a new generation of clockwork technology, including the Construction Specialist Mek, which was based on the Golden Vessel.

People: Antoine Roger is an open-world NPC engineer here. He is the creator of the Miraculous Antoine Roger Aircraft found around Fontaine, and one stands near him. He believes humans should break free of the earth and soar, and he contrasts his clockwork flight work with Edwin Eastinghouse's research.

The wiki lists no other named residents, and the explanation Antoine gives of how his propulsion works is not summarised here.

Dangers: Enemies include Hilichurls and Hydro Hilichurl Rogues, Treasure Hoarders, large Hydro Slimes, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasms and several types of Mek. The boss is the Emperor of Fire and Iron.

Quests: Quests listed for this subarea include "A Lady's Invitation", "Days Beneath the Waves", "Sea Breeze Rendezvous", "Still Mouthwatering!", "Truly Mouthwatering!", "The Art of the Elegant Blade Dance?", "Blade Dance's Unexpected End!" and "Studies in Light and Shadow: A Fontaine of Enchantment". Their stories are not covered here.

The wiki's trivia ties the name to the two seasons' words only as a guess. Antoine's idle line, "break free", sums up his creed that humanity need not be land-bound. The Poisson Tunnel entry states that the tunnel-boring effort pushed the Fontaine Research Institute to produce the Construction Specialist Mek, so the slopes are linked to the nation's mechanical development as much as to its scenery.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the slopes are accessible and unchanged.
